courses.description: An experiential approach to appreciating art and music in central European countries from the period of the Enlightenment to today.

courses.subject: ASST
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the themes and intellectual approaches that comprise the broad field of Asian Studies. It is an interdisciplinary course that aims to introduce students primarily to the study of the peoples and cultures of East and South Asia.

courses.subject: ASST
courses.description: This course explores the representations of culture, politics, society, and identity in a variety of films and other visual culture media (such as television, social media, literature, and music) from Asia. During the semester students will engage a breadth of media representations pertaining to Asia to study the development of different Asian civilizations in a historical and transnational context on some of the key issues facing these countries today.

courses.subject: ASST
courses.description: This course explores special themes in Asian Studies, including, but not limited to, literary, cinematic, social, political, economic, cultural, and international relations topics. Students analyze the course's theme on Asia in transnational contexts through class readings, presentations, discussions, and class assignments. Students will conduct research and write a final paper and/or create a final project on an approved Asian Studies topic, following the guidelines established by the instructor. This class is taught by regular or visiting faculty. Topics change each term. May be repeated for credit as topic changes.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 10154 or PHYS 10324 or concurrent enrollment, and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Basic pilot ground school for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Private Pilot Certificate. Course provides students with aeronautical knowledge and skills required for certification as a private pilot. Course content emphasizes basic instruction in the areas of aerodynamics, aircraft performance, aircraft systems, radio procedures, navigation, aviation weather, flight safety, and FAA regulations. Preparation for the FAA private pilot knowledge exam.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 10154 or PHYS 10324 or concurrent enrollment, and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Basic pilot ground school for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Private Pilot Certificate.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Flight training for beginning pilots. Course prepares students for the completion of the FAA private pilot certification process, including dual and solo flight in the areas of maneuvers and cross-country navigation. Flight training conducted under the 14 CFR Part 141 certification process.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 10003. This course builds upon the content in AVIA 10003 Theory of Primary Flight I to prepare for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Private Pilot Certificate. Course provides students with aeronautical knowledge and skills required for certification as a private pilot. Course content emphasizes instruction in the areas of aircraft construction and flight controls, aircraft systems, instruments, human factors, airport operations and airspace, weather fundamentals, navigation, cross country operations, and FAA regulations. Preparation for the FAA check ride exam.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 10003.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: AVIA 11112 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Second flight training for beginning pilots. Course provides dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction in preparation for earning the private pilot certification. Flight training conducted under the 14 CFR Part 141 certification process. Private pilot certification must be completed during this flight training course.
courses.prereqText: AVIA 11112 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 12223. Course provides students with a detailed study of navigation systems and instruments, forecasting weather trends, FAA regulations, and terminal and enroute procedures necessary for operating Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) in the national airspace system. Preparation for the FAA Instrument Rating exam.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 12223.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: AVIA 11112 and AVIA 12223 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Flight training course designed to prepare students for completion of the FAA Instrument Pilot Rating with mastery of all instrument procedures. Course provides dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction conducted under FAR Part 141.
courses.prereqText: AVIA 11112 and AVIA 12223 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Flight training course designed to prepare students for completion of the FAA Instrument Pilot Rating with mastery of all instrument procedures.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: AVIA 21113 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Flight training course designed to prepare students for completion of the FAA Instrument Pilot Rating Course emphasizes IFR cross-country operations. dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction conducted under FAR Part 141.
courses.prereqText: AVIA 21113 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Flight training course designed to prepare students for completion of the FAA Instrument Pilot Rating Course emphasizes IFR cross-country operations. dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction conducted under FAR Part 141.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Course is designed to prepare the student for the FAA commercial pilot practical exam. Course content includes aircraft performance, advanced aircraft systems, airspace navigation, aircraft weight and balance, multiengine aerodynamics, and FAA regulations relating to commercial pilot maneuvers.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: AVIA 21122 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program. Flight training course designed to develop a higher degree of coordination and judgment through additional flight experience, as well as review the principles of flight, advanced aircraft systems, FAA regulations, and airspace navigation. Course focuses on more advanced flight maneuvers and cross-country flying to prepare the student for the FAA Commercial Pilot Certificate. Course provides dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction. Flight training conducted under the 14 CFR Part 141 certification process.
courses.prereqText: AVIA 21122 and Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course will survey unmanned aerial systems (UAS) and cover UAS history, growth and future applications as well as provide a solid understanding of unmanned aerial systems' design, development, and deployment. Students will be introduced to UAS platforms and sensors, UAS system designs, flight dynamics, communication, navigation, and electronic and mechanical components. The course will also include evolving other issues in unmanned aircraft operations: the aviation regulatory system airspace integration, safety and human factors, ethical and legal issues, and the future of unmanned aircraft systems.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation¿s Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 20003. Course is designed to develop the knowledge and piloting skills necessary to safely and proficiently exercise the responsibilities of a commercial pilot with a multi-engine rating. Course emphasizes advanced knowledge of aerodynamics, aeronautical decision making of multi-engine aircraft systems, aircraft performance, abnormal/emergency procedures, and FAA regulations.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation¿s Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 20003.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Introduces the student to issues influencing human performance in the complex operational aviation environment. Emphasis on theory and practical applications of cognitive processing, aeronautical decision-making, interpersonal interaction and communication, and design elements intended to optimize man-machine interaction.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers a comprehensive range of topics from foundational marketing concepts to specific strategic challenges within the aviation sector, emphasizing strategic frameworks, market analysis (PESTE and SWOT), market segmentation, targeting, and positioning (STP), the 4 Ps/7 Ps marketing mix, pricing strategies, branding, loyalty programs, digital marketing, airline alliances, and sustainability, all applied to the aviation industry context.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program, private pilot certificate, and completion of or concurrent enrollment in AVIA 30001. Flight training course emphasizes multi-engine operations and prepares the student for commercial certification with multi-engine rating. Course provides dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction in a multi-engine aircraft and conducted under FAR Part 141. Flight training conducted under the 14 CFR Part 141 certification process.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot program, private pilot certificate, and completion of or concurrent enrollment in AVIA 30001.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Provides an in-depth study of complex aircraft systems. Emphasis on electronic flight instruments, aircraft monitoring systems, high altitude aerodynamics, pressurization systems, turbine systems, weight and balance, hydraulic, fuel, ignition, and fire protection systems.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers airline business fundamentals, financial statement analysis, different aircraft acquisition and leasing structures, capital sources (debt, equity, and leasing), risk management (fuel hedging), and airline finance. Key topics include understanding the costs and revenues of airlines, evaluating asset values (residual values for aircraft), and analyzing financial performance indicators to support decision-making in the industry.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers historical attempts at flight, the development of early aircraft, key pioneers like the Wright brothers, the Golden Age of flight, the impact of World Wars on aviation technology, the Jet Age, the rise of commercial aviation, modern technological advancements, globalization, and the future of flight. Course content will include cultural, social, economic, and political contexts, as well as military and space exploration aspects.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course will focus on management of aviation/aerospace supply chain processes and performance. A broad instructional approach will encompass the processes associated with the production of goods and services, including the movement of raw materials, inventory, and finished products. Students will be introduced to a variety of industry examples and cases related to aviation/aerospace domestic and global demand-driven supply chains to understand and evaluate the vital role of effective and efficient supply chain management.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course examines the ethical landscape of the aviation industry, exploring the complex interaction between safety, business practices, environmental concerns, social responsibility, and individual actions within the aviation environment.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: History and evolution of aviation governmental regulatory agencies in the US and internationally, including FAA, ICAO, and homeland security. Agency organization and operation, and legislative acts and treaties related to enforcement of aviation standards.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course provides a broad understanding of the air transportation industry and an in-depth knowledge of the organizational structures, managerial functions and operational aspects of major and regional air carriers and all-cargo operations. Historical advancements, economic characteristics, regulatory frameworks, and safety and security will be examined.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: The course covers the entire process of moving cargo by air, from booking and documentation to handling, security, and delivery. Includes aircraft and ground equipment, Unit Load Devices (ULDs), special cargo handling, air cargo documentation, rating and pricing, carrier liability, regulatory requirements, air cargo sales and marketing, and information on the latest technologies and industry best practices.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers fundamental business concepts within the aviation industry, including airline and airport operations, aviation law, financial and economic principles, safety management systems, human resources, revenue management, marketing, sustainability, and regulatory environments. Managing the major elements of the aviation industry, including aircraft manufacturing and air transportation system.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: The course focuses on the fundamentals of project administration and management with emphasis on the human, organizational, and technical dimensions of leading projects within the aviation industry. Students will learn core methodologies and processes, and apply them to real-world aviation projects, including airports, aircraft systems, and operational improvements.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers a wide range of topics including airside and landside operations, aviation safety and security, air traffic management, airport planning and design, airline and cargo logistics, customer service, aviation law and regulations, and financial and economics management. Includes specialized areas like ground handling, crisis management, airport master planning, and airport-airline relations, preparing students to manage the complex, day-to-day functions of an airport.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration, plus instrument and commercial flight ratings. Course provides the student with a detailed study of the responsibilities and teaching concerns of a certified flight instructor (CFI), providing the fundamentals of teaching and learning, including strategic teaching methods, process of learning, effective evaluations, and flight instructor responsibilities. Course emphasizes knowledge of pedagogy for teaching aeronautical knowledge and skills and prepares the student for the CFI Initial Practical Test. The course culminates with the student successfully completing the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Fundamentals of Instructing Knowledge Exam.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration, plus instrument and commercial flight ratings.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 23112. Flight training course required for the student to qualify for the FAA Certified Flight Instructor - Airplane Certificate. Course provides dual flight instruction and solo flight instruction conducted under FAR Part 141. Flight training conducted under the 14 CFR Part 141 certification process.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 23112.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of the strategic management process as applied to the aviation industry, including airlines, airports, and related service providers. Students will analyze the complex and competitive aviation environment, learn to formulate and implement business strategies, and evaluate an organization's performance. The curriculum integrates traditional strategic management theories with specific aviation-related issues such as technological innovation, sustainability, and regulatory landscapes.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and ENSC 30113. Understanding and application of weather theory in relation to flight operations. Problem-based learning situations on the adverse effects of weather to increase hazardous weather awareness for pilots. Course includes meteorology, characteristics of the atmosphere, weather observations and forecasts, and weather phenomena affecting flight safety.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and ENSC 30113. Understanding and application of weather theory in relation to flight operations.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the operational and managerial aspects of the business and general aviation sector. Students will explore the functions of Fixed-Base Operators (FBOs), the management of corporate and private flight departments, and the regulatory framework that governs non-commercial aviation. Topics will include business models, safety management, market analysis, financial considerations, and ground support services for general aviation and business aircraft.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the domestic and international laws and regulations affecting the civil aviation industry. Students will examine key legal instruments, regulatory bodies, and case law that govern various aspects of aviation, including safety, security, liability, and economic issues.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Aviation Administration concentration. Permit required; designed as the capstone course. This capstone, project-based course integrates and applies knowledge and skills from across the Aviation Administration curriculum to real-world industry challenges. Students engage in case studies, applied individual projects, group analysis, and a comprehensive exam to demonstrate mastery of strategic management, regulatory compliance, safety, and operational decision-making. Assignments emphasize analyzing complex problems, applying industry frameworks, proposing solutions, and communicating findings through professional reports and presentations.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Aviation Administration concentration.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration. Introduces crew resource management (CRM) as a cornerstone of modern aviation safety. Provides a thorough understanding of crew communications, team building, leadership, decision-making, situational awareness, and use of automation.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers the fundamentals of aviation and airline economics, including market structure, pricing, and revenue management, alongside financial analysis, demand forecasting, and the economic impacts of regulations and alliances. Key topics include supply and demand dynamics in air transport, cost structures, different airline business models, the role of airports, and emerging market trends. The course will also address cargo transportation, technological advancements, and the broader economic and environmental effects of the aviation industry.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course introduces the principles, practices, and regulatory framework of aviation safety. Students will explore key aspects of safety management and risk assessment, with attention to pilot psychology, physiology, and human factors. Emphasis is placed on developing critical thinking skills to evaluate safety challenges and make informed decisions that support safe aviation operations.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 32333. This course serves as the technical capstone for the professional aviation major seeking pilot training and will prepare students for the transition to 14 CFR 121 operations. The theory, operation, and maintenance of modern aircraft subsystems including engines, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, flight controls, high-speed and high-altitude aerodynamics, performance management and environmental systems, as well as avionics like autopilots and navigation will be covered.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot concentration and AVIA 32333.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course covers foundational human resource management (HRM) principles and their application to the unique aviation context, including human resource planning, recruitment and selection for aviation-specific roles, training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations, and talent and succession planning. Key aviation-specific elements include adherence to civil aviation law, safety management systems, and emergency response planning.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course examines labor relations in the U.S. air transportation industry within the framework of the Railway Labor Act and the National Labor Relations Act. Students will explore the Constitutional foundations of labor law and analyze how these laws shape aviation regulations under 14 CFR, including flight crew workload, staffing requirements, flight deck operations, flight safety, and operations in the National Airspace System.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of aviation security principles, regulatory frameworks, and risk assessment methodologies. Students will develop the knowledge and skills needed to identify threats, assess vulnerabilities, and implement effective security countermeasures for airports, aircraft, and passengers.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: An examination of the regulatory, political, economic impact and structural organization of international aviation. Contemporary issues in the national and international environment will be discussed. Global issues surrounding advances in international Air Traffic Management (ATM) will be discussed, as well as the international Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and its practices.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: The course covers essential leadership skills, ethics, communication, and team dynamics within the context of the aviation industry, including topics such as foundational leadership concepts and styles, strategic management, financial forecasting, organizational behavior, aviation regulations, safety management systems, and the importance of professional ethics and a positive safety culture. Examine the role that airline leaders play in shaping aviation companies and how evolving companies shape airline leaders.

courses.subject: AVIA
courses.description: This course will cover the entire investigation process, from scene management and evidence collection to human factors analysis and report writing, focusing on regulatory requirements and practical skills such as witness interviewing, field techniques, wreckage and evidence analysis, and crashworthiness principles. Key topics include structural and mechanical failures, weather impacts, fire investigation, site documentation, and the use of investigative equipment, often reinforced with real-world case studies and practical exercises.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two hours lecture and one two-hour laboratory period per week. A study of biology spanning contemporary issues in the biological sciences from the cellular and molecular to the ecosystem and biosphere levels of biological organization. Laboratory experiences are conducted in the biology computer lab. Designed for non-science majors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in BIOL 10503 or BIOL 10513 or CHEM 10113. This course provides students with support, advice, professional development, and practice applying various learning strategies as they work to build skills for success in the field of Biology and Pre-Health studies. Pass/No Credit grade basis only. The credit cannot be applied toward the biology requirement of any major or minor.
courses.prereqText: Concurrent enrollment in BIOL 10503 or BIOL 10513 or CHEM 10113.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Microbiology Gen Transfer NSC

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: One laboratory period per week. This laboratory is an inquiry-based course that provides an introduction to investigative techniques in biology and skills required for the analysis and presentation of scientific findings. Throughout the course there will be a focus on molecules through cells. This course is required for each student declaring a major interest in Biology and/or with an interest in pre-health programs.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: A senior high school course in Biology or Chemistry. This course is an introduction to the inner workings of cells, with the theme of examining the common biomolecular foundation of all living things. Topics include the basic principles of evolution, the molecular organization, structure, and function of cells, the cell cycle (including mitosis and meiosis), gene expression, metabolism, and Mendelian and molecular genetics. This course is designed for science majors.
courses.prereqText: A senior high school course in Biology or Chemistry.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: One laboratory period per week. This is a laboratory introduction to the diversity, evolution, anatomy and physiology of eukaryotic organism (protists, fungi, plants, and animals.) Topics covered include the principles of evolution by natural selection , population genetics, speciation, anatomy, physiology, and taxonomy. This course is required for each student declaring a major in Biology and/or with an interest in pre-health programs.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: A senior high school course in Biology or Chemistry. This course is an introduction to the workings of organisms (prokaryotes, protists, fungi, plants, and animals), with the theme of exploring the variety of solutions that have arisen in living things in response to the challenges of life. Topics include the principles of evolution, population genetics, speciation, biological systematics, reproduction, homeostasis, and physiology across various branches of life. This course is designed for science majors.
courses.prereqText: A senior high school course in Biology or Chemistry.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: This is an inquiry-based laboratory course that provides an introduction to investigative techniques in biology and practice in the analysis and presentation of scientific findings. The topics investigated span the full scope of biology, from molecules and cells through populations and ecosystems. The course consists of one credit hour of lecture and two credit hours of lab, and is designed for science majors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Must also be enrolled in BIOL 10503. Special problems.
courses.prereqText: Must also be enrolled in BIOL 10503.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: limited to students who are majoring in Nursing (not Nursing pre-majors), students whose first major is Kinesiology (not Kinesiology minors), junior and senior-level students with the pre-health PA tag, or instructor permission. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. The structure and function of cells and tissues; the architectural plan of the human body, and the integumentary, skeletal, muscular systems and nervous systems. This course is intended for Nursing, Health and Fitness, and Athletic Training majors as well as College of Science and Engineering majors who require Anatomy and Physiology as a prerequisite for application to graduate or professional school.
courses.prereqText: limited to students who are majoring in Nursing (not Nursing pre-majors), students whose first major is Kinesiology (not Kinesiology minors), junior and senior-level students with the pre-health PA tag, or instructor permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 20204 with a grade of C or better, NTDT major with sophomore or higher standing, or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Structure and function of the circulatory, digestive, respiratory, excretory, reproductive and endocrine systems of the human body. This course is intended for Nursing, Nutrition, Health and Fitness and Athletic Training majors, as well as College of Science and Engineering majors who require Anatomy and Physiology as a prerequisite for application to graduate or professional school.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 20204 with a grade of C or better, NTDT major with sophomore or higher standing, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Pre-requisites: Completion of BIOL 20204, NTDT major, BSE in Science Education major, or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Microorganisms and the manner in which they affect health; characteristics, growth requirements, methods of transfer, and reactions of the body toward invading organisms and the principles underlying immunity. This course cannot be applied to the Biology BA, Biology BS, or Biomedical Sciences BS degree and is not intended for pre-health students applying to professional schools such as medical, dental, PA, or veterinary schools. Credit will not be given for both BIOL 20234 and 30304.
courses.prereqText: Completion of BIOL 20204, NTDT major, BSE in Science Education major, or permission of instructor.

The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 10503 and 10513. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Study of the diversity of invertebrate animals including their morphology, physiology, development, evolution, and natural history. Emphasis on their role as model organisms in biological and biomedical research.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: 10501, 10503, 10511, 10513. The economic importance of plants for food, building, material, clothing, fuel, medicine, oils, dyes and other products.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 10503, 10513 and 10501 or 10523. A general course in microbiology intended for Biology majors or pre-health students applying to professional schools such as medical, dental, physician's assistant or veterinary schools. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Credit will not be given for both BIOL 20234 and 30304.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 10503, 10513 and 10501 or 10523. A general course in microbiology intended for Biology majors or pre-health students applying to professional schools such as medical, dental, physician's assistant or veterinary schools.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or ENSC 30133 Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. An Interdisciplinary exploration of the biology, chemistry, geology, physics, and human use of the ocean and its resources. This course is recommended for students with a major interest in the life and earth sciences. (Crosslisted as BIOL/ENSC 30324)
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or ENSC 30133 Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 10503, and 10513. Three hours lecture per week. Principles and concepts of ecology and their application to environmental biology and conservation. Topics will include human impacts on the environment and current issues of importance to global sustainability.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture and one laboratory per week. This course focuses on the form and functional significance of anatomical structures in vertebrate animals. The objectives of the course are to introduce students to the anatomical evidence for evolution and to help students develop an understanding of vertebrate anatomy that will prepare them for graduate or medical gross anatomy courses.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Biol 10513 and Biol 10511 or 10523; Pre-Dental track student. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Study of structure and functional significance of tissues, organs, and organ systems in the human body, with attention to selected disease processes. Students will develop an understanding of human anatomy that will prepare them for graduate or medical gross anatomy courses. Credit will not be given for both BIOL 30414 and either 20204 or 20214.
courses.prereqText: Biol 10513 and Biol 10511 or 10523;

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: PSYC 10213, 10514, 10524 or its equivalent. Study of the nervous system, action systems, and sensory systems as background for the physiological bases of discrimination, motivation, emotions, and learning. (Crosslisted as BIOL/PSYC 30463.)
courses.prereqText: PSYC 10213, 10514, 10524 or its equivalent.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Study of the morphology, life history, physiology, ecology, evolution and socio-economic aspects of plants. Coverage includes the cyanobacteria, fungi and algae.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 10503 completed at TCU, BIOL 10513, and CHEM 10113 or instructor permission. Three hours lecture per week. Basic structure and function of plant and animal cells; molecular genetics of cells and organisms; mechanisms governing cell reproduction and differentiation.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 10503 completed at TCU, BIOL 10513, and CHEM 10113 or instructor permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two hours lecture and one two-hour laboratory per week. This course details the history of life on Earth. Emphasis is placed on the major biomes of the Earth and the unique conditions that influence life in each biome. Students investigate evolutionary processes and historical classifications of lifeforms, and analyze the impact humans have had on life on Earth. There are outdoor labs and field trip opportunities to study local plants and animals. This course is suitable for both Biology majors and non-Biology majors who have broad interests in the outdoors and nature.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Characteristics of the major groups and families of flowering plants. Basic history and general principles of taxonomy and fundamental concepts of phylogeny and plant evolution. Identification of plants represented in the local flora.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 10503 or 10513. In this course, human ecto- and endo-parasites will be discussed along with their associated diseases. Students will gain knowledge of parasite life cycle, molecular mechanisms of entry, mechanisms of immune evasion and current and potential therapies. Public health strategies for control and elimination of parasitic diseases will also be explored.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484 or 20485 or 10164. An introduction to image formation for molecular and medical applications. This course covers the fundamentals of optic, x-ray and MRI, image creation, detectors, basics of image processing, quantitative analysis and a variety of applications in biophysics and in medicine. Includes off-campus lab work. (Crosslisted as BIOL/PHYS 30843.)

courses.description: Honors Seminar. May be repeated for credit when the topic changes.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30403 or 30603. This seminar course will introduce biology students to a wide range of research areas within the biological sciences, aid students in developing scientific communication skills, and provide student an opportunity to network with scientists from diverse fields in biology. At most one credit hour of BIOL 40101 and/or BIOL 40110 may be applied to the Biology major, Biomedical Sciences major, or Biology minor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603. This 0.5-hour course focuses on a variety of topics relevant to students who are interested in careers in the health professions. At most, one credit hour of BIOL 40101 and/or BIOL 40110 may be applied to the Biology majors, Biomedical Science major, or Biology minor.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603. Three hours lecture per week. Survey course in the study of mechanisms of inheritance with particular emphasis on molecular genetics.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603. A one credit hour laboratory course (one laboratory period a week). After completion of the course the student will develop an understanding of concepts and techniques currently in use in molecular biology and biotech research laboratories and will learn how to use basic bioinformatics tools to analyze DNA sequences.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603; CHEM 30123 (or concurrent enrollment) or permission of instructor. A study of the molecular mechanisms of human disease with an emphasis on the role of intracellular signaling events on the manifestation of disease, gene expression/regulation, the structure and function of macromolecules, cell growth and differentiation, and biotechnology based solutions to treatment.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603; CHEM 30123 (or concurrent enrollment) or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two three-hour laboratories plus associated lectures each week. Prerequisites: BIOL 30603 and 40123. Experiments that illustrate the basic principles of transmission and molecular genetics.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 10501, 10503, 10511, 10513, 30403, and 30603. Genetics plays an important and diverse role in the preservation of biological diversity. This course consists of two one-hour lectures and one three-hour laboratory each week and covers genetic theory and methods that are utilized in modern conservation efforts. Laboratory exercises focus on 1) the practical aspects of DNA extraction methods, molecular markers, PCR, sequencing, and capillary electrophoresis, and 2) analyzing the resulting genetic data.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Six semester hours in Biology. This course consists of two one-hour lectures and one three-hour laboratory each week. Lectures cover the evolution, anatomy and physiology, life histories, behaviors, and conservation of birds. The laboratory portion of the course includes identifying birds with molecular methods and field trips to identify common species of Texas birds. Five Saturday morning field trips are required.
courses.prereqText: Six semester hours in Biology.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: six semester hours in Biology. Two hour lectures and two hours of laboratory per week. This course introduces advanced undergraduate students to mammals. Lectures will examine the major topics of mammalian biology, including the evolutionary history, classification, adaptations, ecology, and natural history of mammals. Field techniques for the study of mammalian biodiversity and abundance will also be covered in this course. Field trips will be required. (Crosslisted as BIOL/ENSC 40173.)
courses.prereqText: six semester hours in Biology.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603 and BIOL 30403 OR Instructor Permission. This course critically engages the historical eugenics movement in the United States and its precursors in the broader Western scientific tradition with attention to current and future advancements in biology. Students will employ a combination of scientific and ethical analysis to interrogate social/political and biological claims about inherited traits and race that were dominant in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Students will further analyze contemporary advancements in biology while applying ethical lessons from the past.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603 and BIOL 30403 OR Instructor Permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30603 or permission of the instructor. Two hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Study of basic tissues of the vertebrate body and how they differentiate.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30603 or permission of the instructor. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. An introduction to developmental biology and embryology. Modern molecular and genetic techniques will be combined with classic anatomical embryology.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: C- or better in BIOL 30603, or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. The immune system; characteristics of antigens; antibodies and their reactions; cellular and humoral aspects of immunity; immune disorders.
courses.prereqText: C- or better in BIOL 30603, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30304 or BIOL 40254. This lecture-based course features current research in Immunology that focuses on how manipulations of the innate or adaptive immune system can modulate disease states. This includes how microbes overcome immune defenses, failures in immune system function and how the immune system can be therapeutically modified to treat disease.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30304 or BIOL 40254.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 40123. This class will consist of two hours of lecture and one laboratory per week. The course focuses on the ways in which information at the genome level has become integral to Biology. The labs are designed to give students hands on experience analyzing genomic data to ask and answer specific questions. Contemporary primary literature will be discussed.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40123.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor. This course focuses on advanced topics in medical microbiology including disease mechanisms of major human pathogens, the host response, and antibiotic development and resistance. Scientific approaches used to investigate these topics are emphasized through reading and discussion of the primary literature.
courses.prereqText: Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. An ecological approach to the study of the distribution of plant and animal communities.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Six semester hours in Biology. Two hour lectures and a three hour laboratory each week. This discussion-oriented course introduces advanced undergraduate students to the general principles of wildlife ecology and how those principles can be applied to wildlife management and conservation. The objectives of this course are 1) to provide an introduction to the major concepts of Wildlife Ecology and Management and 2) to allow you to learn the application of the scientific method to ecological problems. Laboratory exercises are required. (Crosslisted as BIOL/ENSC 40353)
courses.prereqText: Six semester hours in Biology.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603 with a C or better or permission of instructor. Basic functions of the major human body systems will be studied in terms of physical and chemical principles and system interactions.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603 with a C or better or permission of instructor. Basic functions of the major human body systems will be studied in terms of physical and chemical principles and system interactions.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 40403. This course focuses on the underlying principles of toxicology including dose-response curves, routes of contaminant exposure, contaminant fate in the environment and in organisms, and xenobiotic metabolism. Discussions of both historical and contemporary primary literature will be used to explore the specific effects of contaminants on various physiological systems.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40403.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 40403. Two hours of lecture and one laboratory period per week. The course will focus on the structure and function of hormone signaling systems in vertebrate organisms. Contemporary primary literature will be discussed and the laboratory will expose students to the experimental design and methods utilized in modern endocrinology research.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40403.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHEM 30123 and C- or better in BIOL 30603, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lecture per week. The structures, properties, and functions of biological molecules (proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, and carbohydrates), with emphasis on analysis techniques and relation to physiology.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30123 and C- or better in BIOL 30603, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 40513 or BIOL/CHEM 50133 or equivalent course. Two hours of lecture and two hours of laboratory per week. Students will learn structural biology techniques important for designing pharmaceuticals and design a drug to their favorite protein target. Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 40523.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40513 or BIOL/CHEM 50133 or equivalent course.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30603 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. Survey of viruses, molecular biology of virus life cycles, viral pathogenesis and gene therapy using viral vectors.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30603 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 40101. This course will build the professional skills necessary for undergraduate students to pursue and succeed in future graduate work and professional endeavors. Students will reflect on how their work, activities and life experiences have prepared them for a career in biological research and develop written and verbal communication skills necessary to apply to graduate school and/or research-focused career opportunities. Credit may not be applied to a Biology degree program or the Biology minor for both BIOL 40701 and SCIE 30613.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40101.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: 6 credit hours of Biology or equivalent. The course examines selected cultures in an international setting. Social and scientific factors are related to health beliefs and practices and health care delivery systems of the country visited and examined. Critical analysis of selected topics will be accomplished. Usually taught in summer abroad program. (Cross-listed as BIOL 40703/NURS 30063/ENSC 40203)
courses.prereqText: of Biology or equivalent.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one to four credit, lecture-only course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one to four credit, lecture-only course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one to four credit lecture with integrated lab course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors. This course can be repeated.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one to four credit lecture with integrated lab course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one or two credit lab course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors. This course can be repeated.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, or permission of the instructor. This one or two credit lab course will deal with a specific topic in Biology that is appropriate for Biology majors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Written permission of the instructor of the course in which the student plans to serve. Students serve as laboratory instructors of one section per week in introductory-level biology courses. Students receive 1 credit for serving as laboratory instructors for one section per week and one additional credit for each three hours of additional duties per week including laboratory staff meetings. May be repeated once.
courses.prereqText: Written permission of the instructor of the course in which the student plans to serve.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Written permission of the instructor of the course in which the student plans to serve. Students receive one credit hour for serving as laboratory instructors of one section per week and one additional credit hour for each three hours of additional duties per week including laboratory staff meetings. This course is intended only for undergraduate Teaching Assistants in courses above the freshman level. Not to exceed six hours credit on the major and eight hours credit total.
courses.prereqText: Written permission of the instructor of the course in which the student plans to serve.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Field and laboratory problems for advanced students. Three clock hours per week of laboratory and/or field work are required for each credit hour, for up to three semester hours credit in a given semester. This course may be taken only once, regardless of the number of credit hours completed, and counts as one upper-level laboratory course towards the Biology BA, Biology BS, or Biomedical Sciences BS degree.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Field and laboratory research experiences for advanced students. An average of nine clock hours per week are required for a total 135 hours per semester. Upon completion of an independent research project, the results will be written in a format suitable for publication in the scientific literature. A student may receive credit for this course only one time. Credit will not be given for both BIOL 40903 and BIOL 40933 for the same project.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 40900 or instructor permission. Field and laboratory problems for advanced students. Three clock hours per week of laboratory and/or field work are required for each semester hour of credit, for up to three semester hours credit in any given semester. This course can be repeated.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40900 or instructor permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Instructor permission. This course focuses on current scientific research in biology including discussions of primary literature and presentations of active research projects. This course may be repeated. May only be taken P/NC. This course cannot be applied toward the course requirements for the biology major or minor.
courses.prereqText: Instructor permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: This course is only for students in the Honors College. Field and laboratory research experiences for advanced students. An average of nine clock hours per week are required for a total of 135 hours. The results will be written in the form of a senior honors research thesis to be presented to the Honors College. A student may receive credit for this course only one time. Credit will not be given for both 40933 and 40903 for the same project.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Senior standing as a biology major with an Intent to Graduate on file in the Dean's Office. One class session. Graduating seniors enrolled in this course will complete the exit exam required of biology majors. May only be taken P/NC.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing as a biology major with an Intent to Graduate on file in the Dean's Office.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor. Concepts, principles, and mechanisms of the function of terrestrial ecosystems, including ecophysiology of component species, nutrient cycling, energy flow, ecosystem stability and global ecology.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or 30603, graduate standing or permission of instructor. Two hours lecture and two hours of computer lab per week. Students will gain knowledge and understanding of how statistical methods are applied to biological research. The course will emphasize hypothesis testing, study design, and the concepts, application, and interpretation of statistical results. Basic probability theory, parametric statistics, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, and non-parametric statistics will be introduced. Credit will not be provided for both BIOL 50123 and BIOL 55123.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or 30603, graduate standing or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 30133 and 40123 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. A general survey of structure and function of biologically important compounds with methods of analysis. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50133.)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30133 and 40123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL/CHEM 50133. Biosynthesis, replication of DNA, synthesis and processing of RNA and proteins, and special topics e.g. brain and muscle functions, hormones and signal transduction, cancer, development, etc. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50143.)
courses.prereqText: BIOL/CHEM 50133.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisites: BIOL/CHEM 50143, or permission of instructor. Molecular mechanism of drug actions, and methods of drug design, discovery and development. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50153.)
courses.prereqText: BIOL/CHEM 50143, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL10503 and BIOL10513 with grades of C or better in each, graduate student standing in a BIOL degree program, or instructor permission. Three hours lecture per week. Concepts and principles of organic evolution. Topics include natural selection, adaptation, quantitative genetics, sexual selection, kin selection, life history characters, speciation, and phylogeny.
courses.prereqText: BIOL10503 and BIOL10513 with grades of C or better in each, graduate student standing in a BIOL degree program, or instructor permission.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: permission of instructor. The current literature associated with the neurobiology of aging, modern research techniques and recent developments in neuroscience and aging research are discussed. This is a participation course in which advanced undergraduate and graduate students will present manuscripts, explain research hypotheses and methodologies and explain results. Open discussion of these papers will include faculty from Biology and Psychology. Topics presented will differ by semester. The course may be repeated three times (taken a maximum of four semesters in all.) (Crosslisted as BIOL/PSYC 50401.)
courses.prereqText: permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Graduate or senior standing or permission of instructor. The fundamentals of functional neuroanatomy and neurophysiology with an emphasis on experimental and theoretical analysis of the basic brain behavior relationships. (Crosslisted as BIOL/PSYC 50463.)
courses.prereqText: Graduate or senior standing or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two four-hour laboratory periods per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 50143 or concurrent registration. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50502)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 50143 or concurrent registration. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50502)

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or graduate student standing. Four semester hours in Biology. This course consists of three 1-hour lectures and one 3-hour lab per week. Lectures cover advanced topics in ecology, with an emphasis on ecological theory, conducting field and lab experiments, and interpreting and communicating scientific findings. The laboratory portion of this course emphasizes study design, hypothesis testing, and the development of independent ecological research projects.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or graduate student standing.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor. Two hours lecture and one laboratory period per week. Study of the physical, chemical and biological factors affecting the ecology of lakes, ponds and streams.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Six semester hours in Biology; travel costs are exclusive of tuition. This course provides an introduction to the marine animals, plants, and ecosystems of the New World tropics. Lecture topics will include tropical oceanography and ecosystems, evolutionary patterns in the tropics, island biogeography, and conservation of marine biodiversity. The field experience will expose students to coastal marine ecosystems (coral reefs, mangroves, beaches, and seagrass beds). Two hours lecture per week, one week of field work in the tropics.
courses.prereqText: Six semester hours in Biology; travel costs are exclusive of tuition.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Two hours lecture per week, one week of field work in the tropics and a terminal project. Prerequisites: Six semester hours in Biology; travel costs are exclusive of tuition; permission of instructors. This course provides an introduction to the animals, plants, and ecosystems of the New World tropics. Lecture topics will include tropical climate and ecosystems, evolutionary patterns in the tropics, and conservation of biodiversity. The field experience will expose students to coastal ecosystems (coral reefs, mangroves, and seagrass beds) as well as tropical, lowland rainforest.
courses.prereqText: Six semester hours in Biology; travel costs are exclusive of tuition; permission of instructors.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: 1. The primary goal is to acquaint the student with the preparation and presentation (oral and/or written) of scientific information from the biological literature. May be repeated for credit with different topics to a maximum of 3 times (one semester hour per topic). 2. Acquainting the student with the preparation and presentation (oral and/or written) of scientific information from the biological literature. May be repeated for credit with different topics to a maximum of 3 times. (One semester hour per topic.)

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 30403 or 30603, and enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program. Two hours lecture and two hours of computer lab per week. Students will gain knowledge and understanding of how statistical methods are applied to biological research. The course will emphasize hypothesis testing, study design, and the concepts, application, and interpretation of statistical results. Basic probability theory, parametric statistics, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, and non-parametric statistics will be introduced. Credit will not be provided for both BIOL 50123 and 55123.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or 30603, and enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program. This course introduces students to foundational skills essential for success in biological research. Topics include literature searches, approaches to reading the scientific literature, research compliance, interpretation of statistics, record keeping, generation of figures and tables, and formulation of a research question.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 55131. This course introduces students to the fundamentals of oral and written scientific communication through the development and presentation of an oral seminar and written proposal over their research goals and objectives.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 55131.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Enrollment in the BIOL BS/MS program and permission of instructor. Field or laboratory research for students in the Biology BS/MS program. Three clock hours per week of laboratory and/or field work are required for each semester hour of credit, for between one to three semester hours credit in any given semester. This course can be repeated once. A minimum of 2 hours of BIOL 55320 Research in Biology is required for the BS/MS in Biology.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in the BIOL BS/MS program and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, and enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program. Advanced coursework in biology, the nature of which is to be determined by the previous preparation and interests of the student. Credit will depend upon the nature of study and amount of work assigned (1-4 hours).
courses.prereqText: BIOL 30403 or BIOL 30603, and enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program.

courses.subject: BIOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program. Up to 3 hours of BIOL 55980 (Thesis 1 ¿ Graded) may be applied to meet the 6-hour thesis requirement for the BS/MS degree in Biology.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in the Biology BS/MS program. Up to 3 hours of BIOL 55980 (Thesis 1 ¿ Graded) may be applied to meet the 6-hour thesis requirement for the BS/MS degree in Biology.

courses.subject: BRST
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: BRST
courses.description: This is a capstone course for the minor, and includes readings in British and colonial/postcolonial studies and an independent project. The independent project is pursued in consultation with the program director, and aims to reflect on the student's work in the minor, to synthesize the skills developed through the student's coursework, and to consider how they might be applied after graduation. Projects may include: an original creative performance; a scientific investigation; a portfolio of critical writing; or a U.S.-based internship with an employer with substantial interests in Britain or the former colonies. All projects also require a journal documenting and reflecting on the student's progress.

courses.subject: BRST
courses.description: Washington Center or at the TCU in London Program. Full-time internships with a public or private agency in Washington, D.C. or in London, England, offered either through the Washington Center or through the TCU in London Program. The internship will allow students to integrate theory and practice in a supervised professional setting, up to 12 semester hours credit. (Offered as BRST or POSC credit.)

courses.subject: BRST
courses.description: 3-day or 4-day per week interns with public or private agencies in London, England, offered through the TCU in London Program. Offered during the fall and spring terms, these internships accommodate students' long-term professional objectives. Internships are offered for either 9 or 12 semester hours credit. Most of the London interns also take one or two classroom courses while in London. (Offered either for BRST or POSC credit.)

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in BUSI 10153. This course is designed to assist students in discovering the wide range of professional opportunities ahead of them. Students will engage in powerful self-assessments, use a variety of skills to continuously expand their opportunity spectrums, learn how to overcome obstacles, conduct effective research, and also experience a first-hand taste of different potential careers.
courses.prereqText: Concurrent enrollment in BUSI 10153.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Sophomore standing AND prior completion of at least one 20000 or 30000 level course (any subject) at TCU. Open to all majors. Does not count toward the Marketing major as an elective. An exploration of professional selling across diverse industries including technology, healthcare, real estate, financial services, and consulting. Students learn modern sales frameworks, discovery questioning, value communication, and relationship-building strategies through industry case studies and AI-enabled simulations. The class is designed to provide broad professional selling skills applicable to any major. Develop transferable communication skills essential for any career. Learn how professionals create value and drive business outcomes without memorizing scripts or making cold calls. For non-Neeley majors, this course may replace MARK 30653 as part of the TCU Certificate in Consultative Selling.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing AND prior completion of at least one 20000 or 30000 level course (any subject) at TCU. Open to all majors. Does not count toward the Marketing major as an elective.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: The class is open to all students admitted to the Neeley School of Business. Students in their First Year enroll in their second semester on campus, or a subsequent semester; transfer students admitted to Neeley may enroll in their first semester on campus, or a subsequent semester. This course provides students seeking a business major with direction and guidance regarding: 1) the major and career selection and exploration process; 2) organizing their internship search; and 3) developing a professional portfolio that will equip them with skills and resources to discover and explore professional opportunities that align with their interests, values, and skills. Students will engage with recruiters, alumni, and Neeley students across a variety of industries and majors to learn about career paths, recruiting timelines, and industry trends. Students will familiarize themselves with Neeley's resources and determine a personalized plan for career exploration and development.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Must be a business major. This course focuses on ethical global business and developing a global mindset from an intellectual, psychological and social perspective. Topics include the global mindset framework, unique characteristics of the global trade environment, globalization of ethical decision making, the role of culture in global business, and responsible, financial and regulatory implications for global business. The student will engage in a cross cultural experience including ethical reflection.
courses.prereqText: Must be a business major.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: A general, semi-technical orientation of the Oil, Gas and Power industries including the origins and overview of the O&G industry, explanation of exploration and production (E&P) processes, logistics, value chain, and the marketing of petroleum, natural gas, and power. Class material will be presented by textbook and guest lecturers.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: 3 hours. Prerequisite: Sophomore standing, must be in the Neeley Leadership Program (NLP). MANA 30833 and MANA 30313 cannot be taken for credit along with this course. This course is designed to help students learn what leadership is and how to be a more effective leader of others. Emphasis in this course is on leading self, including being proactive, setting goals and priorities, and self-awareness of values and strengths and weaknesses as a basis for developing a personalized vision for the kind of leader you want to become.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing, must be in the Neeley Leadership Program (NLP). MANA 30833 and MANA 30313 cannot be taken for credit along with this course.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: 3 hours. Prerequisite: BUSI 30833 with a grade of at least C for students in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program, Sophomore standing, and must be a Business major. This course is designed to help students learn what it takes to effectively lead others one-on-one or in small groups. Emphasis is placed on interpersonal behaviors and skills, including listening, asking questions, feedback giving and receiving, coaching, building trust, followership, and persuasion and communication.
courses.prereqText: BUSI 30833 with a grade of at least C for students in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program, Sophomore standing, and must be a Business major.

courses.description: Prerequisites: Must be a declared Business major or Finance or Accounting minor, and permission of instructor. Students gain practical exposure to business through participation in an internship in a business or community organization. Emphasis is placed on the development of applied skills in one or more of the business disciplines. Students learn about organizational realities and work demands. 1 credit hour. Course may be repeated 3 times to receive a maximum of 3 credit hours.

courses.description: Students gain practical exposure to business through participation in an internship in a business or community organization. Emphasis is placed on developing applied skills in one or more of the business disciplines. Students learn about organizational realities and work demands.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: BUSI 30843 with a grade of at least C and must be in the Neeley Leadership Program (NLP). This course and MANA 40213 cannot both be taken for credit. Organizations rely on team-based structures to increase flexibility and responsiveness in their increasingly dynamic and unpredictable environments. Additionally, given the rapid changes of an Internet-paced global economy, organizations now rely more on teams, versus individuals, to quickly gather complex information, analyze it, and produce sound, timely decisions. As a result, modern organizational work frequently takes place within the boundaries of face-to-face or virtual teams, and knowing how teams function and how best to manage them has become vitally important for successful leadership. The purpose of this course is to expose students to and provide opportunities for them to apply practical knowledge of team dynamics.
courses.prereqText: BUSI 30843 with a grade of at least C and must be in the Neeley Leadership Program (NLP).

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Must be a declared business major. This one-credit course will provide direction and instructional tools for students to complete a departmental honors project in their major department. The goal of the course is to develop a project statement (introduction, literature review, research questions/hypothesis, methodology), and prepare for data collection if applicable.

conditions.text: Declared business major (advanced into a Neeley major)

courses.prereqText: Must be a declared business major. This one-credit course will provide direction and instructional tools for students to complete a departmental honors project in their major department.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Must be a Junior or a Senior standing. An introduction to basic financial literacy. This course will prepare students for lifelong financial success after college by providing them with a foundational knowledge in a number of key topics including: how to create a budget, to buy or lease a car, creating an emergency fund, investment fundamentals, importance of credit scores and much more.
courses.prereqText: Must be a Junior or a Senior standing.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: The course will cover, physical and financial trading of energy commodities ("cash" market, NYMEX contracts, swaps, options, and hedging), technical analysis and, risk control. Addresses the following resource/product groups oil, natural gas, gasoline, heating oil, LNG, electricity and, time permitting, emissions credits. While focused on the North American energy landscape, discussions of international oil and gas markets will be incorporated where appropriate. Students will also actively trade a financial energy derivatives "book" utilizing an online trading simulator.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: A semi-technical study of the electric utility industry, which focuses on traditional and alternative/renewable sources, industry organization, logistics & value chain, power demand management, conservation, and energy efficiency. Demand response methods and programs as well as, smart grids will also be covered.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Principles and practices of doing business in the renewable energy and alternative fuels sectors. Investigates the feasibility and economics of competing energy sources and technologies and considers their contribution to a total system approach to energy business. Includes concepts of innovation, relevant business models, the use of government incentives, tax credits, regulatory mandates, as well as financing, distribution, and infrastructure challenges and evolving markets and consumer demand.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: 3 hours. Prerequisites: Enrolled in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program, and MANA 40213 with at least a grade of C. This course is designed to help students learn what it takes to successfully lead change efforts and plan and implement projects that promote the common good. As such, it will cover topics such as overcoming complacency, creating and communicating new direction, developing support for initiatives, communicating effectively about an initiative, and dealing with resistance, among others. Students in this course are expected to use what they've learned in prior leadership courses to lead a field-based project to a successful completion. Class sessions will help students relate their field experience to topic coverage in this course as well as to other courses in the Neeley Leadership Program.
courses.prereqText: Enrolled in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program, and MANA 40213 with at least a grade of C.

courses.subject: BUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: BUSI 40843 with a grade of at least C for students in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program. For others, any two of the following with a grade of at least C, BUSI 30833, BUSI 30843, MANA 40213, MANA 40343. This course is designed to help students understand the complexity of the contexts in which leadership occurs. Students will gain a better understanding of: 1) the nature of complexity in business and social systems, 2) the implications of complexity for how organizations must think differently about leadership and followership (e.g., regarding organization structure, culture, power and communication), and 3) how each student personally needs to lead and follow in organizational contexts to be successful as they transition into and advance in their careers.
courses.prereqText: BUSI 40843 with a grade of at least C for students in the BNSF Neeley Leadership Program. For others, any two of the following with a grade of at least C, BUSI 30833, BUSI 30843, MANA 40213, MANA 40343.
