courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: This course is designed to provide an introduction to trauma-informed care and interventions. Students will learn about the impact of trauma, the pillars of trauma-informed care and current evidence based, trauma-informed interventions such as Trust-Based Relational Intervention.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: This course is designed to increase awareness about children's issues in the global community both historically and currently. It will focus on children's issues as well as intervention efforts across the globe. Along with class lectures, readings, and video supplements, students will be expected to participate in class discussions and presentations about current global issues. This course is designed to build insight and competency in students who desire to work with children in their future careers.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: 30 cumulative hours of coursework is required. A developmental class is recommended. In this course, history, theory and neuroscience of play are examined. Play as it relates to physical, social, cognitive, language and emotional development is explored in children birth through adolescence. The impact of culture, gender, and technology on children's play is explored. Special attention is given to play observations, assessment through play, and therapeutic play.
courses.prereqText: 30 cumulative hours of coursework is required.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: PSYC 10213 and MATH 10043. The purpose of this course is to familiarize students with the basics of developmental research and evaluation. This class will cover topics such as research versus evaluation, evaluation, research design, research projects start to finish, data and analysis, and reporting findings and publications.
courses.prereqText: PSYC 10213 and MATH 10043.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare students with professional competencies and knowledge in working with children and families. The course will be taught as a seminar style course with visiting professionals and professors teaching on topics such as: Crisis Prevention Intervention (CPI), Child CPR, Child Abuse Prevention and Reporting, Cultural Competencies, Communication Skills, Professional Ethics, Therapeutic Boundaries. At the end of the course, students will have skills and preparation for a variety of careers with children.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 10303 or PSYC 30313 or 40433. This child life course will focus on children in the healthcare environment. It will include study in the following areas pertaining to child life specialists; documentation; scope of practice; impact of illness, injury, and health care of patients and families; family-centered care; therapeutic play; and preparing children for healthcare encounters and life-changing events.
courses.prereqText: NURS 10303 or PSYC 30313 or 40433.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: PSYC/CHDV 50433 and PSYC/CHDV 50443. This experiential course provides advanced opportunities to work with children through internship positions. Service environments will provide experiential learning through which the student will utilize their knowledge of child development. Students can obtain their own positions (e.g., women shelter volunteer; child life specialist practicum) or can take part in internships facilitated by the instructor. Students complete 100 hours at the internship site. Students also attend a weekly one-hour seminar during the semester to discuss their experiences with peers and faculty and learn about working in helping professions. Course may be repeated up to 6 hours. Only 3 hours qualify for credit toward the major.
courses.prereqText: PSYC/CHDV 50433 and PSYC/CHDV 50443.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: This course is designed to explore historical and contemporary theories related to family functioning and to analyze the impact of varying demographics, stressors, and transitions on family dynamics. Theories will be presented in class and applied to diverse family systems within cultural and societal contexts. Emphasis will be placed on non-traditional family systems and the varied impact of stressors on different types of family systems.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: must be a CHDV major and have senior standing. This course is designed for seniors to promote an integrated understanding of the discipline and to examine the significance of research and policy in child development. The emphasis is on assisting the student in developing the ability to critically evaluate methods, problems and findings of research in the field of child development and to evaluate contrasting views of major issues within the discipline.
courses.prereqText: must be a CHDV major and have senior standing.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing. This course is the first of a two-part series of multidisciplinary courses which examine children who have experienced complex developmental trauma, including outcomes, assessments, and interventions through a study of peer-reviewed articles and evidence-based interventions, including Trust-Based Relational Intervention (TBRI). TBRI is an attachment based, trauma-informed intervention designed to meet the complex needs of children through connecting, empowering, and correcting. Emphasis in this course will be attachment theory and the development of healthy relationships. Completing this course is recommended to work at The Hope Connection 2.0 therapeutic camp. (Crosslisted as CHDV/PSYC 50433.)
courses.prereqText: Junior standing.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHDV/PSYC 50433 and junior standing. This course is the second of a two-part series of multidisciplinary courses which examine children who have experienced complex developmental trauma. Emphasis in Trauma and Behavior is on understanding the effects of trauma on the body, brain, and behavior, as well as demonstrating trauma-informed intervention strategies and skills. Completing this course is recommended to work at The Hope Connection 2.0 therapeutic camp. (Crosslisted as CHDV/PSYC 50443.)
courses.prereqText: CHDV/PSYC 50433 and junior standing.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing. This course is designed to present an integrated and comprehensive overview of numerous issues in child development as well as treatments/solutions for those issues. This diverse array of developmental problems will be presented in a series of case-studies by professors from several departments as well as by community professionals who specialize in children's issues. This course is a requirement for the Child Development Minor as well as an elective course in Psychology.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHDV 50433 and 50443. This course is designed to be an intensive study in putting Trust-Based Relational Intervention (TBRI) into practice within a professional setting. Upon successful completion of the course (80% or above) students will earn the title and status of TBRI Practitioner.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admitted to DETR BS/MS 4-1 combined program. This course is the first part of a two-part series of multidisciplinary courses which examine children who have experienced complex developmental trauma, including outcomes, assessments, and interventions through a study of peer-reviewed articles and evidence-based interventions, including Trust-Based Relational Intervention (TBRI). TBRI is an attachment based, trauma-informed intervention designed to meet the complex needs of children through connecting, empowering, and correcting. Emphasis in this course will be attachment theory and the development of healthy relationships.

courses.description: Prerequisites: Admitted to DETR BS/MS 4-1 combined program. This course is designed to present an integrated and comprehensive overview of numerous issues in child development as well as treatments/solutions for those issues. This diverse array of developmental problems will be presented in a series of case studies by professors from several departments as well as by community professionals who specialize in children's issues.
courses.prereqText: Admitted to DETR BS/MS 4-1 combined program.

courses.subject: CHDV
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admitted to DETR BS/MS 4-1 program. This program is designed to immerse students within systems of care supporting and serving children and families. During the class, we will explore the history of and current systems of care serving children and families, hear guest lectures from local providers, visit local organizations serving children and families, and immerse ourselves in the local culture.
courses.prereqText: Admitted to DETR BS/MS 4-1 program.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: Major in engineering. Selected topics from General Chemistry designed to provide mastery of chemistry concepts needed for success in undergraduate engineering courses. Credit will not be given for both CHEM 10013 and CHEM 10113.
courses.prereqText: Major in engineering.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three lecture hours per week. Introduction to chemical principles and their application: stoichiometry, solutions, oxidation-reduction, thermochemistry, atomic structure, bonding theories, molecular geometries, gases/liquids/solids, intermolecular forces of attraction. Emphasis on problem-solving and visualizing matter at the particulate level. Credit will not be given for both CHEM 10013 and CHEM 10113.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: One lecture and one 3-hour laboratory session per week. Prerequisites: CHEM 10113 and prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 10123.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10113 and prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 10123.

courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 10113 with a grade of C- or better. Three lecture hours per week. Introduction to chemical principles and their application: solutions, chemical equilibria (gas, acid/base, solubility), kinetics, thermodynamics, electrochemistry, simple organic nomenclature, transition-metal coordination compounds. Emphasis on problem-solving and visualizing matter at the particulate level.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10113 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 10113 with a grade of C- or better. Three hours lecture, one 3-hour laboratory, and one 1-hour lab lecture per week. The second of a two-semester sequence in introductory chemistry. Selected concepts regarding chemical equilibria, kinetics, electrochemistry, and introductory organic chemistry.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10113 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course, which includes two hours of lecture and one (two hour) laboratory period per week, explores the role of chemistry in artistic expression and cultural practices throughout history. Students will examine the chemical processes involved in various art forms, materials, and techniques involved in the production and preservation of art. Through lectures and hands-on labs, students will investigate topics like color formation, the chemistry of paint mediums, the effects of the environment on artwork and the chemistry of body art and textiles This course is designed for non-science majors.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three lecture hours per week. Introduction to basic chemical principles: atomic & molecular structure, light, bonding, nomenclature, stoichiometry, oxidation-reduction, solutions, gases/liquids/solids, intermolecular forces, and thermochemistry. Emphasis on problem-solving and practical applications from industry, the earth, and living organisms. This course serves as a prerequisite for CHEM 10225, but does not qualify as a prerequisite for CHEM 10123.

Emphasis on problem-solving and practical applications from industry, the earth, and living organisms.

Exposure to techniques, theory, and laboratory practice of quantitative chemical analysis, focusing on gravimetric and volumetric analysis. Students will also gain an introductory understanding of instrumental methods of chemical analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHEM 10122 or 20123. This course aims to cultivate a robust safety culture, aligning with the accreditation standards set by the American Chemical Society (ACS). As safety training becomes a cornerstone of ACS certification, this course empowers students with essential knowledge and skills to navigate laboratory environments safely and responsibly. Designed to be activities-based, the course utilizes hands-on experience to emphasize laboratory safety, allowing students to apply theoretical knowledge in practical settings. Participants will delve into the RAMP framework --Recognize, Assess, Minimize, and Prepare --drawing from the guidelines outlined in Laboratory Safety for Chemistry Students (Hill & Finster, 2010).

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: One hour of lecture per week and seven 4-hour laboratory periods during the semester. Prerequisite: CHEM 10122 or 20123 with a grade of C- or better and prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 30123. Techniques of purification, characterization, and synthesis of organic compounds.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10122 or 20123 with a grade of C- or better and prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 30123.

courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 10123 with a grade of C- or better. A survey of the classes of organic compounds with regard to nomenclature, structure, and reactions.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10123 with a grade of C- or better.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 30123 with a grade of C- or better. Stereochemistry, organic reaction mechanisms, and synthesis of organic compounds.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: The chemical literature, modern research techniques and recent developments in chemistry are discussed. This is a capstone course to be taken by Chemistry and Biochemistry majors in the fall semester of their senior year.

courses.description: Prerequisite: Prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 40123. Alternating weeks of 1-hour laboratory lecture and 4-hour laboratory experiment. Laboratory experiments designed to convey fundamental principles of physical chemistry, with emphasis on chemical equilibrium in solution.
courses.prereqText: Prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 40123.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 10125 or 10122-10123 or 10123- 20123, prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 10524. Studies of the fundamental physical principles relating to the field of chemistry, with an emphasis on thermodynamics and electrochemistry.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10125 or 10122-10123 or 10123- 20123, prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 10524.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: Prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 40133. Alternating weeks of 1-hour laboratory lecture and 4-hour laboratory experiment. Laboratory experiments designed to convey fundamental principles of physical chemistry, with emphasis on polymers and computational methods.
courses.prereqText: Prior or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 40133.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisites: CHEM 40123, MATH 20524, PHYS 20484 or PHYS 10164 (or concurrent enrollment). Continuation of studies of the fundamental physical principles relating to the field of chemistry, with an emphasis on quantum chemistry, spectroscopy, and kinetics.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 40123, MATH 20524, PHYS 20484 or PHYS 10164 (or concurrent enrollment).

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: One hour lecture and one four-hour lab period per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 40123 and CHEM 40121. Theory and application of instrumental methods relevant to the analysis of small molecules and useful macromolecules. Includes electronic, vibrational, NMR, and mass spectroscopic techniques.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 40123 and CHEM 40121.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: A project in chemical research carried out under the direction of a member of the chemistry faculty. The student must have permission from the supervising faculty member prior to registration. (1-3 semester hours).

courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 40513 or BIOL/CHEM 50133 or equivalent course. Two hours of lecture and two hours of laboratory per week. Students will learn structural biology techniques important for designing pharmaceuticals and design a drug to their favorite protein target. Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 40523.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 40513 or BIOL/CHEM 50133 or equivalent course.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: This course deals with the safe handling of chemicals, the inventory and safe disposal of chemicals, safe handling of radioactive materials and lasers as well as details of federal, state and city regulations that apply to safety in academic and industrial laboratories. Ethics in the chemistry and the use of databases and industry-specific software will also be discussed. (This course is only offered P/NC.)

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: One 4-hour laboratory period per week. An introduction to the preparation of laboratory research equipment constructed of sodium and borosilicate glass.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Members of this class act as Chemistry laboratory assistants. Techniques of laboratory instruction are illustrated and the importance of laboratory safety is stressed. 0.5-3 semester hours.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 30133 and 40123 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. A general survey of structure and function of biologically important compounds with methods of analysis. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50133.)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30133 and 40123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL/CHEM 50133. Biosynthesis, replication of DNA, synthesis and processing of RNA and proteins, and special topics e.g. brain and muscle functions, hormones and signal transduction, cancer, development, etc. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50143.)
courses.prereqText: BIOL/CHEM 50133.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisites: BIOL/CHEM 50143, or permission of instructor. Molecular mechanism of drug actions, and methods of drug design, discovery and development. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50153.)
courses.prereqText: BIOL/CHEM 50143, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: One hour lecture and one 4-hour laboratory per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 50163 or concurrent registration. The laboratory emphasizes the synthesis, characterization and transformations of inorganic species.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 50163 or concurrent registration.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 40123 or permission of instructor. A survey of topics in modern inorganic chemistry with emphasis on synthesis, bonding and the mechanisms of reactions.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 40123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Two 4-hour laboratory periods per week. Prerequisite: Prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 50183. Physical chemical principles applied to biochemical systems.
courses.prereqText: Prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 50183.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 40123, prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 50133 or permission of instructor. Biological systems are discussed from the viewpoint of physical chemical theories and methods.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 40123, prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 50133 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 30143, 30133 or permission of instructor. A detailed study of stereochemistry, important organic reactions and mechanisms, organic syntheses and fundamentals of synthetic design.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30143, 30133 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Advanced work in biochemistry, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry to be determined by the previous preparation and interests of the individual student.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHEM 30123. This course will focus on the role that chemistry has played in historical times of conflict. The scientists who made the decisions and the personal and professional conflicts they faced will be presented. Student presentations and daily class discussions will be a significant component of the course grade.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30123.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 30133 and prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 40123. An introduction to modern structural theory and reaction mechanism. Includes a discussion of physical methods.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 30133 and prior or concurrent registration in CHEM 40123.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 50163 or permission of the instructor. An advanced study of the preparative and derivative chemistry of important classes of transition metal and main group element compounds.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 50163 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHEM 40133. An introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics, Transport Phenomena and Physical Chemistry of Surfaces. Continuation of Chemistry 40123-40133.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 40133.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 40133 or permission of instructor. Application of thermodynamics to the study of chemical reactions and phase transitions.

courses.description: Two four-hour laboratory periods per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 50143 or concurrent registration. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50502)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 50143 or concurrent registration. (Crosslisted as BIOL/CHEM 50502)

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. This course will introduce students to experimental techniques developed and used to investigate biological systems. It will discuss modern techniques used in the biomedical sciences, drug discovery and other biophysical and biochemical fields. The course includes lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on exercises in the TCU Biophysics Laboratory and on instrumentation at the Center for Commercialization of Fluorescence Technologies (CCFT) at the UNT Health Sciences Center campus. (Crosslisted as CHEM/PHYS 50763.)
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.description: Prerequisites: CHEM 10123 and 10122 or 10125 or 20123 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. Chemistry of water, soil, energy, and air as related to environmental problems. Subjects include: nutrients and eutrophication, fluorocarbons, sulfur and nitrogen oxides, Eh-pH relationship, natural carbonate reactions, and cation exchange phenomena. (Crosslisted as CHEM/ENSC/GEOL 50783.)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10123 and 10122 or 10125 or 20123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.description: Prerequisite: This course is designed for students with little or no previous knowledge of the Chinese language. It cultivates student cultural knowledge and language skills while communicating in Chinese business environments, tailoring all language training and cultural topics to that end. The language training helps students cultivate basic language skills to interact with the Chinese people. Cultural topics provide a framework for Western learners to develop and Eastern perspective, guiding learners to behave in a culturally appropriate manner when they communicate within Chinese business environments.
courses.prereqText: This course is designed for students with little or no previous knowledge of the Chinese language.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.description: Chinese Calligraphy is designed for students who are interested in Chinese culture, philosophy, and art. Students will practice and acquire basic calligraphy strokes, radicals and characters by using traditional Chinese calligraphy brushes. Students will also learn the meaning and philosophy behind each Chinese character. Prior knowledge in Chinese language and culture is not required.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.description: This is an introductory Chinese course for students with no or little prior experience in standard Mandarin. It provides students a solid training in all four skills -- listening, speaking, reading and writing, with emphasis on practicing pronunciations and building vocabulary, as well as acquiring fundamental grammatical structures. In addition, Chinese cultures will be briefly taught throughout the class. No prerequisite.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHIN 10153 with a C- or better. This course continually covers basic Mandarin Chinese to students who have already taken a semester in Chinese. It continues strengthening integrated training in all four skills -- listening, speaking, reading and writing, but more efforts will be given to spoken and reading practicing. In addition, Chinese cultures will be briefly noted throughout the class.
courses.prereqText: CHIN 10153 with a C- or better.

Working with familiar topics, students will learn to comprehend short paragraph-level utterances; interact effectively in a variety of straightforward, concrete conversational situations; and read short paragraphs and write short, well-focused descriptive or narrative works.

Upon the completion of this course, students should have acquired the following abilities: 1) Listening: can understand interpersonal conversations on practical and social topics; follow presentation on social topics or topics of personal interest and individual relevance; 2) Speaking: can engage in conversations on topics of personal interest and individual relevance and present ideas and opinions with a level of clarity and precision that native speakers can understand; 3) Reading: can comprehend text materials on non-specialized topics with the help of dictionaries; 4) Writing: can produce most kinds of informal correspondence; can present ideas and opinions at paragraph level with a level of clarity and precision that native speakers can understand.

It provides students with an opportunity to rethink the similarities and differences between Chinese and American cultures reflected in Chinese movies. The course will be conducted in Chinese through lectures and guided discussions of designated topics.

Major topics such as the Chinese language, history, philosophy, religion, literature and the arts, as well as contemporary issues, will be studied. The scenes represent the domains of Chinese popular culture, social change, cultural tradition, and politics. The topics include online dating, brand-name fever, television dramas, modern views of marriage, population change, Chinese food culture, Confucianism in modern China, and democracy.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: Instructor permission required and restricted to recognized members of the TCU Forensic Team. Participation credit for members of the competitive forensics team. Course members will practice and engage in intercollegiate competition in public address, oral interpretation, and debate. Repeatable a maximum of 8 times. A maximum total of 4 credits may be applied toward a Communication Studies major, 3 credits toward a minor.
courses.prereqText: Instructor permission required and restricted to recognized members of the TCU Forensic Team. Participation credit for members of the competitive forensics team.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or by permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163 or permission of instructor. Training in clear, logical, and persuasive communication; analysis, exposition, reasoning, and use of evidence; practice in effective delivery; classroom participation in debates.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or by permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. Students will investigate British origins of contemporary parliamentary debate and decision-making, will visit important sites such as the Houses of Parliament and Hyde Park Speaker's Corner, and will learn to conduct parliamentary debates and employ rules of parliamentary procedure in meetings.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113. Participation in decision-making groups to develop skills related to effective group communication. Factors affecting group interactions are considered.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. Students will develop knowledge and skills necessary to facilitate conflict conversations in interpersonal and organizational settings.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. COMM 10123 or 10163. Applies dyadic communication principles to specialized interviewing situations. Skills development is stressed.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. COMM 10123 or 10163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better; COMM 20223 with a C- or better. Communication channels and networks in organizations; analysis of barriers to effective communication; solving practical communication problems; communication and dynamics in work groups.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better; COMM 20223 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10133 or permission of instructor.Training in message and content development for public presentations in a variety of contexts. Students will develop strategic messaging and visual production skills. Theory and practical experience related to the formulation, presentation, and evaluation of public presentations.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10133 or permission of instructor.Training in message and content development for public presentations in a variety of contexts.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20223 and COMM 30163. Explores organizational communication within special contexts. Included theoretical concepts applicable to conflict, culture, media, etc. Repeatable for maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20223 and COMM 30163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better. Introduction to the reception and processing of information. Examines theory and research in areas such as attention, cognitive capacity, and attribution. Examines the role of listening in a variety of contexts, including therapeutic communication, learning, and critical thinking.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better. Introduction of the conceptual foundations of nonverbal communication. Theoretical perspectives, research methods, and applications of nonverbal communication are also explored in a variety of contexts.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113. Explores interpersonal communication within special contexts. Includes theoretical concepts applicable to gender, aging, and health. Repeatable for maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163 and COMM 20113, and COMM 20223. Explores theory and research related to social influence in relationships and communication processes.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163 and COMM 20113, and COMM 20223.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 and 20223 with a C- or better. Introduces students to scientific perspectives on human emotion and examines the social, moral, and cultural dimensions of communication emotions.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 and 20223 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 and COMM 20223. This survey course examines the influence of culture on our communicative interactions with others. Emphasis is placed on identifying the relationship between communication and culture, developing intercultural communication competence, and understanding the elements that constitute and separate cultures.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 20113 and COMM 20223.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163. Examination of the relationship between gender and communication. Critical analysis of how communication creates, maintains, and transforms views of gender in cultural, social, and historical contexts.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. Investigate great British orators, orations, and persuasive techniques used to compel audiences at the actual sites where these famous speeches took place.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163. The purpose of this course is to introduce students to training and development in organizational settings. Students will learn the art and science of designing, delivering, and assessing training programs. Emphasis will be placed on teaching communication skills to adult learners and exploring potential career opportunities in training and development.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better and COMM 20223 with a C- or better. This course is an introduction to theories and research related to health communication. We will focus on how messages from interpersonal, organizational, and mediated sources affect physical, mental, and social health and well-being. Students may not receive credit for both HCOM 10313 and COMM 30313.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better and COMM 20223 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Explores communication within special contexts and content areas. Course topics focus on novel topics or approaches within the study of communication. May be repeated with different course titles to a maximum of six hours.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department. Examines the evolving relationship between society and media from social, cultural, technological, organizational, legal, and economical perspectives by surveying the functions of and influences on media and media engagement.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only; department permission. Independent work in specially designed projects not covered by regular course offerings. (1-6 semester hours, 3 hours maximum per semester.)
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only; department permission.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only; department permission. This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only; department permission.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163. Examination of the major concepts in rhetorical theory. By studying on location, emphasis is placed on understanding the conceptions of rhetoric in antiquity, identifying how these inform historical and contemporary rhetorical acts, and evaluating the persuasive techniques used to compel audiences in a variety of social, political, and religious contexts.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163. Examination of the major concepts in rhetorical theory.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163. Explores a variety of theories and applications of persuasive communication. Focus is on the public discourse of global issues.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or 10163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only; COMM 30163, permission of instructor, and department chair. This course not only explores the analysis, planning and execution of marketing and promotional goals, strategies and tactics for a corporate structure, its divisions and departments through research, discussion, peer and instructor evaluation and experimentation but also places students in the role of communication professionals responsible for the production of tangible solutions and content using the Bob Schieffer College of Communication and other TCU academic units as its primary clients.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only; COMM 30163, permission of instructor, and department chair.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; department permission. A research paper developing from the student's specialization in the Honor's Seminar.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; department permission.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better. Seminar designed to acquaint students with the factors affecting interpersonal conflict and to provide students with appropriate communication skills necessary for successful conflict resolution and negotiation in a variety of contexts, both personal and professional. Emphasis is on exploring practical, theoretical and critical analyses of conflict and negotiation in an active learning environment.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better;

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; complete 15 hours in Communication Studies; junior or senior standing; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better or permission of instructor. Participation in professional internship experience approved by course instructor. Online forums and writing assignments focus on analysis of communication observations and issues in professional environments. May be repeated up to six hours, with unique employer placements. For BS degree, only three hours qualify for credit toward the 3-course, 40000-level departmental requirement.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; complete 15 hours in Communication Studies; junior or senior standing; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better. The development and use of communication skills to manifest positive character traits for the benefit of self, others, and society at large.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; and COMM 30163 with a C- or better. Examines power and privilege in organizations, focusing on gender, race, class, ability, age, sexuality, and religion. Students will develop awareness of how their background shapes communication as well as exploring strategies for increasing inclusion in organizations
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; and COMM 30163 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 30173 or permission of instructor. Advanced training in speech performance and speech evaluation skills. Build skill in communication technology trend use for the presentation and production of public presentations.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 30173 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better. Examination of contrasting models and standards of communication ethics. Students apply standards to specific problem situations in politics, advertising, writing, and interpersonal communication in making reasoned and informed personal judgments concerning the ethics of public and private communication.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better;

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better. This course is designed to investigate the nature of family communication patterns and the extent to which different communication activities contribute to, and change, familial identity. Students will explore complex definitions of family, family interaction from different theoretical lenses, the role of family rituals,narratives, and storytelling in constructing family identity, and the role of family power, conflict, and stress on family interaction.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better;

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better.. Understanding the role of speech communication in the leadership process. Development of practical leadership communication skills and consideration of communication behavior demonstrated by leaders.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better..

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM 30163. This course is a seminar on the dark sides of organizational communication and behavior. Students will examine critical perspectives in organizational communication and discuss readings and case studies in organizational ethics.
courses.prereqText: COMM 30163.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better; MATH 10043 or INSC 20153 with a C- or better. Explores fundamental principles of communication research. Students will develop as critical consumers of communication research and will learn to design, conduct, analyze, and report individual research projects. Students cannot receive credit for both COMM 30283 and COMM 40283.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better;

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better. Explores history, theory, and research related to interpersonal uses of communication technology. Students will critically examine current forms of mediated interpersonal communication in light of the history of communication technology. Students cannot receive credit for both COMM 30233 and COMM 40313.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better. To increase understanding of the multiple ways that food communication occurs. Students will critically analyze how food functions symbolically as a communicative practice by which we create, manage, and share meanings with others. Emphasis on how the various relationships between communication and food negotiate our identities, cultures, and environments. Patterns of communicative food practices--and how those are influenced by social, economic, historical, and cultural contexts--are also examined.
courses.prereqText: COMM majors/minors only, or permission of department; COMM 10123 or COMM 10163 with a C- or better; COMM 30163 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisites: COMM 20113. This advanced seminar is designed to provide an introduction to the various messages and message strategies that fall within the purview of the dark side of interpersonal communication. Students will examine a variety of interpersonal communication behaviors that problematize that is considered ethical, moral, and/or functional in healthy relationships, including jealousy, envy, revenge, conversational dilemmas, fatal attractions, deception, infidelity, and abuse, among others.
courses.prereqText: COMM 20113.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.description: Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing. Specialized work in student's area of concentration. 1-6 semester hours, 3 hours maximum per semester.
courses.prereqText: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: The Computer Science Experience introduces first-year students to the discipline, culture, and professional pathways of computer science. Students explore major subfields of computing¿including cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, machine learning, large language models, software engineering, operating systems, and databases¿while developing essential academic, professional, and community-building skills. The course emphasizes identity formation, ethical responsibility, industry awareness, and long-term academic planning within the Computer Science, Computer Information Technology, and Data Science programs.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Introduction to computers, problem solving, algorithm design, and programming techniques. Includes what a computer is and is not, problem organization, data representation, and how to utilize the computer to solve problems. Numerical and non-numerical problems are solved in a high-level programming language. Students are expected to have a mathematical background equivalent to college algebra or two years of high school algebra.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Topics may vary each time it is offered.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Introduction to computer programming and to problem solving techniques using computer programs with applications in engineering and the physical sciences. Students are expected to have a mathematical background equivalent to college algebra or two years of high school algebra.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: This course will introduce Python data structures and ways to manipulate data. Students will design, implement, and test Python programs. This course will also give the students a working knowledge of how to use Python to perform data analysis.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 10403 with a C- or better. A study of program design, development and programming techniques. Structured programming with problems selected from list processing, string processing, and file manipulation.
courses.prereqText: COSC 10403 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 20203 with a C- or better. Prerequisite or Corequisite: MATH 20123 with a C- or better. Basic concepts of data. Linear lists, strings, and arrays. Representation of trees and graphs. Storage systems and structures. Symbol tables and searching techniques, sorting techniques. Formal specification of data structures and data structures in programming languages.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20203 with a C- or better. Prerequisite or Corequisite: MATH 20123 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Courses dealing with a particular area of investigation in computer science. The topics will be changed from semester to semester and the course may be repeated when the topic is different. (1 - 3 semester hours.)

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: CITE 30103 with a C- or better. Study of the technology, architecture, and software used by systems of network-connected computers. Topics include data transmission, local area network architectures, network protocols, internetworking, distributed systems, security, and network applications such as email, WWW, and FTP. Students will develop programs that run concurrently on multiple computers.
courses.prereqText: CITE 30103 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123 with a C- or better in both. Essential elements of the data science lifecycle from theory to practice. Introduces fundamental skills to prepare for advanced study in data science. Methodologies and several open source tools used in solving data science problems are studied. (Cross-listed as COSC/MATH 30103.)
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123 with a C- or better in both.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: CITE 30103 and COSC 20803 and MATH 20123; both with a C- or better. Topics include a review of machine representation of data, machine language, systems programming, memory hierarchy, linking, exceptional control flow, system-level I/O, network programming, and concurrent programming.
courses.prereqText: CITE 30103 and COSC 20803 and MATH 20123; both with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: COSC Prerequisites: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123, or, ENGR prerequisites: ENGR 30444; all with a C- or better. Treatment of sequential and combinatorial circuits including flip-flops, multiplexers, decoders, adders, registers, counters. Design of functional components, of a computer including memory, ALU, control unit, busses. The tradeoffs of alternative architectural features such as word size, instruction sets, addressing modes. (Crosslisted as COSC 30253/ENGR 30573.)
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123, or, ENGR prerequisites: ENGR 30444; all with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123; both with C- or better. A study and comparison of the concepts and constructs of major programming language paradigms. Topics include programming language syntax, names, scopes, and bindings, semantic analysis, control flow, and data types. In addition, the course includes learning ANTLR to write parsers, and studying Scala, a functional programming language.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123; both with C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 20203. An overview of the UNIX operating system focused on command-line and server interfaces. An introduction to the C/C++ programming language, UNIX commands, shell programming, process management, memory management, I/O, network communication, and systems programming in C/C++ with low-level kernel calls.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20203.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 20803, and MATH 20123. All prerequisites need to be C- or better. Introduction to the design, implementation, and use of relational database systems. Topics include entity-relationship modeling, relational algebra, normalization, SQL, external data structures, query optimization, non-relational models, and applications.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803, and MATH 20123. All prerequisites need to be C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 20803. Discrete event simulation programming and analysis techniques for simulation experiments. Includes experimental sampling and model development in a special purpose simulation language.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 30203 with a C- or better. Introduction to basic data communications concepts, including hardware and software aspects of protocols, asynchronous and synchronous communication, network configurations, and error detection. This course includes the study of both local area networks and long haul networks, the 7 layer ISO network model, the architecture of networks, and network communication protocols. Local and wide area networks including the internet and world wide web will be discussed.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30203 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30203 or CITE 30103; all with a C- or better. This course will cover the fundamental principles, architectures, and standards of modern wireless communications systems, as well as specific applications and uses of these systems.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30203 or CITE 30103; all with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30403 with a C- or better. The course introduces Android app development using Kotlin. This is a project-based course with the focus on developing simple to moderately complex Android apps. Along the way, students will learn the important concepts of Kotlin programming as well as how to implement key Android features.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30403 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: MATH 20123, and COSC 30203 or CITE 30103; all with a C- or better. This course will cover the fundamental principles and techniques in computer systems and network security. Key topics include cryptographic systems, security standards, protocols, tools and applications.
courses.prereqText: MATH 20123, and COSC 30203 or CITE 30103; all with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30253 and a knowledge of linear algebra MATH 30224. A basic course in graphics systems. Considers the equations of lines, planes, and surfaces; hidden line algorithms; rotations, scaling, and cutaway transformations; 3-D images and the use of shading and perspective; animation; and color graphics.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30253 and a knowledge of linear algebra MATH 30224.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30203 with a C- or better, COSC 30253 with a C- or better. Introduction to operating systems concepts, principles, and design. Topics include: processes and threads, CPU scheduling, mutual exclusion and synchronization, deadlock, memory management, file systems, security and protection, networking, and distributed systems. Selected existing operating systems are discussed, compared, and contrasted.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30203 with a C- or better, COSC 30253 with a C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: CITE 30103 with a C- or better and completed at least 18 hours in Major. An introductory course on Cloud Computing, with special emphasis on AWS Cloud Foundations curriculum. The course will provide a detailed overview and help students get an overall understanding of cloud computing concepts. More specifically, students will get hands-on exposure to the AWS cloud, including but not limited to the AWS core services, security, architecture, pricing, and support.
courses.prereqText: CITE 30103 with a C- or better and completed at least 18 hours in Major.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 30253. Introduction to the design of microprocessor based digital systems including the study of processor control signals, address decoding and memory interfacing, interfacing to serial and parallel ports, A/D conversion, and interrupt processing. Features of state-of-the-art microprocessors will be discussed. Both hardware and software assignments will be required. (Crosslisted as COSC 30353/ENGR 30583.)
courses.prereqText: COSC 30253.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: MATH 10524 and COSC 10403 or 10503, and either COSC 20803 or ENGR 40574. The study and practice of the principles, the algorithms and the techniques of image processing such as editing, analysis, segmentation, recognition and classification. Students will use Java to implement and test various image processing algorithms.
courses.prereqText: MATH 10524 and COSC 10403 or 10503, and either COSC 20803 or ENGR 40574.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 20803, Corequisite MATH 30123; all with C- or better, and a knowledge of probability and statistics. This course covers basic approaches for designing and analyzing for a variety of problems. Algorithm design techniques such as divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming will be covered. Other topics include worst, best, and average case analysis, graph algorithms, string matching, and complexity.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803, Corequisite MATH 30123; all with C- or better, and a knowledge of probability and statistics.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30403 with C- or better. This course teaches how to write code of high quality by providing an in-depth coverage of object-oriented programming principles and techniques. Topics include but not limited to fundamental object-oriented programming concepts, software design principles (SOLID), Gang of Four (GoF) design patterns, coding standards, refactoring. Each topic will be explained by using diagrammatic notations Unified Modeling Language (UML) and numerous real-world code demos.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30403 with C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 40403 and MATH 20123, all with grade C- or above. Introduction to knowledge representation and methods for intelligent search, planning, and learning. Fundamental topics include uninformed and informed search, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction problems, logical agents, knowledge representation, reinforcement learning, expert systems, and a bit of machine learning.
courses.prereqText: COSC 40403 and MATH 20123, all with grade C- or above.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 30203, COSC 30403, and MATH 30123. Formal description of algorithmic languages, such as Pascal, and the techniques used in writing compilers for such. Topics include syntax, semantics, storage allocation, code generation, error handling and diagnostics, code optimization, etc. Includes the definition and writing of a compiler for a simple programming language.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30203, COSC 30403, and MATH 30123.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 40203. An introduction to hardware and software topics in high performance and parallel computing. Students will be introduced to a variety of high performance and parallel computing paradigms including message passing, threading models, and shared-memory programming techniques. Topics include motivation and history, parallel architectures, parallel algorithm design, and parallel performance analysis.
courses.prereqText: COSC 40203.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Advanced topics of current interest in computer hardware, such as computer design, computer networks, advanced computer graphics. Students will study current literature. May be repeated for credit when topic changes.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Advanced topics of current interest in computer software, such as natural language programming, advanced operating systems, advanced compiler design, file structures, advanced database. Students will study current literature. May be repeated for credit when topic changes.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 30603 or concurrent, senior standing in COSC or CITE or DASC (24 hours in the major.) All prerequisites need to be C- or better. Stages of the software development life cycle (requirements analysis, specification, design, implementation, testing), evolution, and quality assurance are covered. Classical and alternative process models are described. Project management issues, professional responsibilities, and ethics of the profession are discussed. This course includes team projects.
courses.prereqText: COSC 30603 or concurrent, senior standing in COSC or CITE or DASC (24 hours in the major.) All prerequisites need to be C- or better.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSC 40943 with a C- or better. Senior computer science majors are required to demonstrate their mastery of several computer science topics and their ability to communicate the results of their efforts to others. They are required to identify and analyze a computer science problem, develop and implement a workable solution to the problem, and then document the results of their efforts.
courses.prereqText: COSC 40943 with a C- or better. Senior computer science majors are required to demonstrate their mastery of several computer science topics and their ability to communicate the results of their efforts to others.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 40203 - Operating Systems with C- or better, or permission, or graduate standing. An introduction to hardware and software topics in high performance and parallel computing.Students will be introduced to a variety of high performance and parallel computing paradigms including message passing, threading models, and shared-memory programming techniques. Topics include motivation and history, parallel architectures, parallel algorithm design, and parallel performance analysis.
courses.prereqText: COSC 40203 - Operating Systems with C- or better, or permission, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123 with a C- or better in both, or graduate standing. This course presents, in detail, the following advanced foundational concepts of data mining: similarity and dissimilarity measures, data preprocessing, classification and cluster analysis, frequent pattern mining, anomaly detection, time series mining, and spatial/spatio-temporal data mining. The lectures will provide students with a sufficient foundation to carry out their own projects that explore the challenges of mining unconventional data (e.g., image, time-series, or spatio-temporal data) from publicly available data repositories.
courses.prereqText: COSC 20803 and MATH 20123 with a C- or better in both, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC/MATH 30103 and MATH 30224; MATH 10043 or MATH 30853 (co-requisite); all with a C- or better, or graduate standing. Open to both undergraduate and graduate students. Students will study the principles and practices of machine learning. Specifically, regression and classification will be studied to obtain and analyze patterns in datasets. To facilitate exploratory data analysis, students will also study data preprocessing techniques and data visualization practices.
courses.prereqText: COSC/MATH 30103 and MATH 30224; MATH 10043 or MATH 30853 (co-requisite); all with a C- or better, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisites: COSC/MATH 30103 and MATH 30224; MATH 10043 or MATH 30853 (may be taken concurrently); all with a C- or better, or graduate standing. Open to both undergraduate and graduate students. This course introduces fundamental knowledge of deep learning algorithms, practical skills to build, train and tune a deep artificial neural network with applications such as computer vision, and natural language processing. Topics include but not limited to fully connected neural networks, convolutional networks, recurrent networks, attention-based and transformer-based networks, generative adversarial networks, and multimodal learning.
courses.prereqText: COSC/MATH 30103 and MATH 30224; MATH 10043 or MATH 30853 (may be taken concurrently); all with a C- or better, or graduate standing.

courses.subject: COSC
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. (1-6 semester hours).
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Transfer work.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Survey of disorders of articulation, language, stuttering, voice and hearing.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: An introductory course in signing expressively and understanding basic sign language, receptively. Included is basic information on hearing loss and its effects on children and adults. Recommended for students majoring in special education and service-oriented fields as well as those who are interested in learning sign language.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: An introduction to acoustic and physiological aspects of the speech and hearing mechanisms.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Required of all majors and elective to others. Emphasis on speech perception and sound discrimination. Intensive work in transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 10343 with a grade of C or higher or permission of instructor. Further development and refinement of receptive and expressive skills in Signed English and American Sign Language. Emphasis on vocabulary development for classroom use, ability to sign fluently, and the psycho-social aspects of deafness, including the sociolinguistics of sign language and Deaf Culture.
courses.prereqText: COSD 10343 with a grade of C or higher or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 10303 with a grade of C or better. This course will focus on identifying the fundamental concepts related to scientific inquiry in communication sciences and disorders to allow students to become critical readers of peer-reviewed journal articles. The course will consider identification of research literature relevant to a specific topic or disorder, basic concepts involved in the formulation of research questions and methodology, and levels of research evidence available to audiologists and speech language pathologists.
courses.prereqText: COSD 10303 with a grade of C or better.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: SPPA or DHHS major or minor, or permission of instructor. Structure and function of the normal mechanisms required for speech and hearing.
courses.prereqText: SPPA or DHHS major or minor, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing and membership in the Honors Program. Under the guidance and supervision of a faculty member, current issues in communication sciences and disorders are explored.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing and membership in the Honors Program.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: An overview of normal acquisition and development of language in children from infancy through adolescence for non majors.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisites: SPPA major, COSD 10303 and 20333, with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses or permission of instructor. Basic principles of diagnosis and treatment for individuals with developmental or functional speech sound disorders of articulation.
courses.prereqText: SPPA major, COSD 10303 and 20333, with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: SPPA or DHHS major or permission of instructor. Normal acquisition and development of language in children from infancy through adolescence.
courses.prereqText: SPPA or DHHS major or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 30363 with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses. Overview of management and rehabilitation of persons with hearing loss. Focus on amplification, cochlear implants, assistive devices, speech training, speech reading, auditory training and language development.
courses.prereqText: COSD 30363 with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Curriculum materials and teaching methods for meeting specialized needs of DHH children, in the learning of reading and developing concepts and relationships in arithmetic and science.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 20503 with a grade of C or higher. Basic audiometric techniques and interpretation of audiograms as related to problems of communication of persons with hearing loss.
courses.prereqText: COSD 20503 with a grade of C or higher.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: SPPA major or permission of instructor. COSD 30334 with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of a least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses. Introduction to the causes, characteristics, assessment and treatment of children with language disorders.
courses.prereqText: SPPA major or permission of instructor. COSD 30334 with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of a least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: Basic Sign Language and Intermediate Sign Language or permission of the instructor to complete a proficiency assessment to determine sign language skills. In this course, students will strengthen their expressive fluency and comprehension of American Sign Language (ASL) including advanced study of grammatical structure and signing technique. Students will deepen their knowledge of Deaf culture and increase their ability to support Deaf and Hard of Hearing individuals in society.
courses.prereqText: Basic Sign Language and Intermediate Sign Language or permission of the instructor to complete a proficiency assessment to determine sign language skills.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 30334 with a grade of C or higher, or permission of instructor. This is the first of two courses devoted to the study of language development of Deaf/Hard of Hearing (DHH) students. It will address the early intervention needs of young DHH infants and their parents as well as DDH students in lower primary grades.
courses.prereqText: COSD 30334 with a grade of C or higher, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 10303, 20333, and 30334, with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses or permission of instructor. Principles and procedures in the assessment and treatment of communication disorders.
courses.prereqText: COSD 10303, 20333, and 30334, with a grade of C or higher in all COSD coursework, cumulative GPA of at least 3.00, and a cumulative 3.00 GPA in COSD courses or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Independent study of specially designed topics not addressed in regular course offerings. 1-6 hours, 3 hours maximum per semester.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: COSD
courses.description: Prerequisite: COSD 30003, with a grade of C or higher, senior standing, and membership in the Honors Program. The completion of a research project related to a current issue in normal and/or disordered communication.
courses.prereqText: COSD 30003, with a grade of C or higher, senior standing, and membership in the Honors Program. The completion of a research project related to a current issue in normal and/or disordered communication.
