courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: FTDM 30003. Senior standing and membership in the Honors Program. A supervised research experience and a thesis that is usually based on the subject matter studied in 30003. This course is offered only as a tutorial; arrangements must be made with an instructor prior to enrollment.
courses.prereqText: FTDM 30003. Senior standing and membership in the Honors Program.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 10153 and 30153. Building on the knowledge acquired in Dramatic Style and Structure, students will develop, create, write and revise original screenplays. Conducted as a workshop, all scripts are read aloud and critiqued by the class with the ultimate goal of developing a script suitable for production.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 10153 and 30153.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 20313; FTDM majors only. This course will focus on a particular production-related area not covered elsewhere in the curriculum. It provides a chance for students to pursue in-depth study in such areas as music, sound design, cinematography, post-production, production management, writing, directing, and others. Up to 6 semester hours, maximum of 3 hours per semester.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 20313; FTDM majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20523. An examination of legal and financial issues related to film and television production. Topics covered may include employment contracts, permits and releases, music licensing, guilds and unions, financing, and production and distribution revenues and expenses. Counts as industry credit.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20523.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 20313. Through an examination of documentary styles and journalistic techniques, students will produce, write, direct, and edit a documentary.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 20313.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. Using a variety of theoretical and critical approaches, students will examine limited topics such as films produced within a particular time period, films by specific directors, or film which are unified by theme or style. (6 hours maximum; 3 hours per semester).
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20523. Structural and content regulation of the media industries. Court cases bearing on media industries. Introduction to legal research and writing.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20523.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20523; FTDM and Business of Entertainment Media majors only. An in-depth examination of selected issues relating to media industry business practices. (6 semester hours maximum; 3 hours per semester)
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20523; FTDM and Business of Entertainment Media majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 C or higher grade in FTDM 20523; FTDM, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors only. The organization and administration of broadcast, cable and film operations. Management techniques and strategies, including forecasting, planning, statistical and financial analysis, and interpersonal communication.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher grade in FTDM 20523; FTDM, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors only. The organization and administration of broadcast, cable and film operations.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. An in-depth analysis or selected television genres and industry practices from a variety of critical and theoretical perspectives. (6 semester hours maximum; 3 hours per semester)
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. In this course, students will study the production, circulation, and styles of international films. (6 semester hours maximum; 3 hours per semester)
courses.prereqText: A C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. This course will examine noteworthy topics pertaining to popular culture as represented/communicated in two or more types of media.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: This course explores how popular music functions as a significant media industry and source of culture in contemporary society and explores the technology that made music recording and distribution possible.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. Students in this course will examine current trends in various media forms, looking at the ways texts, the industry, and audiences intersect in contemporary practice. May be repeated for credit under different topics. (6 semester hours maximum; 3 hours per semester.)
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: A 2.0 "C" or higher grade in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103. Survey of classical and contemporary film theories.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher grade in FTDM 20583 or FTDM 30103.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: An overview of contemporary media in Great Britain, focusing on the press, television, and cinema. Taught only in London.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing; a 2.0 C grade or higher in FTDM 10143 and 10153. A conference course designed to give an individual student opportunities for additional specialized work in his or her area of concentration. Prerequisites may vary for different sections of this course. 1-6 semester hours
courses.prereqText: Junior standing; a 2.0 C grade or higher in FTDM 10143 and 10153.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: By permission only. FTDM, Cinema and Media Studies, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors only. Students must be in last semester of senior year. A review and synthesis of material covered in the FTDM, Cinema and Media Studies, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors. This course is required for FTDM, Cinema and Media Studies, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors; the minimum acceptable grade is a 2.0 "C." (1 semester hour)
courses.prereqText: By permission only. FTDM, Cinema and Media Studies, Sports Broadcasting and Business of Entertainment Media majors only. Students must be in last semester of senior year.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21113. This course is designed to give students an opportunity to put into practice play-by-play, color analyst, and sideline reporting skills that were taught in prior classes. The class gives students a chance to put pre-production, background research and interview skills into practice by calling games for television and radio broadcasts.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21113.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21213. This course examines the principles and techniques of non-linear editing for use in sports. Students will spend time on the department's non-linear editing systems. The course will explore the theory and practice of sports editing, and use examples ranging from long form documentaries to sports highlight shows.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21213.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 21213; Sports broadcasting majors only. Students in the course will explore the theory and practice documentary production for the sports broadcasting industry. Students will examine different forms of documentary storytelling, ranging from Ken Burn's Baseball to NFL films. Students will also research and create documentaries that may be aired.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20213 or 21213; Sports broadcasting majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 21113 or permission of instructor. An in-depth examination of selected issues relating to the sports media industry. (6 semester hours maximum; 3 hours per semester)
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 "C" or higher in FTDM 21113 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21213 and 21713; Sports Broadcasting majors only. This course will focus on a particular sports production-related area not covered elsewhere in the curriculum. It provides an opportunity for students to pursue in-depth study in specific topics, practices, and issues related to sports production. 6 semester hours maximum, as topics vary; limit to 3 hours per semester.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21213 and 21713; Sports Broadcasting majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21113 and 20523; Sports Broadcasting majors only. This course will examine legal issues, rights fees, and problems associated with producing an event overseas. Students will examine what is needed to produce sports events internationally, such as the Olympics, World Cup Soccer, Skiing, Sailing, and Golf, and how television networks overcome the problems associated with international broadcasting.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 21113 and 20523; Sports Broadcasting majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20523; FTDM majors only. An advanced exploration of film and video producing, with an examination of techniques used by producers and financial, budgeting, and legal issues facing today's producers. All phases of the producing process will be examined, from acquiring the property, to pre-production, principal photography and post-production, as well as distribution.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C or higher in FTDM 20523; FTDM majors only.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: Preference is given to juniors and seniors. Permission of instructor and/or department chair. This course develops the student's ability to analyze, establish and execute external and internal communication goals, strategies and tactics for a client. Students use research, discussion, peer evaluation and instructor assessment to produce creative and effective solutions to marketing and promotion challenges. The course places students in the role of communication professionals working with the Bob Schieffer College of Communication and other TCU academic units and organizations as their clients.
courses.prereqText: Preference is given to juniors and seniors. Permission of instructor and/or department chair.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: A 2.0 C grade or higher in FTDM 20583 or 30103; Cinema and Media Studies majors only. A capstone course in which Cinema and Media studies majors produce a comprehensive research project that utilizes relevant film, media, and/or cultural theories to guide the process of in-depth media analysis.
courses.prereqText: A 2.0 C grade or higher in FTDM 20583 or 30103; Cinema and Media Studies majors only. A capstone course in which Cinema and Media studies majors produce a comprehensive research project that utilizes relevant film, media, and/or cultural theories to guide the process of in-depth media analysis.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisites: Senior or graduate standing. Seminar in radio, television, and film. 3-6 semester hours; maximum 3 semester hours per semester.
courses.prereqText: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.subject: FTDM
courses.description: Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing. A conference course designed to give an individual student opportunities for additional specialized work in his or her area of concentration. (1-6 semester hours)
courses.prereqText: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: General Transfer Credit-SSC credit.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: A survey of the world's primary regions and the human and physical geography that shape them. Interactions between natural environment, cultural geography, geopolitics, history, land use, and economic geography are highlighted.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course examines the processes that shape our environment and the resulting patterns of landforms, biomes, climates, and water resources. Students will analyze interactions among dynamic systems in the lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere using basic scientific principles and methods, with an emphasis on spatial relationships. Students will also consider the relationship between humans and the environment, including the distribution of resources and adaptation to and modification of environments. The course will be lecture with integrated lab.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course introduces students to the field of urban studies in global context. Major urban themes covered in the class include urban form; neighborhood change; real estate; environmental management; race and immigration; suburbanization; migration and slums; and cities within the global economy. These themes are explored through case studies of major cities around the world.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Transfer work with TCUCC-SSC credit.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: GEOG Transfer Credit - SSC only

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Transfer work with TCUCC-SSC credit.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Geography transfer credit with SSC credit only.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: The systematic subdivisions of human geography are surveyed, including urban, cultural, political, economic, historical, agricultural, and population geography. Within each subdiscipline, applications of geographic concepts and processes are emphasized.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. For geography majors who are Honors students as well as other students with overall GPAs at or above 3.5, who are willing to join the Honors College. Permission by a geography faculty member required. Directed study course for students who intend to complete a Seniors Honors Thesis research paper or equivalent creative project in a selected area of geography.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor. For geography majors who are Honors students as well as other students with overall GPAs at or above 3.5, who are willing to join the Honors College. Permission by a geography faculty member required.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS), with a focus on both the conceptual foundations and applications of GIS software. Topics covered include spatial data models; cartographic design; coordinate systems and map projections; address geocoding and GPS data; spatial analysis; Internet GIS applications; and GIS modeling. Laboratory assignments give students experience using GIS in thematic areas such as demographic analysis, market research, and urban environmental change.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Data literacy is essential to success in many professional fields. In this course, students will gain experience acquiring, manipulating, and analyzing data; and will learn how to effectively communicate their findings with static and interactive visualizations. Students will learn how to work with data using the Python programming language, one of the most popular tools for performing data analysis.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course is an introduction to Geographic Information Systems (GIS), with a focus on the use of GIS for applications that are important for real estate professionals. No prior knowledge of GIS is assumed for this course, although students should have some facility with basic mathematics, statistics, and spreadsheet programs. Students will develop familiarity with leading GIS software programs and build experience managing property-related databases, conductinglocational analysis, site-suitability analyses, mapping market trends, risk-assessment, and utilizing GIS to navigate permitting, zoning, and other regulatory processes.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: An analysis of the human and physical geography of a specific region. Examples of regions include Texas, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Eastern Europe. Regional characteristics investigated may include economic, political, historical, and cultural components as well as topography, climate, and natural resources. May be repeated for credit provided the specified region changes.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: An exploration of the human and physical geography of the United States. Areas of the country, such as the Pacific Northwest and New England, will be surveyed, analyzing the physical, historic, cultural, and economic characteristics that embody their unique regional identities.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: An exploration of the human and physical geography of Latin America. This course analyzes Latin America from a geographical perspective and addresses topics such as landforms, climate, environmental hazards, indigenous peoples, culture, ethnicity, religion, agriculture, political geography, population, cities, and economic production.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: An exploration of the human and physical geography of Western Europe. Countries and regions of the realm will be surveyed, analyzing their economic, political, language and religious characteristics as well as topography, climate, and natural resources. Themes may include the impact of population trends, environmental problems, trade and economic development, interactions between ethnic groups, and geopolitical change.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Concepts, principles, patterns, and processes associated with a specific subdiscipline in geography. Examples of topics include Economic Geography, Geopolitics, Medical Geography, and Physical Geography. May be repeated for credit provided the specified subdiscipline changes.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Urban Geography is the geographical study of cities. Examples of topics include: urban ecosystems; the role of physical geography in the origins and growth of cities; theoretical models of urban size, location, and land use structure; the internal geography of urban economic and social activity; and international and historical variation in the form, functions, and degree of urbanization.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Cultural Geography is the study of human culture from the perspectives of its five geographic themes: culture region, diffusion and migration, cultural ecology, cultural landscape, and cultural integration. Each theme is applied to a variety of topics, which may include religion, language, cultural conflict, folk culture, popular culture, and demography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: The Geography of Religion is the study of religion from the spatial perspective, utilizing the five themes of cultural geography: region, diffusion, culture-environment interaction, landscapes, and integration. Our most important topics cover the relationship between physical geography and religion, and from this context we will analyze religions, past and present.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Problem-solving by application of geographic concepts, methodologies, and techniques. Examples are drawn from physical and human geography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: In this course, students engage with contemporary debates around world population growth and change. Course topics include demographic data and methods; the history and future of world population growth; fertility and population control in the developing world; aging in the developed world; global trends in mortality and disease; internal migration and immigration; and population, climate change, and environmental sustainability.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Economic Geography is the study of how elements within the economy are spatially arranged, as well as the ways that space, place and spatial scales shape economic activities in different parts of the world. Through a series of readings, discussions, and research assignments, this course examines the distribution of economic activities on the earth's surface; market resource and transportation factors in location theory, and the role of state, market and civil society's agents in management of the economy. Students are further introduced to Geographic Information Systems (GIS) through content-focused lab assignments, though no previous experience with GIS is required for this course.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course uses beer (and wine) as a lens to examine the intersections of historical, environmental, cultural, legal, and economic geography. Students are introduced to the major systematic fields of Geographic inquiry: Historical Geography, Cultural Geography, Economic Geography, etc through focused lessons examining the role of beer production in the establishment of historical civilizations, how climate change affects barley and hop production, and the locational characteristics required for a brewery or brewpub to be successful.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Since mass tourism's emergence in the late 19th century, tourism has played an increasingly significant role in shaping and reshaping the geographies of places around the world. This course pays specific attention to the ways in which places develop into tourist destinations, as well as the social, environmental, economic, and political ramifications of that development.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course covers the study of sport through the lens of social science. It introduces students to social scientific theory and analytic methods in the context of historical and contemporary sports topics. Course topics include sports and cultural geography; sports and nationalism; race, gender, politics, and sports; sports business and economics; and sports analytics.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course number will be used for trial runs of upper-division environmentally-focused Geography courses. All the classes will develop student's understanding of Environmental Geography and Human-Environment Interactions. May be repeated for credit as course topic changes.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course examines relationships between people and the environment from multiple perspectives, providing a context for thinking about the causes and consequences of environmental change and their spatial patterns around the world. Of particular interest are the cultural, ethical, economic, technological, and population considerations that make humans want to use, protect, destroy, or adapt to environmental systems and their components. This course will also address the function of specific environmental systems themselves, including how they influence and respond to human actions.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: In this course, we will examine the spatial dimensions of highly contentious issues surrounding nuclear technologies, including power generation, weapons, and medicine. We will approach each of these issues through the perspectives offered by several subdisciplines within Geography, especially Environmental, Economic, Political, and Cultural Geography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course introduces students to urban economic development (UED) policy and strategy in the United States. In particular, students are encouraged to respectfully and thoughtfully address the assumptions and biases embedded in urban economic development policy. For example, final papers will examine the presence or lack thereof of equity and sustainability aims in economic development initiatives, and analyze UED projects that respond to the specific challenges of rising inequality and climate change that threaten UED activity in the US and worldwide.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Topical studies in Geography.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30003 or permission of instructor. A senior Honors Thesis research paper or equivalent creative project, under faculty direction, in a selected area of geography.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30003 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: An intensive field study in the regional and systematic geography of a selected area. Examples include France, Central America, and the American West. May be repeated for credit provided the selected area changes.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30313 or equivalent training with instructor's approval. This course is only open to Geography majors. The purpose of this course is to supplement the internship experience of geography majors through written reflection, periodic conversation with a supervising professor, and exploration of connections between concepts in GIS and practices of GIS in different disciplines. Students may take this course a maximum of two times to earn up to 6 total credit hours. A maximum of 3 credit hours can be applied towards the Geography major. The remaining credit hours can be applied to the student's overall degree as general elective credits.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30313 or equivalent training with instructor's approval.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30313 or with instructor permission. This course number will be used for trial runs of upper-division technically-focused Geography courses. All the classes will develop student's technical mapping and analysis skills using Geographic Information Systems software and/or statistical programs such as R or Python. May be repeated for credit provided the technical and/or topical focus changes.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30313 or with instructor permission.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30313, or instructor consent. In this course, students gain experience with advanced applications of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software. Topics covered include GIS modeling; web GIS applications and distributed GIS services; open-source GIS; developing geoprocessing scripts using the Python programming language; and the current state of the GIS profession. Students will also complete a semester-long course project in which they apply GIS techniques to a topic of their interest.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30313, or instructor consent.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30313; another introductory GIS course; or instructor consent. This advanced GIS course gives students experience applying GIS to solve real-world urban and business problems. Topics covered include demographic analysis; remote sensing of urban areas; network analysis; 3D urban modeling; spatial statistics; time and GIS; geodemographic classification; market area analysis; and web GIS services. Students will also complete a semester-long group project that applies GIS to assist an organization or business in the Fort Worth area.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30313; another introductory GIS course; or instructor consent.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOG 30313 or with instructor permission. Cartography refers to the art and science of map-making. Contemporary cartography is primarily accomplished using digital technologies including Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Mapping is crucial to exploring and understanding distributions of geographic phenomena. It is also an important phase of many database-intensive analyses, because a map is often the best way to visualize results and show them to others. Our emphases in this course will be on designing and producing both thematic and reference maps at multiple scales using symbols and visual hierarchies that allow the content of the maps to be effectively communicated and presented in aesthetically-pleasing and/or engaging ways. Topics covered include: significant eras in cartographic design, key historical and contemporary cartographers, map projections, symbolizing quantitative data, use of space, layout, compilation, verbal content, and the use of computer technology in the design and production of maps.
courses.prereqText: GEOG 30313 or with instructor permission.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a focus on large language models (LLMs) and their applications in Geography. Students will gain foundational knowledge in AI and deep learning, develop skills in prompt engineering, and apply AI tools to solve real-world problems, particularly in geographic analysis and spatial data interpretation. The course emphasizes hands-on experience, ethical considerations, and culminates in a final project where students integrate AI concepts to design their own applications with a geographic focus.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.description: Supervised reading, research, and preparation of a substantial paper focused on a specific regional analysis or topical subdiscipline of geography. Regional characteristics investigated may include economic, political, historical, and cultural components as well as topography, climate, and natural resources. Examples of topics include advanced studies in Urban Geography, Cultural Geography, Geopolitics, and Historical Geography.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit-NSC credit.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Two hours lecture and two hours of laboratory per week. A study of the physical environment of the planet Earth, its makeup, the processes that mold its surface features and an introduction to the resources that it provides.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Two hours of lecture and two hours of laboratory per week. This course provides an overview of the development of the physical Earth over the span of Geologic time from Earth¿s inception to the modern day. The course equally details the co-evolution of life on Earth from the time of the first evidence of life to the modern day. The course also discusses the scientific paradigms and tools used to derive this co-development of Earth and life using evidence from the rock record.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Freshman Seminar in Geology.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Transfer work with NSC and GA credit.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113 should be completed or in progress. All students who are new geology majors must take this course. All new geology majors will be introduced to the Geology Faculty, their areas of research and teaching, and the expectations of the Faculty. Majors will also be introduced to the department, its facilities, expectations for field trips and work, and information on careers and areas of the geosciences.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 should be completed or in progress. All students who are new geology majors must take this course. All new geology majors will be introduced to the Geology Faculty, their areas of research and teaching, and the expectations of the Faculty.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Introductory level course, with integrated lecture and laboratory experience, focusing on Earth as a system of interacting spheres. The course will cover interactions between Earth's biosphere (including people), geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and consequences for current and future population, life expectancy, food, climate, water availability and water quality. Emphasis is placed on how basic scientific knowledge and readily available data can be used in understanding Earth Systems.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 10113. Three hours lecture per week. For the non-science major. Places society's relationship to geological phenomena within a scientific framework. Evaluates the apparent immutability of the earth. Field trip required.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Reading assignments and discussions on topics of great importance in geology.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: This three-credit hour lecture course will examine the connections between science and modern society. This will be accomplished by investing the role of science (particularly geoscience) in education and communication, and how scientific misconceptions influence public perception and understanding of modern socioscientific issues such as dwindling freshwater resources and climate change.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: 'C-' or better in GEOL 10113 and GEOL 20113. This 2.0 credit hour course is designed to introduce students to the field of geoscience education. This course will cover the nature of geoscience education, and the need for geoscience education specialists. Specifically, students will define geoscience education within the context of other science disciplines, examine how geoscientists think about learning, how students learn in geoscience classrooms, and investigate the role of geoscience education toward addressing modern socioscientific issues.
courses.prereqText: 'C-' or better in GEOL 10113 and GEOL 20113.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Introduction to the basic concepts and principles of atmospheric science in a descriptive format; emphasizes the physics responsible for changes in weather and climate complemented with popular treatment. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 30113)

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. Prerequisite: GEOL 10113 or consent of instructor. A broad-based inquiry into dinosaurs, the biological and geological aspects of their world and those who study them. We will approach dinosaurs from many different fields of science in an attempt to reconstruct their world. The course is intended for science and non-science students.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 10113 or equivalent. This first semester of a two semester lab/lecture introduces students to the general principles of earth history. Lab exercises and field trips introduce students to the practical aspects of earth history. Microscope work and field trips are mandatory.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite GEOL 30133 or equivalent. This second semester of a two semester lab/lecture course continues with an in depth look at the details of the geological history of North America and the history of life on earth. Lectures focus on historical detail, while lab exercises and field trips focus on major groups of fossils in the lab and field. Microscope work and field trips are mandatory.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30133 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113, or permission of instructor. Study of dynamic geologic systems and the geology of the North American continent through the study of National Parks and Monuments in the United States. The three hours of lecture per week are designed for science majors and interested non-science majors, who wish to gain in-depth knowledge of processes that actively sculpt and have sculpted our continent through time. Particular emphasis is given to interpretation of visual features of the parks through visual aids. Discussions are encouraged and facilitated by the small class size.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113, or any one of PHYS 10164/10263/10273, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lectures per week. This course will launch you into space with past and present spacecraft missions and bring you back to Earth with meteorite research. Throughout the semester, this course will examine the geology and geologic processes occurring on and within planetary bodies throughout the Solar System. This course is intended for science and non-science majors. (Crosslisted as GEOL/PHYS 30163.)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113, or any one of PHYS 10164/10263/10273, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Three hours lecture per week. The workings of science and scientists considered by examining the emergence of geology as a science in the late 18th and early l9th centuries and its development through the Victorian Age, including the rise and demise of scriptural geology and the impact of geologic thought on social mores and religious beliefs.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite GEOL 10113 and CHEM 10113. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. A composite course consisting of an introduction to crystallography and a study of the common minerals. Credit will not be granted for both GEOL 30213 and ENSC/GEOL 30443. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 30443)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 and CHEM 10113.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 30213. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. A basic course in the origin and identification of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. Field trip required.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30213.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor. Field seminar on the megascopic aspects of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks. Description and interpretation of features seen at scales between that of the individual outcrop and that of an entire basin.
courses.prereqText: Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 20111 or concurrent. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. Principles and techniques of facies analysis, including the description and origin of sedimentary textures and sedimentary structures, and the collection and analysis of paleocurrent data. Field trips required.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 20111 or concurrent.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113 and GEOL 20111. GEOL 20111 may be taken concurrently. Three hours lecture and three hours of laboratory per week. This is an advanced course covering principles of deposition and interpretation of sedimentary rocks, and the fundamental principles of stratigraphy. Field trips required.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 and GEOL 20111. GEOL 20111 may be taken concurrently.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of Geospatial Technologies, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Global Positioning Systems (GPS), cartography, remote sensing, and spatial analysis through a series of hands-on computer-based exercises. Participants will learn how to utilize geospatial technology to address social and environmental issues. This course is designed to be used as a stand-along course to complement other disciplines or as an entry level course into other GIS classes. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 30363.)

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 hours of coursework completed. Two hours of lecture and one three-hour laboratory period per week. This is a field course with potentially lengthy hikes and difficult terrain. Field experience is considered essential for a degree in environmental science or geology and the course offers instruction in fundamental field skills. (Crosslisted as GEOL/ENSC 30403.)
courses.prereqText: Major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 hours of coursework completed.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113, PHYS 10154 or PHYS 20474, GEOL 30213 or 30443. Two hours of lecture and three hours of lab per week. An introductory study of the evolution of plate boundaries focusing on the interconnectedness of plate tectonics, structural geology and earthquakes. Credit will not be given for both GEOL 30423 and 30413.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113, PHYS 10154 or PHYS 20474, GEOL 30213 or 30443.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 10113 and GEOL 30213 or GEOL 30444, or permission of instructor. Two hours of lecture and three hours of lab period per week. An introductory study of deformation of Earth's crust and Plate Tectonic theory.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 and GEOL 30213 or GEOL 30444, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113 or equivalent, and permission of instructor. This course examines the chemical and physical processes involved in producing minerals, soils and rocks on the earth. Students also learn how these materials are used in our society as well as the economic importance and environmental implications of their use. The class combines lecture and laboratory to provide the most complete experience for students. Credit will not be granted forboth GEOL 30213 and ENSC/GEOL 30443. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 30443)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 or equivalent, and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: This is a basic course covering crystallography, recognition, origin, and economic significance of the most important minerals, and origin and identification of igneous and metamorphic rocks. A weekend field trip to the Wichita Mountains in Oklahoma is required and involves some hiking.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 10113 and/or permission of the instructor. Three hours lecture. An introduction to the practical and theoretical aspects of stratigraphy and depositional systems. This course uses practical examples and field- and literature-based projects to familiarize students with the basic theoretical stratigraphic framework in which geology exists. An off-road field trip will be required.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 and/or permission of the instructor.

The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. The student is required to do independent research on a geologic problem, submit a paper and give an oral presentation of the findings. A faculty supervisor will be appointed for each research problem.
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 30423. Designed for science majors who wish to gain in-depth knowledge of advanced structural geology processes by understanding the response of rocks to stress. The course focuses on geomechanical principles such as rock failure/behavior, rock strength, 3D stress and stress polygon, in situ stress, role of pore pressure, stress resolution on planes and reactivation of preexisting mechanical discontinuities. Particular emphasis is given to the determination of rock strength using micro mechanical tools and derivation of various petrophysical constraints from geophysical well logs.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30423.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. Major groups of invertebrate fossils, their morphology, classification, paleoecology, geologic distribution and phylogeny. Field trips required.
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 30143, 30223, 30423. Three hours lecture per week for five weeks. An introduction to techniques of gathering, processing and interpreting seismic data.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 40331 or equivalent. Three hours lecture per week for five weeks. An introduction to the principles of seismic stratigraphy and their application in oil and gas exploration.

courses.subject: GEOL

courses.prereqText: GEOL 30243.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: one year of chemistry, ENSC 10143, or permission of the instructor. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. This course covers the formation, distribution, and classification of soils: major soil properties; field evaluation of soils; the use of soil survey information; and soil hydrology. The emphasis is on the study of soils as products of biophysical processes, and on soil properties of interest to geoscientists and natural resource managers.
courses.prereqText: one year of chemistry, ENSC 10143, or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. The construction and interpretation of geological maps.
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 50423. Petroleum engineering concepts and technology that are needed to find and produce oil and gas are discussed. This course focuses on drilling and production operations for non-engineers. Industry professionals will visit to discuss current technologies for producing hydrocarbon fluids.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 50423.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 30243. This course introduces sequence stratigraphy within the context of all stratigraphy and overviews the history of sequence stratigraphy. It includes an overview of sequence stratigraphy principles and reviews basic fundamental concepts of surface- and facies-based physical stratigraphy. Included are reviews of architectural element analysis, sequence stratigraphy in seismic, borehole expression of sequences and overview of subsurface stratigraphic techniques.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30243.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: ENGR 40223 or GEOL 40423. Oil and gas are essential sources of energy in the modern world. They are found in subsurface reservoirs in many challenging environments. Modern reservoir simulators are computer programs that are designed to model fluid flow in reservoirs. Applied reservoir simulation is the use of computer programs to help understand and forecast the performance of oil and gas problems. (Crosslisted as ENGR 40223/GEOL 40443.)
courses.prereqText: ENGR 40223 or GEOL 40423.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113, 30243 or 30423. Two hours lecture and one two-hour laboratory period per week. This course covers fundamental aspects of subsurface geology, including: 1) principles of the geophysical well logging and seismology, 2) common geophysical data processing and interpretation, and 3) different exploration methods of subsurface geology. Some common software packages used in the Environmental and Energy industries will be introduced and used over the semester.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Two hours lecture and one two hour laboratory per week. Endogenic and exogenic processes and land forms; geologic control; short-term, long term and human-imposed landscape development; morphometric analysis and study of recent movements; environmental geomorphology. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 40493)
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of the instructor. Field investigations and mapping. Those planning to enroll should contact the Department of Geology by March 1 of the year in which enrollment is contemplated. Field work in rough and robust terrain required; a high degree of physical fitness recommended.
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: junior or senior status and/or permission of instructor. Two hours independent study with a focus on original research. Students are strongly recommended to enroll for this course in the penultimate semester of their degree plan.
courses.prereqText: junior or senior status and/or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of instructor. Field and laboratory problems for advanced undergraduate students. Fifty clock hours of laboratory and field work for each semester hour credit. 1-6 semester hours.
courses.prereqText: permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Two hours per week of lecture, and three hours per week of laboratory work. Geologic processes, earth resources and engineering properties of crustal materials in the activities of society. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50213)
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. Analysis of the behavior of light in crystalline substances, complete treatment of crystal optics and the identification of non-opaque, rock-forming minerals using immersion media and thin section techniques. Intensive use of the microscope required.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Use of the S.E.M. in geological applications.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 30243. Three hours laboratory per week for five weeks. A practicum in interpreting seismic data. Prerequisites: GEOL 50331 or equivalent.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30243.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. Explores the relationship between plate motion and the evolution of sedimentary basins.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Origin, migration and entrapment of hydrocarbons, exploration and production techniques used in the petroleum industry.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: permission of the instructor. This course offers an in-depth exploration of natural hazards and disasters, including earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, floods, landslides, hurricanes, tornadoes, and wildfires. Students will examine the dynamic Earth system processes, including atmospheric, surface, and subsurface processes, that drive these phenomena while critically analyzing how human activities contribute to their frequency and severity. Through an interdisciplinary and global perspective, the course investigates how interconnected systems, such as climate change, tectonic activity, socio-economic factors, and anthropogenic influences, shape disaster occurrence, response, and long-term recovery. Emphasis is placed on global variations in risk perception, preparedness, response, and mitigation efforts, highlighting how various factors influence resilience and vulnerability across different regions. Lab exercises incorporate geospatial technology tools to assess risk, model disaster scenarios, and analyze the cascading effects of hazards on populations, infrastructure, and ecosystems.
courses.prereqText: permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite GEOL 10113 and permission of instructor. Two hours lecture and two hours of laboratory per week. A study of the occurrence, movement, and exploitation of water in the hydrologic cycle including surface-atmosphere, groundwater, and surface water processes. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50493)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL/ENSC 30363. Basic introduction to Geographic Information Systems using ESRI-ArcGIS. Elements of spatial data, mapping, data representation, and geodatabases. Training in use of a GIS system to infer relationships among spatial features. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50523.)
courses.prereqText: GEOL/ENSC 30363.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. Facies analysis and facies models applied to the problem of interpreting stratigraphic sequences and reconstructing paleogeography.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 50331 and 50361, or permission of instructor. A workstation-based practicum on managing and integrating geologic data. Students will become familiar with one or more widely-used software packages for handling multiple data sets used in oil and gas exploration and field development.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 50331 and 50361, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 10113 or equivalent. A broad overview of the natural resources utilized for energy, and the geologic, engineering and business sides of the energy industry. The course will acquaint students with all the steps in the production of oil and gas from developing a prospect to delivering a product, including how geologists decide where to drill, the study of drilling and completion operations, the technology required to produce oil and gas, and carbon sequestration. Students will also be acquainted with the natural resources and environmental issues associated with the generation of electricity, including coal, geothermal, biomass, uranium, tidal, hydroelectricity, and the rare earth elements required for renewable energy.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 30243. This course is an overview of the stratigraphy and petroleum geology of Texas and the adjacent Gulf of Mexico. The course will focus on the relationship between plate tectonics, eustacy, basin formation, and stratigraphy, and how the interplay between them generated some of the largest accumulations of hydrocarbons on the planet. The course will also use Texas examples to discuss concepts of petroleum geology.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30243.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. This course will cover physical and empirical models and their applications in areas such as hydrology, wildlife, ecology, and human health. Class consists of 2 hours lecture, and 2 hours hands-on computer modeling laboratory. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50593)
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 10114 and 10124 or permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week. Application of basic chemical principles to understanding the origin, distribution and migration of chemical elements in the earth's lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere.
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10114 and 10124 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 50233, or permission of instructor. Two hours lecture and one three hour laboratory period per week. Petrogenesis of igneous and metamorphic rocks based on field, petrographic, chemical and isotopic data. Inferences on the evolution and dynamics of the crust and mantle. Involves use of microscope.
courses.prereqText: GEOL 50233, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL

Types and processes of volcanic eruptions; characteristics of modern volcanic products; recognition and significance of ancient volcanic deposits in the stratigraphic record. Involves use of microscope. Field trip required.

courses.subject: GEOL

Project-based, integrated laboratory course covering instrumentation, data acquisition, data analysis and data presentation techniques used in the chemical investigations of geological and related systems including rocks, aquifers, streams and soils. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50633)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10113 or equivalent.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week for five weeks. An introduction to the technology used in remote sensing, including MSS, TM and SPOT, thermal scanners and radar imaging.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Three hours lecture per week for five weeks. An introduction to processing techniques used to enhance the display of remote sensing images with emphasis on those techniques useful in resource mapping.
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 30443 and major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 earned hours, or graduate enrollment, or permission of instructor. This course is designed to teach the basics of groundwater hydrogeology including hydrologic cycle, aquifers, groundwater flow, groundwater recharge, water chemistry and groundwater contamination. At the end of this course, students will be able to understand the relationship between surface water and groundwater, groundwater protection, field methods, and groundwater development. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50763.)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30443 and major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 earned hours, or graduate enrollment, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 earned hours; or graduate enrollment. Students will be introduced to and will analyze selected federal statutes governing environmental remediation, discharge of pollution, and management of wastes, including the Comprehensive Environmental Response Compensation and Liability Act, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Clean Water Act, the Clean Air Act, the Endangered Species Act, and others, including the common law (nuisance, trespass, negligence.) Students will be introduced to the American legal system and the role of experts in lawsuits. Students will read and discuss in class statutes, case law, and related materials. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50773.)
courses.prereqText: Major field of study within the College of Science & Engineering with 60 earned hours; or graduate enrollment.

Chemistry of water, soil, energy, and air as related to environmental problems. Subjects include: nutrients and eutrophication, fluorocarbons, sulfur and nitrogen oxides, Eh-pH relationship, natural carbonate reactions, and cation exchange phenomena. (Crosslisted as CHEM/ENSC/GEOL 50783.)
courses.prereqText: CHEM 10123 and 10122 or 10125 or 20123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL

courses.prereqText: MATH 10043 or equivalent, ENSC/GEOL 30363, and ENSC/GEOL 50523, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: GEOL

This course introduces students to fundamental principles and concepts of remote sensing and explores the applications of remote sensing datasets and techniques in geological and environmental sciences. Hands-on exercises on the applications of remote sensing techniques in geological and environmental sciences are key components of the course. The hands-on exercises are mainly based on data from local or international case studies or collected by students in the field (e.g. using Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS)). Digital image processing techniques/software including ENVI as well as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) processing software such as SNAP will be used for data analysis and interpretation. Crosslisted as GEOL/ENSC 50873.
courses.prereqText: Seniors and graduate students who have taken any of the following courses: GEOL(ENSC) 30363, GEOL 50731, 50523, 50863, 50883, 50713 or permission of instructor.

A GIS faculty supervisor will be appointed for each research problem. (Crosslisted as ENSC/GEOL 50883.)

courses.subject: HARE
courses.description: This course examines topics and perspectives on human-animal relationships (HARE) from multiple disciplines within the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. We will explore the complex relationships between humans and other animals, past and present, including the socially constructed meanings of animals that shape animal/human interactions and relations within institutions and social, cultural, geographic and interactional contexts. We will consider many types of relationships between human and nonhuman animals, both beneficial and detrimental, as well as the trends that are impacting the future of animal/human relations on the planet.
