Emphasis is placed on ensemble playing, listening skills, intonation, phrasing, blend, and musical interpretation. Repertoire includes a wide range of styles and periods, from classical to contemporary, with occasional opportunities for cross-instrumental collaboration. Students are expected to come to rehearsals prepared, participate actively, and perform in public concerts throughout the semester. Open to woodwind players by audition or instructor approval. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: This course is open to all majors with a particular focus on students with a background, major, or minor in music. This course is a pass/no credit course. The course focuses on flexibility, balance, strength, and relaxation. Using postures and breathing exercises adapted to each person's individual level, students will develop improved alignment, breathing, and a balanced body/mind. Students will unite these elements to aid in performance anxiety, posture, phrasing, and other activities inherent to their particular instrument. Limited discussion may include ways to incorporate yoga techniques into the students' daily activities, particularly in practice, rehearsal, and performance. This class is designed to accommodate both those who are new to yoga practice, as well as those with some experience.
courses.prereqText: This course is open to all majors with a particular focus on students with a background, major, or minor in music.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor is required through an audition. Exploration of the preparation and presentation of operatic and music theatre repertoire for an audience. Students enhance their knowledge of singing, acting, movement, stagecraft, and technical theatre throughout the semester.
courses.prereqText: Permission of the instructor is required through an audition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Marching Band.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Audition required. The TCU Symphony is one of TCU's major ensembles and allows the students to perform the standard symphonic repertoire. The 70 -90 member TCU Symphony Orchestra presents repertoire representative of all musical styles and periods.
courses.prereqText: Audition required. The TCU Symphony is one of TCU's major ensembles and allows the students to perform the standard symphonic repertoire.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Vox Resonare is a non-auditioned choral ensemble dedicated to the high-quality performance of treble repertoire. Open to both music majors and non-majors, the ensemble welcomes singers of all experience levels¿no prior experience is required. Vox Resonare presents at least one concert each semester and participates in TCU¿s Christmas Festival during the fall.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Frog Corps is a non-auditioned male ensemble that serves as a spirit group for the university campus. Performances include traditional concerts with other university ensembles, appearances at athletic events, and presentation at university and community social occasions.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: The ensemble performs mixed chamber music primarily composed during the past 25 years.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Students enrolling in Brass Ensemble must be concurrently enrolled in Applied Brass Lessons. Brass Ensemble is for undergraduate music majors and minors enrolled in applied study of their instrument who form a duo, trio, quartet, quintet, or more and seek to work with the faculty member on record for the course section enrolled.
courses.prereqText: Students enrolling in Brass Ensemble must be concurrently enrolled in Applied Brass Lessons. Brass Ensemble is for undergraduate music majors and minors enrolled in applied study of their instrument who form a duo, trio, quartet, quintet, or more and seek to work with the faculty member on record for the course section enrolled.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: This course aims to survey, through performance, various collaborative skills and specific strategies that can aid pianists in becoming more professionally skilled collaborators. Topics may include balance, tone, blending, critical listening, rehearsal techniques, instrumental familiarity, sight-reading, orchestral and vocal reductions, crisis management, self-marketing, and more.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Introduction to the International Phonetic Alphabet and its application to the study of Liturgical Latin, Italian, and English lyric diction.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Collegium Musicum.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10171 or permission of instructor. Application of International Phonetic Alphabet to the study of German and French lyric diction.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10171 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: TCU Jazz Ensembles provides students with the opportunity to rehearse and perform big band music in a collaborative setting. Emphasis is placed on listening skills, intonation, style, blend, improvisation, and pedagogy. The ensembles will cover repertoire from legendary to contemporary artists. Students are expected to come to rehearsals prepared, participate actively, and perform in public concerts throughout the semester. Open to students by audition in the fall or by permission of instructor. May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: A study of the techniques of jazz improvisation through performance. May be repeated for maximum of 4 hours credit.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Introduction to sight-singing as well as melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic dictation.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10003 or placement via AP Exam or School of Music Theory Exam. Musical notation and definitions, intervals, scales, and keys. Emphasis on writing four-voice exercises in major and minor keys using triads and seventh chords. Harmonic analysis.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10003 or placement via AP Exam or School of Music Theory Exam.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Development of rehearsal and performance techniques in large wind ensemble setting. Repertoire selections include new and traditional works as well as works on the Texas University Interscholastic League 4A and 5A list. Audition required.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10201 or placement via School of Music Theory Exam. Single-line and two-line sight-singing exercises. Intermediate-level melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic dictations.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10201 or placement via School of Music Theory Exam.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10203 or placement via AP Exam or School of Music Theory Exam. Continuation of MUSI 10203, including study of suspensions and other non-chord tones, diatonic seventh chords, and secondary functions. Harmonic analysis as well as study of cadences, phrases, and periods.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10203 or placement via AP Exam or School of Music Theory Exam. Continuation of MUSI 10203, including study of suspensions and other non-chord tones, diatonic seventh chords, and secondary functions.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Through rehearsal and performance of concert band repertoire, students will learn a wide variety of compositional techniques, rehearsal processes, and expressive possibilities.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide percussion students with rehearsal and performance experience within a steel band setting.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Music major/minor or permission of instructor. All students enrolled in a mariachi course must be able to play an instrument; therefore, vocalists will be asked to learn a mariachi-based instrument if they do not know how to play one already.
courses.prereqText: Music major/minor or permission of instructor. All students enrolled in a mariachi course must be able to play an instrument; therefore, vocalists will be asked to learn a mariachi-based instrument if they do not know how to play one already.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide percussion students with rehearsal and performance experience within a percussion ensemble setting.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: permission of instructor. Study and performance of music for cello ensemble.
courses.prereqText: permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Instructor's permission required. The study and performance of music for harp ensemble.
courses.prereqText: Instructor's permission required.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Audition required and concurrent enrollment in MUSI 10120. This course is for string players playing in Symphony Orchestra. The TCU Symphony allows the students to perform the standard symphonic repertoire representative of all musical styles and periods.
courses.prereqText: Audition required and concurrent enrollment in MUSI 10120.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music major. This course introduces prospective music teachers to the foundations of EC-12 music education through readings, observation, discussion, and guided micro-teaching. Students explore core principles of teaching and learning and gain early experience with practical instructional skills.
courses.prereqText: Music major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Acceptance in Bachelor of Music Education, Bachelor of Music, or Bachelor of Arts degree plan in Voice. A systematic introduction to the multiple skill sets required of the effective vocal performer and exploration of artistic and practical aspects of the performer's world.
courses.prereqText: Acceptance in Bachelor of Music Education, Bachelor of Music, or Bachelor of Arts degree plan in Voice.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Music majors are required to attend a minimum of 15 concerts and recitals each semester, with the exception of the student-teaching semester for Music Education majors. Six (6) of these concerts must be from the weekly School of Music Recital Hour Series. The remainder may be chosen from faculty and guest artist recitals, TCU and guest ensemble concerts, and student recitals. Students will submit original printed concert programs signed by a TCU School of Music faculty member in attendance. This course activity is an important element in the development of critical listening skills. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Beginning piano for non-keyboard music majors who are preparing to pass the basic piano requirement. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 11030. Continuation of MUSI 11030. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: MUSI 11030. Continuation of MUSI 11030.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Class instruction designed to train students in vocal technique and literature.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Keyboard, Piano Pedagogy and Music Education piano concentration majors only; MUSI 10201, 10203, 10211, 10213 and two semesters 20201. Functional keyboard skills for keyboard majors, including transposition, harmonization, score-reduction, improvisation
courses.prereqText: Keyboard, Piano Pedagogy and Music Education piano concentration majors only; MUSI 10201, 10203, 10211, 10213 and two semesters 20201. Functional keyboard skills for keyboard majors, including transposition, harmonization, score-reduction, improvisation

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20071. Continuation of MUSI 20071.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20071. Continuation of MUSI 20071.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10211. Single line, two-voice, and four-voice sight-singing exercises. Advanced melodic and rhythmic dictation exercises. Harmonic dictation exercises including seventh chords and modulations.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10211.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10213. Modulatory techniques, simple binary and ternary forms, modal mixture, and chromatic chords. Harmonic analysis and compositional exercises.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20201. Emphasis on two- to four-voice sight-singing exercises. Advanced melodic and rhythmic dictation exercises. Harmonic dictation exercises, including modulations.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20201.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Sophomore standing in music or permission of instructor. A workshop class for pianists in which selected works of the piano literature are performed, analyzed and discussed. Special focus is on the etude and its development. Class members perform assigned works and present individual reports on topics relating to the music.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing in music or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20203. Continuation of MUSI 20203, including tonal harmony in the late 19th century and an introduction to 20th century practice. Harmonic analysis and compositional exercises.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20203. Continuation of MUSI 20203, including tonal harmony in the late 19th century and an introduction to 20th century practice.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music major. A study of foundational music pedagogy, learning theory, lesson planning, behavioral principles, inclusive practices, and assessment in PreK-12 settings. Learning is reinforced through guided observations, structured teaching experiences, and reflective analysis.
courses.prereqText: Music major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 10203, 10213 and declared major or minor in theory/composition. Beginning compositional exercises in tonal genres with emphasis on basic chromatic usage in short keyboard, vocal, and rondo forms.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 10203, 10213 and declared major or minor in theory/composition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20203 and declared major or minor in theory/composition. Continuation of MUSI 20412. Compositional exercises in tonal genres with emphasis on advanced chromatic usage in short keyboard and vocal forms as well as in small chamber ensembles.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20203 and declared major or minor in theory/composition. Continuation of MUSI 20412.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: This course is a study and development of skills pertinent to choral pedagogy methods including score preparation; technical discernment; error detection; analysis of vocal tone, timbre, and production; musicianship; effective teaching strategies, and rehearsal techniques for the secondary choral classroom. Lab Required.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Sophomore standing, music major or permission of instructor. Conducting patterns, preparation, cues, release, and technical and expressive movements applicable to vocal and instrumental conductors.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore standing, music major or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce the fundamental principles of contemporary marching band and provide opportunities to practice applying these skills in order to prepare, organize, teach, and rehearse this type of ensemble. Students will gain a command of the terminology, pedagogy, and structure of the marching band activity; learn technical elements of drill design and construction; and develop an understanding of the trends and philosophies facing contemporary school marching band programs.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Successful completion of MUSI 10213 or permission of instructor. This course is designed to help students understand the position of music in history, contributions to musical thought, and the development of musical style in Western culture to the mid-seventeenth century through a detailed study of music literature.
courses.prereqText: Successful completion of MUSI 10213 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 11040. Continuation of MUSI 11040. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: MUSI 11040. Continuation of MUSI 11040.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 21030. Continuation of MUSI 21030. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: MUSI 21030. Continuation of MUSI 21030.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Upper division standing (junior or senior) in vocal music education or permission from instructor. This course is an introduction to vocal pedagogy and voice science. Topics will include anatomy and physiology of the vocal mechanism, diagnosis and correction of vocal faults, acoustics, and technology in the classroom. Supplemental seminars will provide practical experience with audio recording concepts and technologies.
courses.prereqText: Upper division standing (junior or senior) in vocal music education or permission from instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing in music and in piano. Introduction to methods, materials and techniques employed in the teaching of beginning piano students. Establishing and managing a piano studio public relations, equipment and layout, professional memberships, budget and tax information, studio policy and teacher-student-parent roles. Lecture and observation.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in music and in piano.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 30052. Examines materials for the intermediate piano student method books, standard piano repertoire, theory and technique, jazz and ensemble works. Also focuses on practice motivation, recital preparation, and auditions, festivals and contests. Also deals with teaching preschool and adult beginners. Lecture and observation.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 30052.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: MUSI 20213. Development of skills in music arranging for instrumental ensembles in educational settings. Students will use music notation software to produce creative musical arrangements in traditional and digital formats including music designed for both classroom teaching and ensemble performance.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music Major. This course introduces foundational skills for playing and teaching the saxophone, oboe, and bassoon, with emphasis on beginning-level pedagogy. Students develop functional performance ability, essential tone production and articulation techniques, and pedagogical strategies for introducing and sequencing early instruction in both homogeneous and heterogeneous ensemble settings. Selected intermediate techniques may be addressed as appropriate.
courses.prereqText: Music Major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music Major. This course introduces foundational skills for playing and teaching the trumpet and horn, with emphasis on beginning-level pedagogy. Students develop functional performance ability, essential tone production and articulation techniques, and pedagogical strategies for introducing and sequencing early instruction in both homogeneous and heterogeneous ensemble settings.
courses.prereqText: Music Major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Corequisite: Concurrent enrollment in MUSI 10100 Opera Studio is required. Development of acting techniques to enhance the dramatic presentation of vocal music. Units include musical and text analysis, character development, focus choices, gestures, attitudes, dramatic arcs and interpretive methods for presenting sung repertoire in public settings..

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music Major. This course introduces foundational skills for playing and teaching the flute and clarinet, with emphasis on beginning-level pedagogy. Students develop functional performance ability, essential tone production and articulation techniques, and pedagogical strategies for introducing and sequencing early instruction in both homogeneous and heterogeneous ensemble settings.
courses.prereqText: Music Major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music Major. This course introduces foundational skills for playing and teaching the trombone, euphonium, and tuba, with emphasis on beginning-level pedagogy. Students develop functional performance ability, essential tone production and articulation techniques, and pedagogical strategies for introducing and sequencing early instruction in both homogeneous and heterogeneous ensemble settings.
courses.prereqText: Music Major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20213. Analysis of phrases, periods, simple and compound forms, rondo, sonata, and elements of fugue. Emphasis on the standard designs found in instrumental music from Bach on.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20213. Fundamental skills, philosophy, and concepts for teaching jazz in an educational setting.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20213. Counterpoint in the style of 16th century vocal/choral compositions. Topics include ecclesiastical modes, melodic structure, two-part composition, multiple-part textures, cadences, and imitation.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20213. Counterpoint in the style of 18th century compositions. Topics include melodic structure, two-part textures, multiple-part textures, chromaticism, invertible counterpoint, imitation, the trio sonata, fugue, cantata, and contrapuntal variation forms.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20213.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior standing as a BME student in the School of Music, or by permission of instructor. In this course, students will learn fundamental skills and concepts for teaching jazz in the school setting, including standard notation and instrumentation, styles, improvisation, rehearsal techniques, repertoire, and programming considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of jazz theory, and will participate in and teach a lab ensemble as part of the class.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing as a BME student in the School of Music, or by permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: MUSI 20211, 20213. Practical consideration of techniques, capabilities and effective uses of orchestral and band instruments in various combinations. Arranging and scoring.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Completion of Music Education (MUSI 10511) and Field Experience (MUSI 20311). Simultaneous enrollment or completion of Choral Methods and Materials II (MUSI 30912) or Instrumental Methods and Materials (MUSI 30812). This course prepares students to effectively teach music to children from early childhood through sixth grade. Students will explore a variety of elementary music education methods and engage in hands-on experiences. Emphasis will be placed on developing skills in vocal and instrumental expression, rhythmic activities, critical listening, creative experience, and music reading.
courses.prereqText: Completion of Music Education (MUSI 10511) and Field Experience (MUSI 20311). Simultaneous enrollment or completion of Choral Methods and Materials II (MUSI 30912) or Instrumental Methods and Materials (MUSI 30812).

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Open to Music Composition majors who have completed MUSI 30312 (Instrumentation), or by permission of instructor. Project-based application of concepts learned in MUSI 30312 to music arranging and composition.
courses.prereqText: Open to Music Composition majors who have completed MUSI 30312 (Instrumentation), or by permission of instructor. Project-based application of concepts learned in MUSI 30312 to music arranging and composition.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: MUSI 20203/20213, 30312, or permission of instructor. Study in technique of scoring for the contemporary marching band.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20203/20213, 30312, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: MUSI 20203/ 20213, 30312, or permission of instructor. Study in technique of scoring for the modern jazz orchestra.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20203/ 20213, 30312, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music major, music minor, or permission of instructor. Through a project based curriculum students will explore the fundamental principles and techniques of electronic and electro-acoustic compositional techniques, synthesis, audio recording principles and techniques, the function and operation of music studio equipment including microphones, digital audio workstations, audio editing and effects software, synthesizers, mixers and MIDI devices.
courses.prereqText: Music major, music minor, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Sophomore Level. Any major. An investigation of basic and electronic audio concepts, psychoacoustics, digital audio recording techniques, and synthesis. Projects are produced with student owned computers utilizing microphones, connectors and interfaces provided by the university. Students will demonstrate understanding of recording apparatus including, microphones, digital audio workstations, editing software, audio mixers and MIDI controllers.
courses.prereqText: Sophomore Level. Any major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20412 or permission of instructor. Advanced private study in composition. Primarily intended for composition majors. 1-10 semester hours.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20412 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20512. Technique of the baton, score reading, tone production, rehearsal routines, vocal materials, organization problems, supervised practice in conducting chorus. Meets choral conducting requirements for secondary school teachers.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20512.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 20512. Instrumental conducting technique, score reading and analysis, supervised practice conducting ensembles. Meets instrumental conducting requirements for secondary school teachers. Lab required.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 20512.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior-level standing as a music major, or permission of instructor. This course serves as an introduction for music majors to the variety of musics found in cultures around the world outside the Western art music tradition.
courses.prereqText: Junior-level standing as a music major, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Successful completion of MUSI 20613 or permission of instructor and completion of ENGL 10803 and 20803. Exploration of musical genres, forms, composers, and styles in Europe and the New World from the mid-seventeenth to the late nineteenth century.
courses.prereqText: Successful completion of MUSI 20613 or permission of instructor and completion of ENGL 10803 and 20803.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Successful completion of MUSI 30613, ENGL 10803 and 20803. Historical and cultural overview of trends in Western music from the late nineteenth century to the present, addressing topics including art music, jazz, and popular music.
courses.prereqText: Successful completion of MUSI 30613, ENGL 10803 and 20803.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Music major. This course is a study of wind band pedagogy methods with emphasis on instrumental instructional techniques, effective teaching strategies, rehearsal techniques, comprehensive musicianship, classroom management, motivation, and administration of the secondary band program. Lab required.
courses.prereqText: Music major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 30812. This course is a continuation of the study and development of wind and percussion pedagogy methods with emphasis on effective teaching strategies, rehearsal techniques, comprehensive musicianship, classroom management, motivation, and administration in the secondary band program. Lab required.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 30812.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Acceptance to the College of Education and completion of MUSI 20511. This course is a study of choral pedagogy methods with emphasis on vocal and choral techniques, effective teaching strategies, rehearsal techniques, comprehensive musicianship, classroom management, motivation, and administration the secondary choral program. Lab required.
courses.prereqText: Acceptance to the College of Education and completion of MUSI 20511.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Completion of MUSI 30912. This course is a continuation of the study and development of choral pedagogy methods with emphasis on effective teaching strategies, rehearsal techniques, teaching comprehensive musicianship, classroom management and motivation of the secondary choral program. Lab Required.
courses.prereqText: Completion of MUSI 30912.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Specialized work in student's area of concentration. 1-6 Hours
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior standing. This course is an introduction to the history, music, and culture of hip-hop and rap from their origins in the Bronx in the 1970s to the present. The course examines rap as a major American expressive art form with a global influence, exploring its historical development, musical and performance practices, and its political and social impact¿particularly within the U.S. and Black diasporic cultures.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Senior standing and MUSI 30613, 30623 Honors. Under the guidance of a faculty committee, the student will present an Honors Project, e.g., Lecture/Recital, Composition, Research Paper.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing and MUSI 30613, 30623 Honors.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Junior or senior standing as an instrumental performance major. The study and analysis of teaching music literature; teaching concepts and the practical application of these concepts; the comparisons of the schools of performance/teaching methods.
courses.prereqText: Junior or senior standing as an instrumental performance major.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Senior standing in music and piano; MUSI 30052, 30062. Explores group piano instruction at all levels pre-K through grade 12, adult non-credit, college non-music majors and music majors. Texts, supplementary materials, electronic instruments; teaching techniques and group dynamics. Lecture, observation and supervised teaching.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing in music and piano; MUSI 30052, 30062. Explores group piano instruction at all levels pre-K through grade 12, adult non-credit, college non-music majors and music majors.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: MUSI 40052. Each student will teach two piano pupils for the semester, culminating in an evaluation and recital. Weekly classes serve as a forum for discussion of problems and exchange of ideas, as well as the examination of current trends and research in piano pedagogy. Lecture, observation and supervised teaching.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 40052.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Upper division standing in vocal performance or vocal concentration. Methods and materials for teaching voice. Topics will include anatomy and physiology of the vocal mechanism, diagnosis and correction of vocal faults, acoustics, and audio recording technologies.
courses.prereqText: Upper division standing in vocal performance or vocal concentration.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Senior standing in music or permission of instructor. A workshop class for pianists in which the piano works of a major composer are performed, analyzed and discussed. Class members perform assigned works and present individual reports on topics relating to the music.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing in music or permission of instructor. A workshop class for pianists in which the piano works of a major composer are performed, analyzed and discussed.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisites: Music major or permission of instructor. This course serves as an enhancement to individual private study and ensemble participation through the development of professional preparation of symphonic, operatic, ballet, and chamber repertoire. Precise repertoire selection will vary based on instrument. Additional skills developed through this course may include professional resume review and professional conduct, especially as they relate to professional auditions.
courses.prereqText: Music major or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 50053 or equivalent and permission of instructor. Students are encouraged to develop their own practical studio procedures in harmony with the common ideals of Western artistic voice culture.
courses.prereqText: MUSI 50053 or equivalent and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: MUSI
courses.description: Prerequisite: Senior or graduate standing. The lecture course will address business practices needed to successfully establish and maintain an independent music studio. The course will discuss business models, self-employment issues, studio organization, record keeping, tax concerns, marketing, recruiting, and retaining students. Reading and research assignments and preparation of materials will provide the basis for learning.
courses.prereqText: Senior or graduate standing.

courses.description: In-depth study of the International Phonetic Alphabet and its application to the performance of English (multiple dialects) and Italian lyric diction.

courses.description: Prerequisite: MUSI 30623 and senior standing; or graduate standing in music; or permission of instructor. Comprehensive survey of non-operatic solo vocal repertoire designed for students in voice, choral conducting, and collaborative piano. Topics will alternate between Italian (Baroque and Classical), German, Slavic, Scandinavian, and Spanish/Latin American repertoire from the 19th and 20th centuries; and Italian (Romantic and 20th Century), French, British, and American art song traditions. May be repeated once for credit when topics differ.

Students will develop ensemble musicianship through the study and performance of diverse repertoire appropriate to the group¿s instrumentation and focus. Emphasis is placed on technical proficiency, stylistic awareness, rehearsal strategies, and active listening skills. Participants are expected to prepare individual parts outside of rehearsal, contribute constructively to group rehearsals, and engage in public performances.

Students will concentrate on foundational skills regarding practice, independent music learning, diction, and style. The repertoire studied will be assigned by the primary studio teacher. courses.subject: MUSP
courses.description: Prerequisites: Concurrent enrollment in MUSP 20110. This elective course will further the development of vocal technique through the application of measurable analyses to the coordination of vocal-fold vibration, airflow and resonation factors resulting in the desired chiaroscuro tone. The Kay-elemetrics Computerized Speech Lab, the Voce Vista program (in conjunction with electroglottography), and recording and video equipment will be used. In addition to analyzing their own singing in the vocal laboratory, students may examine recordings from their studio lessons, and compare technical strategies of recorded professional singers. All work will be coordinated with the studio teacher.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: A study of contemporary issues in nutrition and food science that impact the individual and span the global community. Two hours lecture and one two-hour laboratory period per week. Course is offered with TCU Online components that support learning by multiple instructional formats including lecture, class discussions, lab interactives, group learning projects and oral presentations. Laboratory interactives will include traditional and computer laboratory exercises.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two 1-hour lectures, one 3-hour laboratory per week. Scientific principles and fundamental processes underlying food preparation with practical application.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Topics may vary each time it is offered.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: The science of nutrition integrating physiological, biochemical, and psychological aspects of food ingestion and nutrient utilization.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: This course addresses the cultural and social meanings of food. It explores the study of world food patterns, including food customs of peoples with different ethnic backgrounds. An emphasis is placed upon the significance of the social, economic, religious, and aesthetic aspects of food customs. Learning activities include lectures, group discussions, film/videos, mapping, cooking demonstrations and food tastings, and individual field experiences.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: Advanced standing in Nutrition Sciences, and permission of instructor.Observe and review honors students' presentations. Complete draft of background and methods sections of written research manuscript.
courses.prereqText: Advanced standing in Nutrition Sciences, and permission of instructor.Observe and review honors students' presentations.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Didactic Program in Dietetics major. An introduction to Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics organization and structure, dietetic registration requirements, and the Supervised Practice application process.
courses.prereqText: Didactic Program in Dietetics major.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two 1-hour lectures, one 2-hour laboratory per week. Planning, preparation and presentation of nutritious, attractive gourmet food, with practical laboratory experiences.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Emphasizes the significance and role of nutrition during pregnancy, lactation, and childhood. Nutritional needs and assessment of mother, infant and children under normal and special circumstances will be discussed. Credit cannot be earned for both NTDT 30113 and 30123.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: A study of the relationship of nutritional requirements to the life cycle, prenatal to old age; cultural and socioeconomic factors related to food with major focus on nutrition and health; nutritional assessment; interrelationships of nutrients; other nutrition related issues such as dental health, weight management, athletic training, drugs and alcohol, government agencies, and nutrition education for all age groups. Credit cannot be earned for both NTDT 30113 and 30123.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: NTDT 10103. Two 1-hour lectures, one 2-hour laboratory per week. Managing resources in meal planning and preparation; technology of food preservation; identification of market places and legislative concerns; aesthetic and practical experience in a laboratory.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 10103.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Three 1-hour lectures and one 3-hour laboratory/supervised practice per week. Prerequisite: NTDT 10103. Advanced study in food preparation, emphasizing standards, principles and techniques of producing quality food in quantity. Care and use of equipment, work simplification, menu planning, and basic cost controls.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 10103.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: NTDT 20403. Psychological effects of exercise and nutrition on the human body. Current topics of interest, current research, and their relationship to athletic performance.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 20403.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 20403, NTDT 30123 or NTDT 30133, CHEM 30123, and BIOL 20214. Emphasizes fundamental knowledge for the Registered Dietitian (RD) and the role of the Registered Dietitian within the health care team. Course content includes the Nutrition Care Process and Medical Nutrition Therapy documentation for enhancing development of skills to perform nutrition assessment, diagnosis, intervention and monitoring/evaluation.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 20403, NTDT 30123 or NTDT 30133, CHEM 30123, and BIOL 20214.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: MANA 30653 or permission of instructor. Introductory communications course with applications in counseling and education with emphasis on developing interpersonal and professional practice skills in food, nutrition, and dietetics.
courses.prereqText: MANA 30653 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two lecture hours and 14 to 16 hours of supervised practice per week. Prerequisite: Admission to Coordinated Program in Dietetics and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 30303. Introduction to the practice of all aspects of dietetics through weekly observation and participation in foodservice and nutrition care settings.
courses.prereqText: Admission to Coordinated Program in Dietetics and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 30303.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30144 and 30303. Systems approach to the organization and management of foodservice operations including the functional subsystems (procurement, production, service, and maintenance).

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two lecture hours and 20 hours of supervised practice per week. Prerequisites: Admission to Coordinated Program in Dietetics and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 30313. Selected problems and supervised practice directly correlated with NTDT 30313.
courses.prereqText: Admission to Coordinated Program in Dietetics and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 30313. Selected problems and supervised practice directly correlated with NTDT 30313.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior standing or permission of instructor. Terminology describing normal anatomical, physiological, and psychological conditions and those related to disease and its treatments. For students entering health professions.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 20403, 30123 or 30113, 30233, 30331 or concurrent enrollment, CHEM 30123 and BIOL 20214, or permission of the instructor. Knowledge and skills necessary for implementation of the Nutrition Care Process and evidence-based nutrition intervention among individuals with physiological and biochemical abnormalities associated with various conditions such as, but not limited to, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and gastrointestinal (GI) disorders. Study of pharmacology and nutrition support as a component of Medical Nutrition Therapy. Lecture format incorporates case studies to provide skill enhancement.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 20403, 30123 or 30113, 30233, 30331 or concurrent enrollment, CHEM 30123 and BIOL 20214, or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: An in-depth study of local, national, and international food issues and the way critical analysis and rational thought can be utilized in the study of these issues. The role of ethics in citizenship and social values will be utilized to justify positions related to foods and nutrition. Issues and insights regarding the relationship of food/nutrition to health and well-being is emphasized so that students are able to demonstrate an understanding of individual rights/responsibilities and critically assess the intentions and consequences of personal, professional, or societal actions. Problem solving, critical thinking, and various methods of inquiry are emphasized in discussions/assignments related to ethical dilemmas surrounding controversial food/nutrition-related issues.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior or Senior classification. Priority for enrollment in this course will be as follows: Human-Animal Relationships Minor, Nutrition Minor, Nutritional Sciences Major, all other TCU students. This course will critically examine scientific, environmental, historical, cultural, and societal contexts of the eating habits of humans, with particular attention to plant-based cultures and the ideology of the vegan movement.
courses.prereqText: Junior or Senior classification. Priority for enrollment in this course will be as follows: Human-Animal Relationships Minor, Nutrition Minor, Nutritional Sciences Major, all other TCU students.

The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: A Global Perspective of Food Insecurity provides students with opportunities to actively engage in critical thinking and problem-solving regarding various food and nutrition issues that affect the global community. With a focus on a study abroad experience in Seville, Spain, students will explore the incidence of food insecurity on a local level (Fort Worth, TX) and the global stage (Seville, Spain), utilizing comparisons and contrasts to make informed judgments. Hands-on service-learning and community engagement will take place at non-profit social service agencies. Lectures, assigned readings, field trips, guest speakers, threaded discussions, cultural events are included to expand the global awareness and to develop global responsibility of students. The course is open to all majors. Fluency in Spanish is NOT required.

Students will also develop a research design, including purpose and primary research objectives, null hypothesis, literature review, and research methods/procedures. (1-3 semester hours).
courses.prereqText: Current enrollment in the BS in Dietetics (DIET) Students will begin the investigatory process of a nutrition research study by completing research training and evidence-based practice tutorials.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: Advanced standing in Nutritional Sciences, and permission of instructor. Prepare for oral presentation and present research during Honors Week. Prepare written research manuscript under the direction of faculty. .
courses.prereqText: Advanced standing in Nutritional Sciences, and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 40000 and enrollment in the Combined BS/MS in Dietetics Program in Department of Nutritional Sciences. Students will apply scientific principles of investigation in a nutrition research study while completing a Protocol Review Request for research and utilizing appropriate research methods, ethical procedures, data coding and statistical analysis using SPSS or other applicable technology.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40000 and enrollment in the Combined BS/MS in Dietetics Program in Department of Nutritional Sciences.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Didactic Program in Dietetics major. This course consists of seminar topics designed for planning and preparation for professional advancement, including application to Supervised Practice programs and graduate school placement.
courses.prereqText: Didactic Program in Dietetics major.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 20403, or concurrent enrollment. Projects in nutritional science research carried out under the direction of a faculty member. Because ongoing research projects differ from one semester to the next, students gain additional research skills each time they take the course. Variable credit between one to four hours per enrollment canbe earned for this course. The course may be repeated for a maximum of four times. However, a maximum of 4 credits can be earned for this course.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 20403, or concurrent enrollment.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Current enrollment in the BS in Dietetics (DIET) major. Supervised practice experiences are in selected community, foodservice and nutrition care settings with an emphasis on the provision of nutritional services, nutrition education, interprofessional education and team collaboration.
courses.prereqText: Current enrollment in the BS in Dietetics (DIET) major.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 40403 and current enrollment in the BS in Dietetics (DIET) major. Supervised practice experiences are in selected community and foodservice settings with an emphasis on food systems management and the provision of nutritional services and nutrition education.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40403 and current enrollment in the BS in Dietetics (DIET) major.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30333 or permission of the instructor. Physiological and biochemical abnormalities associated with various diseases and disorders. Advanced knowledge and techniques necessary for comprehensive medical nutrition therapy. Discussion of the importance of nutrition intervention and the role of the registered dietitian as a member of the health care team.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30333 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two lecture hours and 20 hours of supervised practice per week. Prerequisites: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 30317 and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40333. Application of principles of nutritional care in a clinical setting under the supervision of a Registered Dietitian.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 30317 and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40333.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 20403, 30333; BIOL 20214; CHEM 30123. Biochemical and physiological mechanisms of nutrition science and metabolism are covered.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two 1-hour lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week. Prerequisites: NTDT 20403, CHEM 30123 or permission of instructor. Advanced theory and methods used in study of chemical and physical factors affecting food preparation and processing. Application of analytical methods to sensory and instrumental evaluation of food quality.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 20403, CHEM 30123 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30113 or 30123, 30303, or permission of instructor. Nutritional problems and the services available in the community. Management of nutrition services, provision of nutrition information to the public, and the legislative process.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30113 or 30123, 30303, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two lecture hours and twenty hours of supervised practice per week 8 weeks. Prerequisites: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 40337, and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40363. Supervised experiences in selected community agencies and schools with emphasis on the provision of nutritional services and education.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 40337, and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40363.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Two lecture hours and twenty hours of supervised practice per week 6 weeks. Prerequisite: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 40364, and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40363. Supervised experience while working as an independent staff dietitian in an area of chosen specialty.
courses.prereqText: Enrollment in Coordinated Program in Dietetics, NTDT 40364, and concurrent enrollment in NTDT 40363.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: NTDT 30303 or concurrent enrollment. Integration of scientific information and nutrition research into practice. Completion of research training and evidence-based practice tutorials. Completion of research design, including purpose and primary research objectives, null hypothesis, literature review, and research methods/procedures.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30303 or concurrent enrollment.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30313. Course includes principles of management as applied to foodservice organizations and dietetics practice. Leadership, ethics, human resources management, marketing, and financial management are covered.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30313.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisite: NTDT 40411, or concurrent enrollment. Integration of scientific information and nutrition research into practice. Completion of a Protocol Review Request for Research. Completion of a nutrition research project using appropriate research methods, ethical procedures, and statistical analysis.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40411, or concurrent enrollment.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30144, 30303, and 30313. Advanced study of organization and management of foodservice operations. Financial management, marketing, and system analysis concepts applied to the foodservice industry.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 40421, or concurrent enrollment. Integration of scientific information and nutrition research into practice. Compilation of nutrition research into visual materials appropriate for presentation at local, state, and/or national professional meetings. Students will present research poster at the annual TCU College of Science and Engineering Student Research Symposium (SRS) during Honor's Week.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40421, or concurrent enrollment.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior standing in the Department of Nutritional Sciences. This course includes the application of current theories and techniques of counseling and education to the field of nutrition and dietetics. Practical application of communication techniques, client-centered counseling methods, motivational interviewing, group counseling learning theories and behavior change techniques, and factors affecting eating patterns will be covered. Instructional material and media design will also be incorporated.
courses.prereqText: Junior standing in the Department of Nutritional Sciences.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Food Management major and junior standing. Supervised practical experiences in food, nutrition, and/or dietetics provide opportunities for learning and applications in organizational management, foodservice and culinary arts, and nutrition or dietetics health-care settings.
courses.prereqText: Food Management major and junior standing.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Hours to be arranged. Special problems requiring independent research and study within a related area of field experience in food, nutrition, or dietetics. (1-6 semester hours)

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the current and emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare. Students will learn about AI-powered tools and technologies used in hospitals, clinics, and research settings, including AI-driven diagnostic systems, robotic surgery, predictive analytics for disease diagnosis and management, and AI-assisted drug discovery. The course will emphasize practical applications and case studies, allowing students to gain a deeper understanding of how AI is transforming healthcare delivery and patient outcomes. Ethical implications and challenges related to AI adoption in healthcare will also be addressed. This course is designed for students with an interest in the practical implementation of AI in medicine.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing. This seminar will provide the student with an advanced exploration and study of culinary medicine principles. The field of culinary medicine blends culinary skills with the science of medicine and nutrition. Through this course, students will gain skills and knowledge in both areas. Learning activities include lectures, group discussions, and cooking demonstrations, application, and food tasting. The course is designed for students pursuing clinical and healthcare-related fields of study.
courses.prereqText: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20234 or BIOL 30304 or permission of instructor. This class will cover the composition and function of the human gut microbiota, its relevance to health, and the different environmental factors that play a role on its configuration. The class also addresses the gut microbial changes that have been linked to the incidence of diseases and the potential therapeutics that can be employed to prevent and/or treat diseases by modifying the gut microbiota. Lastly, antibiotics, antibiotic resistance, and antibiotic stewardship will be reviewed.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 20234 or BIOL 30304 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 40343 or BIOL 40513, graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval. This course provides an advanced study of the principles of nutrition in relation to the biochemical, physiological, and molecular aspects of the human body.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40343 or BIOL 40513, graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 10103, NTDT 20403, and CHEM 30123. Advanced theory and methods used in study of chemical and physical factors affecting food preparation and processing. Application of analytical methods to sensory and instrumental evaluation of food quality.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 10103, NTDT 20403, and CHEM 30123.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30123 and NTDT 30303, or instructor approval. Course explores nutritional problems and the services available in the community. Management of nutrition services, provision of nutrition information to the public, and the legislative process are studied. Activities to prevent disease and promote health at the local, state, national and global levels will be examined.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30123 and NTDT 30303, or instructor approval.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing. Fundamentals of research methods, research design, treatment and interpretation of data in nutrition. Primarily designed for students with an interest in Nutrition and Dietetics.
courses.prereqText: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval. This graduate seminar will provide the student with an advanced exploration and study of selected topics and emerging issues in food, nutrition, and dietetics as determined by faculty. This course may be repeated for additional credit with faculty approval, provided the topics differ from previous enrollment (up to 6 hours).
courses.prereqText: Graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing. This course provides a comprehensive overview of the current and emerging applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare. Students will learn about AI-powered tools and technologies used in hospitals, clinics, and research settings, including AI-driven diagnostic systems, robotic surgery, predictive analytics for disease diagnosis and management, and AI-assisted drug discovery. The course will emphasize practical applications and case studies, allowing students to gain a deeper understanding of how AI is transforming healthcare delivery and patient outcomes. Ethical implications and challenges related to AI adoption in healthcare will also be addressed. This course is designed for students with an interest in the practical implementation of AI in medicine.
courses.prereqText: Junior or above undergraduate standing or graduate standing.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20234 or BIOL 30304 or permission of instructor. This class will cover the composition and function of the human gut microbiota, its relevance to health, and the different environmental factors that play a role on its configuration. The class also addresses the gut microbial changes that have been linked to the incidence of diseases and the potential therapeutics that can be employed to prevent and/or treat diseases by modifying the gut microbiota. Lastly, antibiotics, antibiotic resistance, and antibiotic stewardship will be reviewed.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 20234 or BIOL 30304 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 40343 or BIOL 40513, graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval. This course provides an advanced study of the principles of nutrition in relation to the biochemical, physiological, and molecular aspects of the human body.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 40343 or BIOL 40513, graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 10103, NTDT 20403, and CHEM 30123. Advanced theory and methods used in study of chemical and physical factors affecting food preparation and processing. Application of analytical methods to sensory and instrumental evaluation of food quality.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 10103, NTDT 20403, and CHEM 30123.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: NTDT 30123 and NTDT 30303. Course explores nutritional problems and the services available in the community. Management of nutrition services, provision of nutrition information to the public, and the legislative process are studied. Activities to prevent disease and promote health at the local, state, national and global levels will be examined.
courses.prereqText: NTDT 30123 and NTDT 30303.

courses.subject: NTDT
courses.description: Prerequisites: Graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval. This graduate seminar will provide the student with an advanced exploration and study of selected topics and emerging issues in food, nutrition, and dietetics as determined by faculty. This course may be repeated for additional credit with faculty approval, provided the topics differ from previous enrollment (up to 6 hours).
courses.prereqText: Graduate status in the department of Nutritional Sciences, or instructor approval.
