courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Open to all majors. Prerequisite: a C or better in PSYC 10213. Introduces the student to principles of growth and development throughout life cycle from conception to death. Provides an overview of the major theories of human development.
courses.prereqText: a C or better in PSYC 10213.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course will provide a broad overview of health disparities in African Americans. Key determinants including biological, genetic, social, environmental, cultural, and institutional impacting health outcomes will be explored. In addition a historical and economical perspective will be presented.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20204, 20214, 20234, NTDT 20403, SOCI 20213 and NURS 10303. This course introduces the student to the profession of nursing through an overview of nursing based on historical, theoretical, political, social, and economic perspectives. Students are introduced to nursing roles, the US healthcare system, ethical decision making, cultural competency, health promotion, standards of practice, and professional accountability.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Supervised study for students who transfer into Nursing or for students who exhibit special needs during the freshman or sophomore years.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Supervised study for students who transfer into Nursing or for students who exhibit special needs during the freshman or sophomore years.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20204, 20214, 20234, NTDT 20403, SOCI 20213, and NURS 10303. This course presents an overview of client assessments. It will focus on expected findings, normal variations, and most common unexpected findings for diverse clients. Principles and theories of growth and development throughout lifecycle as they relate to assessment will be discussed. Additionally, there will be an emphasis on communication and interviewing strategies, and techniques to conduct comprehensive and focused assessments as well as the use of standardized assessment tools. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20204, 20214, 20234, NTDT 20403, SOCI 20213, NURS 10303. This course guides the student to perform total and focused assessments and in the use of standardized assessment tools for clients across the life span. The student will practice interviewing, assessing, and documenting findings and applying concepts of human development, cultural and ethnic cultural considerations when performing assessments. Fees apply per Nursing policy.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: BIOL 20204, 20214, 20234, NTDT 20403, SOCI 20213, and NURS 10303. Introduction to abnormal functioning of cells, tissues, organs, and systems over the human lifespan. Clinical manifestations of disease processes will be explored.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth view of health disparities in African Americans addressing the key determinants impacting health outcomes incorporating a multidisciplinary, theoretical approach. Students will also explore the importance of federal, state, and local organizations in decreasing health disparities.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to nursing, health science or pre-nursing program. This course will explore collaborative approaches for addressing global solutions in integrated health, business, education and engineering systems using culturally intelligent team-based approaches.
courses.prereqText: Admission to nursing, health science or pre-nursing program.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: The course examines selected cultures in an international setting. Social and scientific factors are related to health beliefs and practices and health care delivery systems of the country visited and examined. Critical analysis of selected topics will be accomplished. Open to all majors. Usually taught in summer abroad program.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Current nursing major and successful completion of NURS 20363, NURS 20263, NURS 20271. This course engages nursing students to further develop their critical thinking skills and clinical judgment through patient scenarios, case studies, and active learning activities such as games, virtual escape rooms, and other hands-on activities. Students will apply the steps of the clinical judgment measurement model to reinforce and complement prior knowledge gained in the nursing curriculum.
courses.prereqText: Current nursing major and successful completion of NURS 20363, NURS 20263, NURS 20271.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisite: BIOL 20204, 20214, 20263, 20271, 20363; Concurrent: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171. This course begins the nursing student's education on the concepts of pharmacotherapeutics by establishing a knowledge base that applies to safety, patient care, and education. At the completion of this course, the student will understand the major drug classifications and the nurse's responsibility in relation to medication administration and the nursing process. Basic mathematics skills are also necessary. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 20263, NURS 20271, NURS 20363, and NURS 20043. This course introduces basic nursing skills with focus on safe performance of psychomotor skills, safety, communication, professionalism, and critical thinking. Clinical/lab Fee $170
courses.prereqText: NURS 20263, NURS 20271, NURS 20363, and NURS 20043.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 20263, NURS 20271, NURS 20363, and NURS 20043. This course focuses on basic nursing skills with focus on safe performance of psychomotor skills, safety, communication, professionalism, and critical thinking in the clinical setting. Clinical/lab Fee $170 Liability Ins Fee $10
courses.prereqText: NURS 20263, NURS 20271, NURS 20363, and NURS 20043.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 20263, 20271, and 10303. This is a companion course with NURS 30182 Foundations of Nsg Care: Clinical intended to enhance learning about geriatric nursing care. This class will address the complex nursing care issues of older adults. The multifaceted concepts of aging, the physiologic and psychosocial changes and challenges associated with the process, and the appropriate nursing interventions will be discussed.
courses.prereqText: NURS 20263, 20271, and 10303. This is a companion course with NURS 30182 Foundations of Nsg Care: Clinical intended to enhance learning about geriatric nursing care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisite or concurrent: NURS 20263, 20271, 20363, 20043; ENGL 10803, 20803. This course introduces and explores the role of the nurse as a member of the interprofessional team within the local and global community. Students are introduced to global health care delivery systems and population health principles. The course includes an emphasis on innovative teaching strategies for diverse learners and emerging uses of technology within the healthcare system.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 10303, 20263, 20271, 30263 & 30182/30171, and 30241. This is a companion course with NURS 30582 Adults Health Alt. I: Clinical intended to continue to enhance learning about geriatric nursing care. This directed study will address the complex nursing care issues of older adults. The multifaceted concepts of aging, the physiologic and psychosocial changes and challenges associated with the process, and the appropriate nursing interventions will be discussed.
courses.prereqText: NURS 10303, 20263, 20271, 30263 & 30182/30171, and 30241. This is a companion course with NURS 30582 Adults Health Alt.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 20263, 20271, 20363, and NURS 20043. This course introduces basic nursing concepts to provide a foundation for nursing practice. Major concepts emphasized are health and wellness, health promotion, nursing process, critical thinking, communication, safety, and education. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Variable credit, 1-3 hours. Prerequisites: Faculty permission required; junior standing. Directed readings or projects in nursing requiring independent or small group study in consultation with a faculty. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: Faculty permission required; junior standing.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisite: NURS 20163 and permission of instructor. A one-semester hour course of supervised study for students who exhibit special needs during the junior or senior year in dosage calculation. Offers instruction to the student who needs continued guided learning and practice in the calculation of dosages and solutions. The student will concentrate on the performance of the necessary math skills for calculation, the importance of accuracy and application to specific kinds of nursing situations. This course is taught as a module during the first 6 weeks of the semester. Course completion can range up to 6 weeks depending on concurrent practicum course enrollment and expectations. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: NURS 20163 and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of faculty. Designed for students who undertake readings or projects in nursing in consultation with faculty. Letter graded and variable credit of 1-3 credit hours.
courses.prereqText: Permission of faculty.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30243, 30263, 30182, 30171 and 30163. This course prepares nursing honors students to envision and develop a creative, scholarly project supporting nursing practice, patient outcomes, or identifying new knowledge.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course is an introduction to dementia and those people living with dementia. Major concepts and theories of dementia and person-centered care will be introduced. Students will explore the current demographic trends in society, health and healthcare concerns of people living with dementia, issues of stigma, family relationships and social support, and quality of life. Offered as HCHS 30783 or NURS 30433 credit. Nursing majors will enroll in NURS 30433. All other students will enroll in HCHS 30783.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Students must be entering their Junior I semester of nursing school or have special permission from the instructor. This is an introduction to skills that foster resiliency in healthcare workers. We will explore major concepts of resiliency in healthcare, personal awareness, adaptation to stress, values and burnout, empathy, mindfulness meditation/mindfulness in daily living, self-compassion practices, and other strategies to deal with difficult emotions.
courses.prereqText: Students must be entering their Junior I semester of nursing school or have special permission from the instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Open to NURS majors who have successfully completed NURS 20043, NURS 20363, NURS 20271 and NURS 20263 and with the permission by an instructor. This course provides the student an introduction to women's health nursing in our community and in various geographical locations and various care settings.
courses.prereqText: Open to NURS majors who have successfully completed NURS 20043, NURS 20363, NURS 20271 and NURS 20263 and with the permission by an instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Open to all majors. Prerequisite: Junior status or permission of instructor. An overview of women's health issues using various social frameworks for analysis. Emphases include prevention, self-care, and social parameters of issues related to reproduction, aging, stress, and roles.
courses.prereqText: Junior status or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Permission of the instructor and Senior 1 or Senior 2 standing. This course focuses on labor support and how to provide labor support to a woman during childbirth. The course provides a deeper understanding of birth experiences and how the nurse can impact maternal outcomes. The course also reviews the physiology of labor and birth within the context of viewing various roles of providers in the interdisciplinary healthcare team. The role of nursing in promoting, supporting, advocating, and implementing nonpharmacological labor support will be emphasized.
courses.prereqText: Permission of the instructor and Senior 1 or Senior 2 standing.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. This course applies the nursing process to meet the health promotion, restoration, and chronicity needs of clients and families experiencing alteration of selected body systems. Emphasizes the use of critical thinking, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based practice in planning care for diverse adults across the lifespan. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. This practicum applies the nursing process to meet the health promotion, restoration, and chronicity needs of patients experiencing health alterations. Students utilize critical thinking, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based practice in implementing patient/family-centered professional care. Clinical/lab Fee $170 Liability Ins Fee $10

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582 or permission of instructor. This course provides the student an introduction to oncology nursing with clinical opportunities in various oncology settings. It will serve as the first course for students interested in an oncology clinical focus.
courses.prereqText: NURS 30563, 30582 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582 and 30583. The student will have the opportunity to provide care in an inpatient oncology setting that requires the application of principles and knowledge necessary for interdisciplinary care of cancer patients along the cancer continuum.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, NURS 30182, NURS 10171, NURS 30163, NURS 30243, or permission of the faculty. In this course, students examine different nursing roles and functions in the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative settings. Students implement the nursing process in the perioperative setting, including identification and intervention for common patient safety issues. Students utilize critical thinking, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based practice, and uphold professional, ethical, and legal standards while implementing patient/family-centered professional care.
courses.prereqText: NURS 30263, NURS 30182, NURS 10171, NURS 30163, NURS 30243, or permission of the faculty.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. This course examines the research process and the theory and technique related to development of evidence-based nursing practice. The student will learn to critique nursing research and identify examples of evidence based change in the practice setting.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. Explores concepts and principles of individual, family, group and community systems experiencing psychopathology. Introduces behavioral health alterations and human responses evoked by those alterations. Emphasizes nursing strategies and actions to promote behavioral health. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. This course builds on previously learned concepts and nursing skills, introduces selected additional nursing skills and reinforces current level-specific concepts in simulation-based learning experiences. More complex clinical reasoning concepts and strategies are incorporated into learning experiences. Clinical/lab Fee $170

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. Explores concepts and principles of individual, family, group and community systems experiencing psychopathology. Introduces behavioral health alterations and human responses evoked by those alterations. Emphasizes nursing strategies and actions to promote behavioral health. Fees apply per Nursing policy.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30263, 30182, 30171, 30163, 30243. Explores concepts and principles of individual, family, group and community systems experiencing psychopathology. Introduces behavioral health alterations and human responses evoked by those alterations. Emphasizes nursing strategies and actions to promote behavioral health.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course represents credit earned through a semester study abroad experience with an institution or program with which Texas Christian University has an official agreement to accept credit. The site and specific content will be identified on the official transcript. Courses appearing on a student's official transcript have been included in the student's grade point average.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 20224. Emphasizes application of nursing concepts and encourages development of learning strategies and self-improvement techniques to foster success in the undergraduate nursing program. This course is offered to selected students in all clinical levels based on individualized assessments. Department permit required.
courses.prereqText: NURS 20224.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: This course will reinforce and complement prior knowledge gained in the nursing curriculum. Students will utilize clinical judgement to review previously learned nursing concepts. Completion of the course will assist students to further prepare for National Council Licensure Examination in Nursing (NCLEX). Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30633, 30341, and 30342. This course applies the concepts of theory, research, and evidence-based practice learning in NURS 30633 and NURS 30342 to support the design, implementation, and successful completion of a scholarly project.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30633, 30341, 30342 and 40011. This course applies the concepts of theory, research, and evidence-based practice learning in NURS 40011 to support implementation, and successful completion of a scholarly project. A scholarly project is required involving an area of nursing for in-depth investigations. Both internal and external dissemination via poster, podium, and potential manuscript will be emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671. This course focuses on nursing care related to maternal health within the context of the family. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health during pregnancy, labor, and immediately postpartum will be emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30633. This course applies the nursing process to meet the health promotion, restoration, and chronicity needs of clients and families experiencing complex alterations of selected or multiple body systems. Emphasizes the use of critical thinking, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based practice in planning care of diverse adults across the lifespan. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40663, NURS 40682. This course provides the student an in-depth introduction to pediatric oncology nursing. Observational opportunities in various oncology settings will be provided. Legal, political, socio-cultural, ethical, and research implications for pediatric nursing practice will also be considered. This class builds upon previous knowledge mastered in adult medical-surgical nursing, pediatric nursing, child development, pharmacology, teaching strategies and the sciences.
courses.prereqText: NURS 40663, NURS 40682.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30633. This practicum applies the nursing process to meet the health promotion, restoration, and chronicity needs of patients experiencing complex health alterations of multiple body systems. Students operationalize critical thinking, interprofessional collaboration, and evidence-based practice in implementing patient/family-centered professional care. Clinical/lab Fee $170 Liability Ins Fee $10

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Only nursing students in the senior II status may take this course. This course is designed to be a two hour lecture once a week with a preceptor led clinical observation component (comprised of 12 hours). This is an elective for senior II students. In the class meetings we examine the most common health conditions of neonates in the neonatal intensive care unit. The students will learn the principles and knowledge of care of a neonate. Students will have the opportunity to observe care in the neonatal intensive care setting that will reinforce the application of principles and knowledge necessary for interdisciplinary care of neonates and their families.
courses.prereqText: Only nursing students in the senior II status may take this course.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, and 30671. This clinical explores pediatric nursing with a focus on understanding the physical and developmental needs of the pediatric patient within the context of the family. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health will be emphasized. Fees apply per Nursing policy.
courses.prereqText: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, and 30671. This clinical explores pediatric nursing with a focus on understanding the physical and developmental needs of the pediatric patient within the context of the family.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, and 30671. This course focuses on nursing care related to children, ages 0-18, within the context of the family. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health during all stages of child development will be emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30633. This course focuses on nursing care related to maternal child health within the context of the family. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health will be emphasized. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30663. This course builds on previously learned concepts and nursing skills, introduces selected additional nursing skills and reinforces current level-specific concepts in simulation-based learning experiences. More complex clinical reasoning concepts and strategies are incorporated into learning experiences. Fees apply per nursing policy.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30633. This course builds on previously learned concepts and nursing skills, introduces selected additional nursing skills and reinforces current level-specific concepts in simulation-based learning experiences. More complex clinical reasoning concepts and strategies are incorporated into learning experiences. Clinical/lab Fee $170

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, and 30671. This clinical explores the provision of nursing care related to maternal health. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health will be emphasized. Fees apply per Nursing policy.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 30563, 30582, 30663, 30681, 30671, 30633. Provision of nursing care related to maternal child health within the context of the family. The role of nursing in promoting, maintaining and restoring health will be emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40563, 40582, 40663, 40682, and 40672. Theories and principles of leadership and management provide the foundation for managing health care systems. Analyzes management roles and leadership competencies within various health care settings. Explores concepts that promote safety and a healthy workplace in health care organizations. Standardized Exam Fee $205

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40563, 40582, 40663, 40682, and 40672. Provides an intensive opportunity for the student to integrate prior knowledge in clinical practice. Students are required to demonstrate competence in assessment, planning, prioritizing, and evaluation in the care of multiple clients.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40563, 40582, 40663, 40682, and 40672. Explores the concept of community/population as client. Examines population-focused methods of assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation. Emphasizes the public health nurse's role in addressing health care needs of populations using systems theory, epidemiology, levels of prevention, and the national agenda for population health.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40563, 40582, 40663, 40682, and 40672. This course builds on previously learned concepts and nursing skills, introduces selected additional nursing skills and reinforces current level specific concepts in simulation-based learning experiences. More complex clinical reasoning concepts and strategies are introduced and incorporated into simulation-based learning experiences. Clinical/lab Fee $170

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: NURS 40563, 40582, 40663, 40682, and 40672. Students assume professional roles that require application of leadership principles and team building for assessment, implementation, and evaluation for population-focused interventions. Clinical/lab Fee $170 Liability Ins Fee $10

courses.subject: NURS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Program. The course will facilitate transition to the role of the DNP prepared advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) through exploration of leadership, profession, and practice prospectives within the metaparadigm of nursing. Emphasis is placed on exploring roles within advance practice, theories of change,collaboration, advocacy, autonomy, titling, certification, and licensure issues.
courses.prereqText: Admission to Graduate Program.

(This course is only offered as P/NC)

courses.description: This course provides students with the knowledge of strength and conditioning principles to improve muscular strength, endurance, and overall fitness. Designed for students with varying levels of experience, it promotes safe and effective exercise practices and provides the knowledge necessary to design personalized strength training programs for lifelong fitness. Emphasizing safety, effective resistance training techniques, and exercise science fundamentals, students will engage in resistance training using a combination of free weights, machines, resistance bands, and bodyweight exercises. (This course is only offered as P/NC)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Takes place both indoors and outdoors, focusing on group leadership and hard skills needed for climbing, backpacking and paddling trips. Additionally, to meet the student learning outcomes of this course, all students are required to attend a minimum of two overnight trips as scheduled through TCU Outdoor Program during the semester of which the course is taken. A course fee is charged to cover gear, transportation, all costs associated with required overnight trips, and equipment. Certifications available such as Leave No Trace & Wilderness Education Association: Outdoor Leader Certificate. Course fee of $245.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: This course covers the basics of safe and responsible rock climbing. Topics include equipment, knots, belaying, rappelling, and a range of climbing techniques.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Equipment selection, safety, riding techniques and training programs associated with biking. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Techniques, principles and practice in jogging. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Aerobic conditioning rhythmic workouts, with emphasis on fitness and cardiovascular conditioning while performing directed and individual routines. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Emphasis on stroke development and water safety designed for the non-swimmer. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Individual stroke development, conditioning and water safety. American Red Cross standards maintained with emphasis on improving swimming skills. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Knowledge and skill development for life guarding in accordance with American Red Cross standards. Lifesaving and CPR test and certification for those meeting required standards. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Lifesaving skills as well as a training program for students who want to teach swimming. Prerequisite: Current Red Cross Advance Life-saving Certificate and strong execution of swimming skills. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: Current Red Cross Advance Life-saving Certificate and strong execution of swimming skills.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Prerequisite: Good health and basic swimming skills. This class consists of knowledge development in the classroom, and confined water skills in the pool with the goal of being able to safely plan and execute repetitive scuba dives to the depth limit appropriate for beginning divers. PADI Certification available. (This course is only offered as P/NC).
courses.prereqText: Good health and basic swimming skills.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: This course covers the basics of safe and responsible sailing. Topics include tacking, jibing, upwind and downwind sailing, docking, mooring, crewing, basic knot tying, and rigging and derigging of a sailboat. Students will also learn teamwork, safety procedures, and the management of emergency situations on the water. Class will meet once a week for the entire semester at a sailing facility at a local lake.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Fundamental skills, rules and offensive tactics of water polo. Conditioning and game situations. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Physical conditioning through aquatic activities. Concepts of swim conditioning and endurance as well as stroke improvement. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Skill, techniques of play and competitive strategies of badminton. Singles and doubles play. (This course is only offered as P/NC.).

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Fundamental skills, rules, basic shots, game strategies, equipment and safety of racquetball. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Continuation of racquetball. Prerequisite: PEAC 10721 or equivalent experience. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: PEAC 10721 or equivalent experience.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Fundamental skills, basic strokes, rules, strategies and game play of tennis. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Review of basic tennis skills as well as development advanced strokes, strategies and game play in both singles and doubles. Prerequisite: PEAC 10741 or equivalent experience. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: PEAC 10741 or equivalent experience.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Refinement of advanced techniques and strategies of tennis. Prerequisite: PEAC 10751 or equivalent experience. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)
courses.prereqText: PEAC 10751 or equivalent experience.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Fundamental skills of swing, stance, and basic club use, putting and practice in course play. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Emphasis will be on skill and stroke improvement with individual assistance in game play. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: In this course, students will develop baslc skills for playing pickleball. Instruction will focus on overhead and underhand groundstrokes, volleys, and serves. Students will also learn court markings, rules, scoring, etiquette, and fundamental strategies used in both singles and double play. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Basic skills rules and strategies of bowling. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Transfer work.

courses.subject: PEAC
courses.description: Fundamental knowledge and the development of skills associated with selected team sports. (This course is only offered as P/NC.)

courses.description: General Transfer Credit with TCUCC-HUM credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: (Subtitle and content may vary in different sections.) This course focuses on the basic human concerns treated under the classical core elements of philosophical inquiry, and prepares students for more detailed treatments of these areas in courses at the 30000 level. Major topics include ethics, epistemology, metaphysics and the philosophies of religion, science, art and mind, and introductory logic. Note: Credit not awarded for both PHIL 10003 and PHIL 10103.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to philosophy focused on the metaphysical, ethical, and value questions, What (who) are we? What should we do? and What makes life meaningful? Answers from various figures in Western thought will be explored, compared, and evaluated, providing a basis for further study of these in upper level courses. Note: Credit not awarded for both PHIL 10003 and PHIL 10103.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 10103. This course is a continuation of PHIL 10103 (Mind, Meaning, and Morality I) and provides an exploration of various conceptions of freedom, determinism, and objectivity, particularly as they emerge out of ancient and modern explanations of human agency and purpose into 19th and 20th Century attitudes towards the self, moral responsibility, socio-political organization, scientific knowledge, and the natural world.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 10103.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Topics may vary each time course is offered.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Topics may vary each time it is offered.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: How to detect, analyze, and critically evaluate reasoning in ordinary language and its technical counterparts found in business, economics, etc. The course is designed to enhance skills for handling arguments in a variety of texts. Understanding the arguments and theories encountered in one's situations is stressed, along with how one can improve one's own expression of arguments and theories, especially in writing. Topics include techniques of reconstruction and evaluation in a process of self-editing, detection of fallacies, and distinguishing correct from incorrect reasoning.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: What is the purpose of your education? How does it relate to creating a flourishing life, one filled with deep satisfaction, well-being, resilience, and accomplishment? What can we learn from the humanities and sciences about the varieties of human flourishing and its key ingredients, and how can you develop your own personal vision of that life? What skills and knowledge would you need to realize that vision? This course aims to assist you in finding your own answers to these questions so as to lay the foundation for flourishing during your undergraduate years, while also preparing you for a life of flourishing in personal, civic, and professional contexts. We will explore perspectives from both the humanities and sciences in ways that are directly relevant to university life, and we will engage in practices, such as mindfulness and meditation, which will help you develop the intellectual and emotional dispositions¿resilience, compassion, gratitude, and others¿that research shows are central to human flourishing.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Students will examine and critically evaluate important philosophical ideas as they are expressed in film. Students will watch films and read accompanying philosophical texts that deal with perennial philosophical questions.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: In this course, students will be introduced to the philosophical investigation of the socially and politically fraught ways people can use language. Topics may include bad words, e.g. swears, slurs, dogwhistles, and dehumanizing terms, as well as bad discourse, e.g. subordinating expression, epistemic injustice, epistemic isolation, and gaslighting. Topics may also include some of the ways that language can be used to counteract such bad uses, through e.g. linguistic reclamation and counter-expression. Through the exploration of these topics, students will gain familiarity with several central topics in the philosophy of language, social epistemology, and feminist philosophy, and the philosophy of race. Previous familiarity with these areas will not be presupposed.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: An examination of contemporary moral issues. Typical topics include abortion, euthanasia, discrimination, preferential hiring, the enforcement of community standards, the morality of war, punishment, the rights of distant peoples and future generations, and environmental ethics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: In this class we will explore some of the classic metaphysical and moral problems that surround the topic of death. Some of the questions the class may discuss include: What is death? Do we have a soul? Is death a harm? Is life a benefit? Is euthanasia morally permissible? Is abortion morally permissible? Is it morally permissible to kill animals so that we may eat them? May we sacrifice the lives of some in order to save the lives of others?

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: An examination of some of the ethical issues that arise in the field of medicine. Topics typically include the moral status of abortion, euthanasia, stem cell research, informed consent, cloning, and the just distribution of scarce medical resources.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: This course surveys several contemporary approaches for understanding our moral obligation to the environment, including intuitionism, utilitarianism, deontology and feminism. By applying these approaches to concrete environmental issues, the course illustrates how efforts to preserve the environment raise special difficulties for traditional moral categories, such as intrinsic and instrumental value. The course also explores the peculiarly aesthetic dimension of environmental ethics, including claims about the value of natural beauty and unspoiled wilderness.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: This course explores several conceptions of mind, consciousness, and self within both the Western and Eastern traditions. These conceptions are similar in their rejection of the view that cognition and consciousness reside exclusively (or in any way) within a thinking substance or ego, or are somehow uniquely enskulled or brainbound. Topics we will consider include attention and awareness, extended cognition and mind, embodiment, situatedness, self-consciousness, interpersonal neurobiology, animal minds, neurotechnology, personal identity, boundaries of self, not-self or selflessness, the evolutionary self, and the ecological self.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: An introduction to some basic issues in the philosophy of music. What is the difference between music and noise? What is a work of music? Are works of different traditions fundamentally different kinds of entities? What is a musical performance, and what is it for a performance to be accurate or authentic? What are the relevant social, cultural, economic, and ethical considerations when playing or otherwise engaging with certain kinds of music? Readings will be a mix of classic and contemporary papers by leading philosophers of music.

courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: An introduction to the scope and limits of modern logic. The nature of logical systems and the various areas of logic are discussed. Alternative proof- procedures in propositional logic and predicate logic are presented.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30133. A continuation of 30133, with an emphasis on predicate logic, nonstandard logic, and metalogic.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 30133.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A systematic examination of the central issues in metaphysics. Topics include the nature of possibility and necessity, persistence through time and change, material constitution and composition, and criteria of ontological commitment. A portion of the course will also focus on methodological issues pertaining to the nature of metaphysical questions and claims. Readings will be a mix of classic and contemporary papers by leading metaphysicians.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A systematic treatment of basic issues in moral theory, critically examining such issues as the possibility of providing rational foundations for moral belief, and the nature of moral judgments and moral reasoning, focusing on the work of major historical and contemporary figures.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A systematic treatment of basic issues in moral theory, critically examining such issues as the possibility of providing rational foundations for moral belief, and the nature of moral judgments and moral reasoning, focusing on the work of major historical and contemporary figures.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: RELI 30633 Prerequisite: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course, or any religion course. Philosophy of Religion today is centrally concerned with issues relating to the rationality and justification of religious convictions. There is also an interest in the coherence of religious concepts. In this course various philosophical models for understanding and evaluating religious convictions and practices are examined and applied.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course, or any religion course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: A survey of major intellectual traditions of Asia, including Indian, Chinese, and Japanese philosophies. Topics include social and political philosophy, concepts of the individual and Nature, and the nature of reality and knowledge.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: This course introduces students to the myriad ways in which sexual desire and sexual activity are structured by social relations and to the ways that sexuality, sexual practices, and sexual identities vary in time and space. We will also consider how those social relations and sexual identities influence ethical judgment regarding various sexual practices and attitudes. Social science and philosophical theories of sexuality will be considered and cross-cultural and historical accounts of sexual practices will be reviewed. (Offered as PHIL 30343 or SOCI 30773 credit)

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. An introduction to the classical systems and central issues in political philosophy. The approach is largely historical, and selected major thinkers of most recent four centuries form the focus of the course.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. This course offers students an opportunity to reflect on such topics as the search for meaning, being, freedom, the self, embodiment, authenticity, love, and ethics as they are dealt with in texts by major writers in the 19th and 20th century movement known as existentialism.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course or an upper-division Psychology or Neuroscience course. This course will focus on Philosophical issues foundational to Psychology. Specifically, it will involve an interdisciplinary exploration of the nature, mechanisms, and architecture of cognition. Topics include: models of psychological explanation, the nature of commonsense psychology and the relationship between rationality and mental causation, functionalist approaches to cognition, computational vs. neural network models of mind, and the relationships between perception, action, and cognition.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course or an upper-division Psychology or Neuroscience course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A survey of past and present accounts of human mentality. Beginning with the classical ideas of the soul the course concentrates on the major theories of mind advanced by Western philosophers in the last four centuries.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course . An examination of the basic issues in Legal Theory. Topics typically include the nature of legal reasoning, the relationship between law and morality, and classical theories of law.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course .

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A systematic examination of the central issues in epistemology (e.g., the nature and structure of knowledge, and external-world skepticism), focusing on a series of papers by leading philosophers in epistemology.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. A systematic examination of the central issues in the philosophy of science (e.g., theory confirmation in science, and scientific explanation), focusing on a series of papers by leading philosophers in the philosophy of science (for instance, Carl Hempel and Thomas Kuhn).
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course. While we praise, blame, and punish people for their actions, we don't hold everyone responsible for everything they do. Moral responsibility looks to be intimately tied to a person's free will. We will discuss a range of views on what's required for agents to be free, and therefore morally responsible for their actions.
courses.prereqText: any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: None, but PHIL 10003, 10103, or 20343 encouraged. This course will explore various Western and non-Western conceptions of mind, consciousness, and self with particular attention to the interconnectedness of mind, body, and environment. An expanded understanding of our interconnectedness can enhance our awareness of climate change so that we can make positive changes in our lifestyles an assume important leadership roles for the betterment of humanity and the environment. Topics include attention and awareness, mindfulness, embodiment, situatedness, neuroscience, phenomenology, ecology, ecocentrism, inequity, and climate.
courses.prereqText: None, but PHIL 10003, 10103, or 20343 encouraged.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course or an upper-division Psychology or Neuroscience course. The aim of this course is to focus on philosophical principles that are implicitly assumed in "standard" Cognitive Science.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level or 20000-level PHIL course or an upper-division Psychology or Neuroscience course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 20103 or PHIL 30133 (or permission of instructor). Advanced topics in logic. Course content to vary by semester and will include areas such as formal languages, mathematical logic, deontic logic, modal systems, and philosophy of language.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 20103 or PHIL 30133 (or permission of instructor).

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 30000 level PHIL course. An examination of one or more advanced issues in metaphysics. Examples of possible topics include ontology, cosmology, modality, mereology, existence, persistence, causation, laws of nature, natural kinds, free will, personal identity, and the nature of mind.
courses.prereqText: Any 30000 level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 30000 level PHIL course. A survey of the major figures in Western thought between the sixth century BCE and fifth century CE. Among those included are the Presocratics, Plato, Aristotle, and the Hellenistic philosophers. This course also applies to the minor in Classical Studies minor.
courses.prereqText: Any 30000 level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 30000-level PHIL course. A survey of the major figures in Western thought from 1500 to 1800. Among those included are Descartes, Spinoza, Leibniz, Locke, Berkeley, Hume and Kant.
courses.prereqText: Any 30000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHIL 40223. The philosophical tradition after Kant developed in different ways in Continental Europe from the ways it did in English speaking countries. This course examines those developments, especially in Germany and France. Such thinkers as Hegel and the German Idealists, Kierkegaard and Nietzsche, Husserl and Heidegger, Sartre and Merleau-Ponty, Gadamer, Ricoeur and Derrida are discussed.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 40223.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHIL 40223. A historical study of either the analytic or pragmatic tradition. Such figures as Carnap, Neurath, Schlick, Moore, Russell, and Ayer; or Royce, Peirce, Mead, James, Dewey, and Quine; or a combination of philosophers are studied.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 40223.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 30000-level PHIL course and permission of the instructor. A philosophical study of one or more philosophers or philosophical movements of the ancient, medieval, or modern periods. Course content will vary by semester. Course may be repeated for credit.
courses.prereqText: Any 30000-level PHIL course and permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Any 10000-level and any 30000-level Philosophy course. This course is a survey of the philosophy of Socrates and the development of his ideas in Plato and Aristotle. Students will read various Socratic dialogues and a few of Plato's middle dialogues that show significant Socratic influence. The course will conclude with a brief survey of Aristotle's conception of language, thought, reality, and virtue.
courses.prereqText: Any 10000-level and any 30000-level Philosophy course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 30000-level PHIL course and permission of the instructor. An historical study of one or more philosophical movements in the 20th Century to the present. Topics vary and may include analytic philosophy, or Buddhist modernism. May be repeated once for a total of 6 hours credit as course topic changes.
courses.prereqText: Any 30000-level PHIL course and permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30303. A close examination of advanced issues in value theory. Topics may include the views of major historical figures such as Bentham, Hume, Kant, Locke, and Sidgwick, the moral realism-antirealism, debate, topics in moral psychology, and moral epistemology.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 30303.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30423 or 30433. An examination of advanced issues in philosophy of science, for example, issues concerning theory confirmation and issues concerning explanation.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHIL 30303 or 30353 or 30413. Philosophy of Law and Economics asks students to consider economics as a justification for legal decision-making. Different perspectives regarding the nature of law are juxtaposed against different perspectives regarding the nature of economics. Students develop their own synthesis by examining landmark legal cases from various perspectives.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30303 or 30353 or 30413. A rigorous examination of specific issues in legal theory and jurisprudence. Topics may include the nature of law, legal adjudication, law and economics, theories of punishment, and legal responsibility and obligation.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHIL 30303 or 30353 or 30413. A philosophical analysis of some selected topics that are central to political philosophy. Topics may include analyses of the nature of human rights, political authority, the moral duty to obey the law, freedom, or justice.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisites: Two prior PHIL courses (any level), or permission of instructor. Moral psychology is precisely what it sounds like - the intersection of the study of morality (typically the domain of philosophy) and the study of our mental processes (typically the domain of psychology). It is an area in which we ask fundamental questions about the moral nature of human beings, and purse the answers to these questions via a constant exchange between philosophical theory and empirical data.
courses.prereqText: Two prior PHIL courses (any level), or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Any 30000-level PHIL course. Philosophical theories are presented regarding the nature of art and aesthetic experience. The concepts of representation, expression, formalism, the work of art, intention, meaning, truth, and criticism are discussed along with how they contribute to answering the question, "What is art?"
courses.prereqText: Any 30000-level PHIL course.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30383 or PHIL 30393. Critical analysis of contemporary theories of human nature advanced by philosophers, psychologists, biologists, cognitive scientists and others. The thinkers under consideration will vary but examples would include E. O. Wilson, B. F. Skinner, Sigmund Freud, John Searle and Daniel Dennett.
courses.prereqText: PHIL 30383 or PHIL 30393.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHIL 30423 or 30433. An examination of advanced issues in epistemology, for example, issues concerning rational degrees of belief, issues concerning the intersection of epistemology, philosophy of language, and philosophy of mind, and issues concerning epistemological methodology.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor.

courses.description: Transfer work with TCUCC-NSC credit.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Three hours lecture and one 2-hours laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. Part one of a two-semester survey of general physics recommended for students in the life sciences and premedical program. It is strongly recommended that students have taken high school algebra and trigonometry. Topics covered include mechanics of solids and fluids, thermodynamics, sound and wave motion. Emphasis will be given to the application of these concepts to problems in the life and health sciences. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 20474, 20475.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 10154 or approval of instructor. Three hours lecture and one 2-hour laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. Part two of a two-semester survey of general physics recommended for students in the life sciences and premedical program. Topics covered include electricity and magnetism, optics, atomic and nuclear physics. Emphasis will be given to the application of these concepts to problems in the life and health science. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 20484, 20485.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 10154 or approval of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: This course will examine the development of human understanding of the critical events in the origin and evolution of the Universe. Two hours of lectures and one two-hour lab per week.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Two hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week. Structure and origin of the solar system. Laboratory assignments may be scheduled in the evening.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Two hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week. The course will explore naked-eye astronomy, including motion of the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. Course will investigate the development of astronomy, calendars, writing and numeration among early civilizations, and how it supported or established their societies.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot, or permission from the instructor. This course will be a survey of first-semester physics, including Newtonian mechanics, fluid mechanics, and thermodynamics with applications to aeronautical topics, including aerodynamic theory, airfoils, wings, and aircraft performance & design. Three hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week.
courses.prereqText: Admission to the B.S. in Professional Aviation's Professional Pilot, or permission from the instructor.

courses.description: General Transfer Credit

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Two hours lecture and one 2-hour laboratory per week. The course will explore the fundamental laws and natural processes related to energy production, transport, storage, and uses.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Declared major or minor in Physics or Astronomy. A first year seminar for majors. Introduction of 'modern' physics and astrophysics ideas. Experimental, theoretical, observational, and computational research methods. Areas of application of physics to pure and applied research. Introduction to career opportunities in academic, industrial, and other settings. Physics educational experiences at TCU outside of the academic classroom.
courses.prereqText: Declared major or minor in Physics or Astronomy. A first year seminar for majors.

courses.description: Structure and origin of the solar system. Students may receive credit for PHYS 20013 or 20073, but not both.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Stars, galaxies, stellar evolution, and cosmology. Students may receive credit for PHYS 20023 or 20083, but not both.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Fundamental statistical analysis techniques, plotting, and data management. Introduction to Python programming, coding standards, documentation, and version control. Database query skills, introduction to instrument control systems.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: MATH 10524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. The first of a two-semester survey recommended for students majoring in the physical sciences or engineering. Newton's laws of motion, the conservation of momentum, angular momentum, and energy; and the theory of gravitation. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 10154, 20475.
courses.prereqText: MATH 10524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: MATH 10524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor. Four hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. The first of a three-semester sequence for students in Department of Physics & Astronomy majors, including Newton's laws of motion, the conservation of momentum, angular momentum, and energy; and the theory of gravitation. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 10154, 20474.
courses.prereqText: MATH 10524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20473 and MATH 20524, which is normally taken concurrently or permission of instructor. The second of a three-semester sequence recommended for students of physical sciences. Electric charge, current and field; magnetism, time varying electromagnetic fields; geometrical optics; interference and diffraction. No more than four semester hours of credit (three semester hours for lecture and one semester hour for lab) will be granted for any combination of PHYS 10161, 10163, 10164, 20481, 20483, and 20484.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20473 and MATH 20524, which is normally taken concurrently or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20474, MATH 20524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. The second of a two-semester sequence recommended for students of physical sciences or engineering. Electric charge, current and field; magnetism, time varying electromagnetic fields; physical and geometric optics. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 10164. 20485.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20474, MATH 20524, which may be taken concurrently, or permission of instructor.

Four hours of lectures and one 2-hour laboratory per week selected to reinforce the concepts discussed in lecture. The second of a three-semester sequence for students majoring in Department of Physics & Astronomy majors, including electric charge, current and field; magnetism, time varying electromagnetic fields; physical and geometric optics. Credit will not be granted for this course and any of the following: PHYS 10164, 20484.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Admission to Honors Program in Physics and junior standing in Physics. The first of two courses required for Honors in Physics in which the candidate will carry out a program of research under the direction of a faculty member. The results of this research must be satisfactorily communicated to the department in an oral presentation and/or a written report.
courses.prereqText: Admission to Honors Program in Physics and junior standing in Physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: CHEM 10013 or 10113. Introduction to the physical, chemical, mechanical, electrical, and optical properties of metals, semiconductors, ceramics, and polymers. Emphasis on the relationship between these properties and how performance is influenced by microstructure and processing. Atomic bonding. Crystal structure. Phase equilibria. Deformation and fracture. Composite materials. Electronic, magnetic, dielectric and optical properties. Laboratory methods for characterizing materials emphasized. (Crosslisted as ENGR/PHYS 30014.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 10263 and 10273, 10154 or 20474 or 20475 or permission of instructor. Observed properties and evolution of stars, exoplanets, clusters, and galaxies, including kinematics, chemistry, and spectral energy distributions. Qualitative and quantitative discussion of the Milky way and various types of galaxies (ellipticals, spirals, dwarf, starburst), including groups and clusters of galaxies, active galaxies, and galaxy evolution.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 10263 and 10273, 10154 or 20474 or 20475 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 10263 and 10273. Two hours of lectures and two hours of lab per week. Topics covered include telescopes, astronomical measurement techniques, modern detectors and instrumentation, the effect of the Earth's atmosphere on light. Selected experiments in telescope properties and resolution, photometry, spectroscopy, geometrical and physical optics, atomic physics, and studies of astronomical survey data.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: GEOL 10113, or any one of PHYS 10164/10263/10273, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lectures per week. This course will launch you into space with past and present spacecraft missions and bring you back to Earth with meteorite research. Throughout the semester, this course will examine the geology and geologic processes occurring on and within planetary bodies throughout the Solar System. This course is intended for science and non-science majors. (Crosslisted as GEOL/PHYS 30163.)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 10113, or any one of PHYS 10164/10263/10273, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484 or 20485, PHYS 20323 and MATH 20524 and permission of instructor. Survey of mathematical and computational methods used in the junior and senior level physics courses. Students will develop analytic problem-solving skills and numerical problem-solving skills using Python programming.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20484 or 20485, PHYS 20323 and MATH 20524 and permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: pre-calculus, PHYS 10164 or PHYS 20484 or 20485 or permission of instructor. Three hours of lecture and one two-hour lab per week. This course will explore the fundamental lows and natural processes related to the mechanics, biophysics, and biochemistry of the human body. It is designed for pre-health, kinesiology, biology nursing and physics students who want to understand the foundations and biophysical principles that govern human life. The course will focus on the science of physiological processes from simple mechanical motion, breathing, blood flow and oxygen exchange to vision, neuronal processes and the basics of genetics and proteomics. The biophysical elements of human function and human development in the context of environmental influences and live adaptation will be discussed. The evolution of approaches to understanding physiological functions as it has been governed by modern scientific developments will be briefly discusses. The course will also provide a simple understanding of recent technologies that have been applied to the study of physiological processes like muscle contraction, blood transport, cell function, neuronal processing, and DNA replication.
courses.prereqText: pre-calculus, PHYS 10164 or PHYS 20484 or 20485 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHYS 30493, which may be taken concurrently. The course introduces students to modern experimental research techniques through a variety of experiments that might include spectroscopy, imaging, ultrasound, digital electronics, circuits, and magnetic resonance. One hour of lecture and four hours of laboratory per week.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30493, which may be taken concurrently.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484, or 20485, or 10164; and MATH 20524. Relativity, introduction to quantum mechanics, atomic structure, nuclear physics, and the standard model.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor. Particle motion in one and three dimensions including oscillatory motion and motion under a central force. Dynamics of many particle systems. Lagrange's and Hamilton's equations.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20323,30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor. This course explores the bulk behavior of large collections of particles, including how systems of particles behave when they have different properties, when they interact with different environments, and when they undergo different processes. This course connects concepts associated with classical quantum, and statistical mechanics.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20323,30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484 or 20485 or 10164. An introduction to image formation for molecular and medical applications. This course covers the fundamentals of optic, x-ray and MRI, image creation, detectors, basics of image processing, quantitative analysis and a variety of applications in biophysics and in medicine. Includes off-campus lab work. (Crosslisted as BIOL/PHYS 30843.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor. The Schrodinger equations, operators, stationary states; Quantum theory of angular momentum; the harmonic oscillator; the hydrogen atom; perturbation theory and the variational method.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30313, 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484 or 20485 and MATH 30524 or permission of instructor. Development of Maxwell's equations; electrostatics; potential; magnetostatics; electric and magnetic fields in matter; electromagnetic waves.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20484 or 20485 and MATH 30524 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: PHYS 40653 or permission of instructor. Electromagnetic radiation in free space and in materials; geometrical optics; interference and diffraction; Fourier optics; introduction to nonlinear optics.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 40653 or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20323, and 30313, and 30493, and MATH 30524 and all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor. Techniques for analyzing nonlinear and pattern-forming systems. Topics covered may include maps, bifurcations, strange attractors, fractals, linear stability methods, amplitude equations, defects, instabilities and traveling waves, Lyapunov spectra and correlation functions. Students will learn to build models of biological systems and to use analytical tools to develop intuition and make quantitative predictions about the system's behavior.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20323, and 30313, and 30493, and MATH 30524 and all with a C- or better, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524. Crystal structure, lattice dynamics,free electron theory, band theory, optical, electric and magnetic properties of solids.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524.

courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. Students enrolled will be expected to participate in, prepare, and lead discussions on selected topics in physics and astronomy as suggested by the current journal literature. (1-4 hours)
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of department chair. Three hours of lecture in an area of physics & astronomy of current interest.

courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30313, PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or graduate standing and PHYS 60323, or permission of instructor. Computational methods used in physics, systems of linear equations, eigenvalues problems, numerical solution of differential equations using Python.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30313, PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or graduate standing and PHYS 60323, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30313, PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or graduate standing and PHYS 60323, or permission of instructor. This course explores how stars emit light and how astronomers interpret observations of them, including the processes that affect the spectral energy distribution of the light as it travels from the cores of stars, through the atmosphere of stars, and through the intervening medium. This course includes topics on radiative transfer, stellar interiors, stellar atmospheres, and stellar evolution.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30313, PHYS 30493 and MATH 30524 all with a C- or better, or graduate standing and PHYS 60323, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 20484 or PHYS 20485 or PHYS 10164 and MATH 10524, or graduate standing, or permission of instructor. This course will introduce students to a variety of biophysics topics focusing on the application of physics principles to biological systems. Topics covered might include membrane transport, impulses in nerve cells, external electric and magnetic fields, imaging, ultrasound, electromagnetic radiation, radiation therapy, nuclear magnetic resonance, crystallography, spectroscopy and signal analysis.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 20484 or PHYS 20485 or PHYS 10164 and MATH 10524, or graduate standing, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: Permission of instructor. This course will introduce students to experimental techniques developed and used to investigate biological systems. It will discuss modern techniques used in the biomedical sciences, drug discovery and other biophysical and biochemical fields. The course includes lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on exercises in the TCU Biophysics Laboratory and on instrumentation at the Center for Commercialization of Fluorescence Technologies (CCFT) at the UNT Health Sciences Center campus. (Crosslisted as CHEM/PHYS 50763.)
courses.prereqText: Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: PHYS 30113, PHYS 30493 and permission of instructor or graduate standing. Three hours of lectures per week covering concepts including the early universe, dark matter, dark energy and a theoretical understanding of early galaxy formation and evolution.
courses.prereqText: PHYS 30113, PHYS 30493 and permission of instructor or graduate standing. Three hours of lectures per week covering concepts including the early universe, dark matter, dark energy and a theoretical understanding of early galaxy formation and evolution.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisite: GEOL 30213 or PHYS 30493, or permission of instructor. Three hours of lectures per week. An interdisciplinary course exploring the history and formation of the Solar System from the Big Bang through the formation and evolution of the planets. (Crosslisted as GEOL/PHYS 50813.)
courses.prereqText: GEOL 30213 or PHYS 30493, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.description: Prerequisites: Junior, Senior, or Graduate standing. This is a senior and graduate seminar for majors to prepare advanced undergraduates and graduate students for success within and beyond the TCU Physics and Astronomy program. This class will provide basic skills and knowledge essential for student academic and career success. Five-week topics will rotate on a two to three year cycle and include topics such as: Career Skills, Scientific & Public Communication, Intro to Scientific Programing, Publishing & Grants, Basic Research Statistics, Research Policy, and Ethics & Diversity. Course may be repeated for credit.
courses.prereqText: Junior, Senior, or Graduate standing. This is a senior and graduate seminar for majors to prepare advanced undergraduates and graduate students for success within and beyond the TCU Physics and Astronomy program.
